Andreas Christopheros, a property developer, was critically injured in a corrosive liquid attack outside his home in Truro, Cornwall. He now faces life-changing injuries including vision loss and facial scars. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, has been charged with perverting the course of justice, while her husband David Phillips has been charged with grievous bodily harm with intent. Christopheros, a popular event organizer, is a director of Chase 3000 and owns properties in Newquay.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has posted signs warning against defecating along the path, which has become an amusing attraction for some pilgrims. Despite the signs, residents complain about littering and lack of public facilities for pilgrims, who walk up to 500 miles to reach the Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela.

A fire engulfed a building formerly housing a strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon. The blaze, which started around 1pm, affected only the building and a few nearby power lines. The site was previously known as The Body Shop, and a local resident reported a previous fire at the location. An investigation into the cause of the blaze is ongoing.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent, was strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport on the 10th anniversary of 9/11. She won a $40,000 settlement after a lawsuit against the federal government, TSA, and airport authorities, alleging ethnic profiling. The settlement aims to prevent future incidents and improve airport policies.

A tailstrike and skid occurred during Asiana Airlines flight OZ162's landing at Hiroshima Airport, injuring 20 people. The Airbus A320, which had departed from Seoul, reportedly missed the runway and spun 180 degrees, causing a crash landing and emergency services to respond. The airport was closed, and emergency services were treating injured passengers.

Made In Chelsea star Mark-Francis Vandelli, a wealthy Londoner, has a watch collection worth several thousand pounds. He buys a new watch each year, aiming to have an impressive collection by middle age. Vandelli owns a Cartier Moonphase worth £32,000 and a Bulgari Chrono 42 he bought on holiday, showcasing his passion for expensive timepieces.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is auctioning over 200 antiques, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt and a longbow, in a £100,000 sale to downsize his home. His collection, spanning military history and classic literature, includes paintings, furniture, swords, and crystal chandeliers. Hardy, 89, is sad to part with his extensive collection but hopes the items find new owners joy and pleasure.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo of two women hugging on a train platform, criticizing it as a challenge to social norms. His post, intended to mock conservative attitudes, went viral, revealing he was actually warning against a safety violation. The image was later revealed to depict a man standing on a yellow safety line, prompting a mix of confusion and praise for Felippe's clever satire.

A 16-year-old English cricket fan's letter to Richie Benaud, a legendary Australian spin bowler, was recently shared. Benaud, in a detailed 1996 response, offered advice on left-handed leg spin bowling and emphasized the unique challenges for left-arm bowlers. The letter, now shared as a tribute to Benaud's passing, includes a full sheet of coaching notes.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts the future of travel will involve sharing virtual reality environments, allowing users to experience world locations from multiple viewpoints without physical travel. This includes plans for immersive videos and VR support on the newsfeed, facilitated by Facebook's acquisition of Oculus VR. Marriott hotels have also tested VR tours of their properties.

A bedridden girlfriend, diagnosed with bone cancer, had her birthday wish granted by her boyfriend. Despite her condition, they had professional photos taken in her hospital room, with friends helping her dress and pose. The couple, who met after the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake, exchanged rings and vows, making their special day meaningful despite the postponement of their official wedding.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, was charged with multiple DUI-related offenses after causing three separate crashes in Houston, killing a 6-year-old boy and a homeless man, and injuring a mother and her toddler. Boudreaux, with a history of DUIs, was arrested after the first crash and allegedly fell asleep at the wheel, leading to a fatal hit-and-run on a homeless man and another fatal collision.

Microsoft is launching a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time IT positions at its Redmond campus, partnering with Specialisterne. This initiative follows Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's apology for comments suggesting women should trust the system for raises, highlighting the company's focus on diversity.

Two deputies involved in the fatal arrest of Eric Harris in Tulsa were reassigned due to threats against them. They were criticized for their handling of Harris, who was shot by Reserve Deputy Robert Bates. The deputies are not charged but face scrutiny, with the sheriff suspending the drug unit and reviewing the shooting.

Katie Prager, 24, diagnosed with cystic fibrosis and Burkholderia cepacia infection, needs a lung transplant but her Kentucky Medicaid will not cover the $1 million out-of-state treatment at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Her husband Dalton, who received a transplant, is desperate to save her life, facing financial and healthcare barriers despite their long-term commitment.

New data from the Sleep Cycle app shows that South Africans wake up earliest on Mondays at 6:09 am, while Americans wake up earliest at 7 am on Tuesdays. The best sleep quality worldwide occurs on Wednesdays, with 58% of countries reporting the most restful sleep on this day, led by China. Americans sleep the latest on Fridays at 8:24 am, but report the best wake-up mood.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo wrote passionate love letters to Jose Bartoli during her marriage to Diego Rivera. These 25 unpublished letters, written between 1946 and 1949, are expected to fetch up to $120,000 at auction. The collection includes drafts of Jose's responses and other personal items, offering insight into Kahlo's complex relationships and creative process.

Red-haired trade union leader Len McCluskey, popular with activists, campaigns for Labour in Wales. However, his union's influence extends beyond popularity, wielding significant financial and organizational power within the Labour movement, which critics view as potentially disastrous for governance. McCluskey advocates for socialist policies reminiscent of the 1970s, including expanded public sector, higher taxes, and more state spending, despite his claims of being "more radical."

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz filmed 30 hours of animals drinking water using a GoPro camera placed in their troughs. The footage, culled down to four minutes, showcases unique drinking methods from various animals, from a rhino almost kissing the water to a lemur delicately licking it. Hershkowitz noted differences in drinking habits between carnivores and herbivores, and some animals initially skeptical of the camera's presence.

A poll shows that only 25% of voters think David Cameron is the hungriest to win the election, while 43% believe Ed Miliband is most eager. Despite Cameron's efforts to appear more engaged, he faces criticism for a perceived lack of campaign passion, with Miliband seen as more enthusiastic.

Zaur Dadaev, accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov, retracted his confession in court, claiming he was beaten and pressured into confessing. Initially confessing to the murder, Dadaev now says he was tortured and abducted. Five Chechen men are accused of the crime, with Dadaev being the only one to initially admit guilt.

A 4-month-old baby named Sonit Awal was pulled from under the rubble of the Nepal earthquake, surviving for 22 hours trapped. Rescuers found him alive and uninjured, providing hope amidst the devastation that killed over 5,000 people.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narconon, is attempting to have a 40-acre property near Camp David designated as historic to circumvent zoning laws and build a drug rehab center. The property, originally purchased by a Scientology-affiliated real estate company, was once used by President Herbert Hoover. However, opponents argue that Narconon's methods, including sauna therapy and vitamin Niacin, are dangerous and potentially convert patients to Scientology, despite the group's claims of secularism.

Kabul, once a bustling city during America's longest war, now faces a transformed landscape with a population five times larger. Formerly skilled English speakers are jobless and blacklisted, living in isolation and fear. The city's infrastructure, once filled with foreign workers and contractors, is now largely abandoned, reflecting the end of America's presence in Afghanistan.

Two US Navy SEALs died and one was critically injured during pool training at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia. The incident occurred while the SEALs were swimming in lap lanes without gear, and an investigation is ongoing.

NBC expects Premier League viewership in the USA to surpass Britain in one season, with US interest doubling in the past two years. NBC's live coverage in the US, led by star anchor Rebecca Lowe, has transported their entire production to England for the first time, showcasing matches including the Manchester derby and Liverpool-Newcastle. Lowe's presence has helped make the Premier League more accessible and appealing to American audiences.

London Mayor Boris Johnson attacked Ed Miliband on the Andrew Marr Show, calling him "deeply alarming" for considering a deal with the SNP, which he claimed would make Miliband unable to govern for the UK. Miliband, who beat his brother David to the Labour leadership, laughed off Johnson's attack, stating that Johnson would do more harm to the country than his brother did.

Prisoner Dustin Irons flashed a judge during a video court hearing, leading to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court. Despite being handcuffed, Irons exposed himself to the judge, who sentenced him to extra time behind bars. Irons, already serving time for assault and mischief, is described as a difficult inmate who needs constant supervision.

McLaren improved their pace significantly after the Malaysian Grand Prix, moving from a lackluster start to a competitive midfield position. Jenson Button, optimistic about the team's progress, believes they are now racing with Force Indias, Saubers, and Lotuses, though they still need more downforce and power unit improvements. Button sees progress despite cooler Shanghai weather potentially hindering tyre temperature benefits.

A $2 billion hospital in Western Australia found blood and bone fragments on medical instruments despite a previous fine and audit. The Fiona Stanley Hospital was stripped of its medical service provider Serco for failing to return sterilizing equipment, and Australian Medical Association WA president Michael Gannon expressed concerns about ongoing issues damaging the hospital's public image.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, after failing two rounds of IVF, decided to use their remaining savings for a wedding instead, but won a competition to have a second wedding. They subsequently conceived twins Darci-Mai and Stanley, achieving both their dreams of a family and a wedding.

A family-friendly coffee shop's Facebook page was hacked and flooded with adult content for nearly 24 hours after an employee clicked on a malicious link. The breach, similar to those on other major brands, was only resolved after repeated attempts to contact Facebook, leading to an apology and removal of inappropriate content.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center barked and squeaked after meeting a husky, causing amusement among onlookers. The puppies conversed with high-pitched whines and yaps, with the Shibu Inu eventually barking loudly, leading to laughter from passersby. This behavior is typical for puppies, who usually begin vocalizing around two-to-three weeks and develop stronger barks by eight weeks.

Liam Plunkett, an England seamer, is eager to use his pace to dominate West Indies' batting line-up in the upcoming Test series. After recovering from an ankle injury, he aims to prove his worth in the competition, vying with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood for a spot in the England Test side alongside experienced bowlers James Anderson and Stuart Broad.

Paul Smith, a Liverpool boxer, faces a potential third fight against Andre Ward, a former world champion, as Ward sees Smith as a suitable warm-up opponent before a potential rematch with Carl Froch. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to meet in a unification fight, but Froch prefers to stay in the UK, leading to Ward potentially facing Smith in Oakland.

Tyrus Byrd, the first black mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in after her election, but five of six police officers and several other top officials resigned. The reasons for their departures, citing 'safety concerns,' remain unclear, overshadowing Byrd's victory. Residents and the outgoing mayor Randall Ramsey are puzzled by the resignations, with some suggesting the move may have been politically motivated.

Manchester City will make Yaya Toure available for sale this summer, despite not forcing him out, as the club looks to reshape their squad. Toure, who has been with City since 2010 and is content at the club, is reportedly interested in a potential move to Inter Milan, but the wages are a sticking point. Meanwhile, City will not allow Valencia to block a £24m deal for Alvaro Negredo, who has struggled at the Spanish club.

A new study suggests that over two-thirds of people taking antidepressants do not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. The research also found that antidepressants are often prescribed for conditions like obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, and generalized anxiety disorder, where many patients do not meet the diagnostic criteria. This raises questions about the overprescription of antidepressants without clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller, mother of mentally ill daughter Natalie, 28, who died by stepping in front of a train. Fuller revealed Natalie suffered from bipolar disorder and psychosis, undiagnosed until her 20s, leading to her tragic suicide. Fuller wrote about how Natalie's illness worsened, filled with terrifying voices, and how her daughter's bravery and creativity contrasted with her struggles.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest during a British Bulldog game in the school playground, collapsing and losing consciousness for 12 minutes. His heart stopped beating, and he was revived by CPR and a defibrillator by teachers and paramedics, who later diagnosed him with a condition similar to that of footballer Fabrice Muamba.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, advocates for divorce laws that remove the need for allegations of adultery or blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. She proposes a 'no fault' divorce system, encouraging couples to resolve child and financial arrangements before obtaining a divorce, with a one-year cooling-off period.

Tottenham are considering a £400m stadium with a retractable pitch for an NFL London franchise, potentially sharing it with NFL teams testing logistics at Wembley. The new stadium could better accommodate NFL squad sizes and offer advantages like quicker player return to the US, future-proofing for a potential NFL franchise.

U.S. senators urge FIFA to remove Russia as 2018 World Cup host, citing Russia's involvement in the Ukraine crisis and Crimea occupation. The senators argue this would better align with international sanctions and economic pressures on Russia. England is considering a bid for Euro 2028 but unlikely for 2026 World Cup, with the decision on the latter to be made in 2017.

Universal announced "Fifty Shades Darker" will be released on February 10, 2017, with Niall Leonard writing the script. The sequel, "Fifty Shades Freed," is set for February 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, the author's husband, will write the script, while Sam Taylor-Johnson is not returning to direct. Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan are renegotiating their contracts for the sequel, which is expected to earn more than the first film.

West Brom manager Tony Pulis faces a challenging return to Crystal Palace, having never managed a top-half finish in the Premier League despite his success at Stoke and Palace. His overall record is the worst of any long-serving Premier League manager, and his current team's struggles, including recent defeats, threaten to end his record of never being relegated.

Fenerbahçe called for a championship suspension after their team bus was attacked by armed assailants near the airport, injuring the driver. The incident occurred following a match, and the club emphasized the need for justice and safety, citing damage to the bus and blood on the driver's seat.

A massive avalanche hit Everest Base Camp, causing panic and injury. At least 17 people died, and dozens were injured or missing. The earthquake, which killed over 4,300 people, also blocked rescue efforts due to damaged icefall routes and aftershocks. Helicopters were used to evacuate survivors from higher camps.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during WWII, fought Nazis and later survived another war in Ukraine. Now 87, he faces another conflict, suffering from Alzheimer's but remembering the horrors of WWII. His family moved to Israel after his house was hit by a missile, fearing further war. Margolin, part of a wave of Ukrainian Jewish immigrants to Israel, now lives in the quietest place for him.

John Carver, now fighting for the Newcastle head coach position, is acutely aware of the impact of a Tyne-Wear derby result. In 1999, his mentor Ruud Gullit's controversial decision to leave out key players Alan Shearer and Duncan Ferguson led to Newcastle's defeat and Gullit's dismissal. Carver is eager to avoid a similar fate, knowing a derby win could significantly boost his chances.

Revered Al Sharpton attended a vigil in North Charleston for Walter Scott, a black man fatally shot by a white police officer. Sharpton preached at Charity Missionary Baptist Church, addressing the Scott case and calling for police reform. He also spoke at a vigil near the shooting scene, praising Mayor Keith Summey for firing the officer involved.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the winger's recent off-field controversies, including videos of him allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide and smoking a shisha pipe. Sterling scored the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United, but Rodgers emphasized that the club will investigate his behavior and that Sterling will be spoken to internally about his responsibilities as a professional.

Labour received £1.1 million in donations from unions in the final week of the election, more than twice as much as the Conservatives, who received £492,512. Unions like Unison and Unite provided over £700,000, while the Tories received most of their donations from wealthy individuals. This funding gap is seen as a disadvantage for the Conservatives and highlights the influence of union money on Labour's campaign.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight diverted to Birmingham Airport due to severe winds became disruptive, leading to police intervention. After a delay, passengers were stranded for hours in Manchester, causing frustration and some passengers claiming they waited up to 24 hours. Police were called twice, and Qatar Airways apologized, stating safety was prioritized and a new crew was quickly arranged.

Justin Bieber, a close friend of boxing legend Floyd Mayweather, will accompany Mayweather into the ring for his $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao. The 21-year-old pop star has been part of Mayweather's entourage in previous fights and is set to lead the American boxer's team for the upcoming bout, despite initial reports suggesting he would only accompany Mayweather into the ring.

Corinthian Colleges, once a major player with over 70,000 students, is shutting down all campuses due to federal restrictions on federal student aid. For-profit colleges, which often exploit students with high debt and poor job prospects, enroll about 1.3 million students and are a significant source of federal student loan defaults. Recent actions, including a debt strike by graduates and potential loan forgiveness, aim to address the problematic practices of these institutions.

Former Bayern Munich doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt quit the club after claiming the medical staff was blamed for the 3-1 Champions League loss to Porto. Guardiola denied any feud with Muller-Wohlfahrt, stating the doctor's decision was personal and unrelated to their professional relationship. Muller-Wohlfahrt cited injuries as the reason for the bond of trust being damaged, while Guardiola blamed himself for the defeat.

Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, 39, is preparing for his world title defense against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden. He recalls winning Olympic gold in 1996, which catapulted him into a hero in Ukraine. Despite being just a year shy of 40, Klitschko remains dominant, attributing his longevity to a healthy lifestyle and experience.

Jeremy Clarkson, fired from Top Gear after an altercation with a producer, expressed his regret at leaving the show, saying he would miss being there. Former presenter Angela Rippon, who first hosted the show 38 years ago, expressed interest in returning, while Clarkson welcomed support from fans. The future of the show remains uncertain, with Lord Hall stating no new contract will be renewed for Clarkson, and suggestions of potential new presenters like Nick Knowles and Jodie Kidd.

In a La Liga match, Celta Vigo striker Fabian Orellana was shown a red card and struck by a lump of grass thrown at Barcelona's Sergio Busquets during a heated final stage. Busquets, known for his resilience, took advantage of the incident, but Orellana was sent off. Despite the incident, Barcelona secured a 1-0 win over Celta Vigo, thanks to Jeremy Mathieu's header, and maintained their position in the league.

In 2013, the Boston Marathon was marred by bombings that killed three and injured over 200. This year, a federal judge warned jurors to avoid the marathon and related events during the sentencing phase of Dzhokhar Tsarnaev's trial, which begins April 21. Tsarnaev was convicted of all charges related to the bombings, with a possible death penalty.

Millions of Chinese marked the Qingming Festival by visiting ancestral graves, cleaning tombs, and holding colorful ceremonies in honor of the 'Yellow Emperor' Huangdi, celebrating the start of spring and the beauty of nature. The three-day holiday, falling in April, includes outdoor celebrations, traditional dances, and offerings to ancestors, reflecting China's rich cultural heritage.

Paul Simon, 73, has returned to the UK album chart's top spot with "The Ultimate Collection," his first since 1990. The album, featuring hits from his 50-year career, topped the charts, beating out newer artists like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. His recent tour with Sting is believed to have contributed to the album's success.

Iker Casillas, Real Madrid's long-serving goalkeeper, insists he will stay at the club until his contract ends, despite David de Gea's potential return from Manchester United. Casillas, 33, claims he will fight for the starting position and help Real Madrid defend their Champions League title, emphasizing his commitment to the club.

Britain saw its highest employment level in history, with 557,000 more people in work in the past year. This has won international praise, including from the International Monetary Fund, which commended Chancellor George Osborne. Despite Labour's opposition to austerity measures, the UK's deficit has been significantly reduced, and the economy is on track for growth and low inflation. However, Greece's potential default poses a threat to the global economy, including Britain.

Korea's SsangYong is launching a new sports utility vehicle, the Tivoli, priced under £13,000, aimed at budget-conscious drivers. The Tivoli offers European styling and features like six-speed manual and automatic transmissions, seven airbags, and a choice of engines. In contrast, Citroen's Aircross, shown in prototype form, features protective alloy bumps for added durability, reminiscent of old Tonka toys.

Chef Sam Longhurst created a 10-inch tall, 2,000-calorie burger at Splendid Kitchen in Manchester, featuring six types of meat including two beef patties, ham, chicken, pulled pork, and bacon, in response to a customer's challenge. The burger, named "The Whole Damn Farm," weighs half a kilogram and contains a meat equivalent of six Big Macs.

Yeo Valley's staff canteen offers Michelin-starred dishes for as little as £2, sourced from organic, locally-sourced ingredients. The canteen, staffed by a Michelin-trained chef, serves daily-changing menus including beef burgers, fish cakes, and desserts, all at subsidized prices for 120 dairy workers overlooking the Blagdon countryside.

Legendary blues musician B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration due to Type II diabetes, but he recovered quickly and is now back home with his family, thanking fans for their well-wishes. King, 89, has a history of health issues, including a canceled tour in 2022 due to similar dehydration.

Manhattan's Fifth Avenue hosted an Easter parade with participants wearing bizarre hats, including bunny ears, eggs, flowers, and elaborate designs. The event featured a mix of religious attendees, secular revelers, and creative headwear, reflecting the parade's evolution from a strolling display of fashionable attire in the 1880s to a celebration of individual creativity.

Emergency crews in Essex dispatched two ambulances to Epping Forest after a caller reported a person hit by a car, only to discover the "victim" was a squirrel. The East of England ambulance service has released a list of 1,248 inappropriate calls, including a man who dropped a burger that "bleeded," a woman who claimed to be locked out, and a man who said his feet hurt from small shoes. These calls divert resources from genuine emergencies, potentially endangering lives.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake won an Audi-sponsored football challenge, defeating team-mates Loic Remy and Willian in two rounds. In the final, Remy and Willian won but caused damage by smashing a wing mirror off an Audi with a long-range shot.

Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, for allegedly manipulating Sterling, who has two years left on his Liverpool contract. Rodgers believes Sterling would stay if left to make a decision alone, citing the player's enjoyment of playing for Liverpool and the club's financial benefits for him. Rodgers also noted that Sterling was flattered by Arsenal's interest but has rejected a contract extension.

Countdown host Nick Hewer struggled to keep from laughing when contestants offered the double entendre 'erection' as a word. This incident followed other embarrassing moments for hosts, including 'todgers' and 'm*nges', highlighting the show's history of unintentionally humorous word submissions.

A 16-year-old boy from Greater Manchester who tried to buy deadly poison online was spared jail after the court heard he wanted to commit suicide. Officers from the North West Counter Terrorism Unit intervened after receiving information he was attempting to obtain the toxin, which they found on the dark web. The teenager pleaded guilty and was sentenced to a 12-month referral order.

Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four, died three hours after giving birth to her baby girl at North Manchester General Hospital, where three other babies and one mother had died in the previous months. Her partner Chris Barnes called for action to prevent further tragedies at the hospital, citing concerns about inadequate care and staff presence during her birth.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after training while eight months pregnant. The 32-year-old, a two-time world champion hurdler, plans to compete in the 2016 Rio Olympics and has been managing her pregnancy and training carefully. Emily was conceived with an anonymous sperm donor, and Pittman credits her son Cornelis for changing her life.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats during a regatta, resulting in at least one death and missing crew members. Over 100 boats and 200 people were involved in the Dauphin Island Regatta in Mobile Bay; at least one person was confirmed dead, and search efforts continued into the night. The storm was more severe than expected, causing boats to sink rapidly and leaving crews exhausted but uninjured.

Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma. These eye diseases progressively worsen, with symptoms worsening for Barr. While there is no cure, treatments can delay progression and protect vision.

A 17-year-old Oklahoma youth, Chancey Allen Luna, was convicted of first-degree murder for shooting and killing Christopher Lane, an Australian college baseball player, during a jog. The jury recommended life in prison without parole, despite Luna firing from a passing car with no apparent motive. Luna's defense argued it was a reckless act by a 16-year-old, but the judge denied a second-degree murder charge.

Arsene Wenger insists his 12-0-7 record against Jose Mourinho won't affect their upcoming match, focusing on the game's outcome rather than past rivalries. Despite Wenger's poor record, Arsenal are on a good run and aim to beat Chelsea, who are top of the Premier League. Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas will face his former team in the match, with Wenger asking for respect for Fabregas.

Manny Pacquiao, born into poverty in the Philippines, rose to global fame through a series of high-profile fights, including those against Oscar De La Hoya and Juan Manuel Marquez. He began his career in the Far East, moving to Manila at 14, and made his big break in 2001 with a world super-bantamweight title fight. Now 36, Pacquiao faces Floyd Mayweather in the "Fight of the Century" on the Las Vegas Strip, a far cry from his early days as a 17-year-old training in Manila's LM Gym.

Jack Grealish, a top football player, was photographed using nitrous oxide, a legal but illegal substance for athletes. This incident highlights the importance of maintaining a clean body for professional sports, as seen by Arsenal's former manager Arsene Wenger, who emphasized the need to prioritize health over pleasure. Despite his talent, Grealish's future success depends on making the right choices.

Sam Barton, who underwent £55,000 of cosmetic surgery, was attacked with eggs by a group of men on Easter Monday after checking in at a pub on Facebook. The incident occurred after he was criticized online for his appearance, forcing him to move houses. Barton, who has also spent money on teeth, Botox, and waxing, was targeted for his celebrity aspirations, including filming with reality TV stars.

An Indiana university was placed on lockdown after receiving a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the administration building. Police responded but determined it was a hoax, and the university advised students to shelter in place, though no injuries were confirmed.

Edinson Cavani, known as El Matador, prepares for a crucial Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona. PSG, without key players like Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Veratti, relies heavily on Cavani to break through Barcelona's defense. However, Cavani has been struggling with a goal drought and recent off-field issues, making his performance crucial for PSG's chances.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title by unanimous decision over Tony Luis in Liverpool, after Richar Abril and Ismael Barroso pulled out due to illness or visa issues. Mathews controlled the fight, landing an uppercut, while Luis showed aggression but ultimately lost the tight decision.

Hull secured a surprise 28-20 victory over St Helens at Langtree Park, reversing their previous loss to the same team. Despite St Helens' early lead and a late surge, Hull's pressure and a try by Jamie Shaul sealed the win, ending St Helens' three-game losing streak.

The U.S. immigrant population, including documented and undocumented, is projected to reach 51 million by 2023, making up 14.8% of the population. By 2060, immigrants could account for 82% of the country's population growth, with their share of the population expected to rise to 18.8% by then. This growth is driven by net immigration that will increase by 64 million over the next 45 years, without changes to current immigration policies.

Jack Wilshere made his return from injury as captain for Arsenal U21s, but they lost 1-0 to Reading's U21s. Wilshere and other injured first-team players like Abou Diaby and Serge Gnabri played, with Martin Keown's son scoring the only goal in the opening minutes.

English golfer Justin Rose, struggling with form after a poor Florida swing, has shown encouraging signs at the Shell Houston Open, hitting 17 out of 18 greens and recording a 69. Rose attributes his recent improvement to correcting his swing faults and using an old putter, emphasizing that his focus is on his game rather than the world rankings, which he acknowledges can be a source of pride.

A former milking parlour in Mayfair, London, has been transformed into a £25 million luxury mansion featuring modern amenities like an indoor pool, cinema room, and lift. Originally used for milking in the 19th century, the site now houses four bedrooms and a grand piano in its grand hall.

Bayern Munich, despite facing significant injuries, showed unity in recent games against Dortmund and Leverkusen. Coach Thomas Muller believes this cohesion will help them against Porto in the Champions League, relying on Muller and Lewandowski's goalscoring ability. Bayern will face Porto in the quarter-final first leg on April 15, aiming to avoid the team's recent dominance in the group stage.

Mercedes team-mates Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited Mercedes' Brackley base to strategize against Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel, who won the Malaysian Grand Prix. Despite Mercedes' comfortable one-two start, Vettel's victory in hot conditions highlighted Mercedes' need to improve their race strategy.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection is deemed unconstitutional or unavailable. The gas causes quick unconsciousness and death from lack of oxygen, though it has never been used in U.S. executions. Fallin supports the death penalty, citing the need for an effective and humane method of execution.

Swansea's Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in a 3-1 win over Hull, topping this week's EA Sports Performance Index with a Game Index score of 52.9. Gomis has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games. Charlie Austin of Queens Park Rangers is the runner-up with a score of 52.2, following a 4-1 win against West Brom.

A Russian freezer trawler carrying 132 crew members sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 and injuring many more. The ship, Dalny Vostok, sank in just 15 minutes after a fishing net was pulled in, causing it to become unstable. A massive rescue operation involving over 1,300 people is underway, with 63 survivors rescued and 13 still missing. Temperatures in the water are extremely low, posing significant challenges for rescue efforts.

A pioneering drug originally used for women with cancer caused by BRCA gene mutations is showing promise in treating advanced prostate cancer in men with DNA repair defects. Clinical trials indicate olaparib, or Lynparza, can delay disease progression and extend survival, marking the first PARP inhibitor to show efficacy in prostate cancer. The drug targets inherited genetic mutations, offering a new precision treatment option for this group of patients.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, reviews luxurious hotels and documents her experiences on her Instagram-based website 'In Bed With'. With over 12,000 followers, she has turned her passion for photography into a business, earning commissions from hotels and travel product companies for her reviews and photos.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was fatally injured and thrown into the air during a fight between two adult males in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, South Africa. The calf's mother, believing it safer to stay with the herd, watched helplessly as her baby was dragged away and died, having been caught in the jaws of one of the fighting adults.

The Football Association will investigate an incident at a Chelsea vs. QPR match where supporters threw objects, including a cigarette lighter, at the players. QPR is unlikely to face disciplinary action but will review CCTV and ban those involved. Chelsea players were struck during celebrations, and the club is appealing for witness information to identify the culprits.

LaTasha Gosling and her three children, Janyaa, Jenika, and Landen, were found murdered in their Saskatchewan home. The suspect, believed to know the family, was found dead hours later, though his cause of death is unknown. The family's GoFundMe page has exceeded its initial goal for funeral costs.

Labour MP Emily Thornberry, who opposes the right to buy for council tenants, has been criticized for renting out a housing association property she bought for £1 million eight years ago. Thornberry's hypocrisy has been highlighted as she supports the policy for council homes but not for housing association properties, which are now worth almost £1 million.

Police dropped an investigation into a violent assault on Mike Lane, a huntsman, despite substantial evidence. Lane, who was beaten by protesters during a hunt, criticized the decision, stating the police could have made more effort. The case was shelved by Wiltshire Police, leaving Lane and supporters disappointed and questioning the police's commitment to justice.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, insists he has no plans to leave the club this summer, despite Premier League interest from Manchester United and Chelsea. Gomes, who joined Valencia from Benfica last summer, has scored four goals in 25 La Liga appearances and is happy with his current situation.

Australian teenager Audrey Pekin, 19, alleges she was raped twice by Henry Alafu on Christmas Eve in Bali. Initially lured to Alafu's remote home, she was raped again in a taxi after trying to flee. Despite her pleas for help, Alafu followed her, and she escaped only to be raped again in a cab. Pekin criticizes Indonesian police for failing to prevent Alafu's escape back to Nigeria.

Former Made In Chelsea star Ashley James, in solidarity with animal rights group PETA, posed with a fake skinned fox at Harvey Nichols, a department store that recently reintroduced fur products. James, who supports veganism and avoids fur, aims to raise awareness about the cruelty in the fur industry through this campaign, challenging customers to question the authenticity of fur items and make informed purchasing decisions.

Chile has enacted a new law recognizing civil unions between same-sex couples, joining several South American countries in this move. The law, signed by President Michelle Bachelet, will take effect in six months and aims to provide legal rights and protections similar to those of heterosexual couples, ending discrimination faced by common-law same-sex couples.

Chelsea are on track to break the Premier League record for most days at the top of the table in a single season, currently leading for 230 days. They are seven points clear of second-placed rivals with a game in hand, and their upcoming matches against QPR, Manchester United, and Arsenal could be decisive in securing the title.

Cape Verde, known for its musical diversity and rich cultural heritage, is leveraging its music industry to boost its economy. Despite being resource-poor, the country has turned to music as a key sector, with initiatives like the Kriol Jazz Festival attracting international artists. This approach aims to capitalize on the island's unique musical traditions and foster a vibrant creative economy.

An old hoax video of a wave rider surfing in front of Sydney's Opera House has gone viral again, following heavy storms. Initially posted by a Sydney radio duo in June 2012, the video was quickly retweeted and mocked for inaccuracies, including the appearance of rocks and the man's unrealistic surfing attire. Experts dismissed it as impossible due to the distance from the ocean and the strength of waves.

Reading lost to Birmingham 1-0 in a Championship match, despite dominating the first half. Clayton Donaldson scored the decisive goal in the 87th minute, securing Birmingham's victory and preventing Reading from securing a top-flight spot.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, suffered a hamstring injury during a match against Marseille, potentially missing the Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona for at least four weeks. This injury could impact PSG's Ligue One title defense and their upcoming Champions League campaign.

The return of Game of Thrones has led to a significant surge in illegal downloads, with over 100,000 illegal episodes downloaded daily. More than seven million episodes from seasons one to four were illegally downloaded between February and April, up 45% year-on-year. Despite HBO's efforts to launch the season globally and offer a streaming service, piracy remains a major issue.

Leicester City faces West Ham United at King Power Stadium with Matt Upson and Dean Hammond unavailable. Leicester is fighting for survival, while West Ham welcomes back Winston Reid from injury. The match features key stats showing West Ham's recent defensive struggles and Leicester's poor home form.

Residents of Celoron, NY, are outraged by a statue of Lucile Ball that they find unflattering, resembling her drunken pitch for a health tonic on I Love Lucy. A Facebook page calling for its removal has over 600 likes, with critics arguing it doesn't resemble the beloved comedian. The statue's artist, Dave Poulin, has declined to comment, and a replacement would cost around $8,000-$10,000.

Sharon Smith, a 43-year-old woman who weighed nearly 20 stone, lost over half her weight to 9 stone 9 pounds after an uncomfortable flight forced her to stand for 11 hours. Initially joining Weight Watchers Online, she then started running and quitting her job to freelance, leading to significant weight loss and a healthier lifestyle.

Nicola Bonn, a new mother from London, started an online blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and challenges of raising her 14-month-old daughter Poppy. She aims to help other new mothers by sharing her candid experiences and addressing common criticisms, emphasizing the importance of self-justification and confidence in parenting decisions.

Two 17-year-old British teenagers, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, are believed to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS. They are related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested for planning to murder non-Muslims at 15. The families are in shock and deeply worried about their safety, urging anyone with information to contact authorities.

Stephanie Scott, a school teacher, was brutally murdered just days before her wedding, leaving her family devastated. Her father, Robert, explains the pain of her untimely death, especially as she had so much to look forward to, including a wedding with a guest list of 120. The couple had been preparing for their first dance, but the ceremony was canceled after her body was found nearby.

Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old Feyenoord winger, is set to leave the club this summer, with Southampton interested and Ronald Koeman keen to bring him to St Mary's. Additionally, Southampton is monitoring Jordy Clasie, a £10m-rated midfielder, and may make Eljero Elia's loan permanent to strengthen the squad for potential European qualification.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, sparking controversy among heritage experts. The move, intended to encourage visitors to 'dwell' in the room, was deemed misguided by some, while the Trust defended it as a short-term experiment to engage new audiences.

Former Prime Minister John Howard found himself with a flat tyre in Sydney, and his driver changed it while standing on the footpath. Felicity Waterford, waiting for her daughter at the Sydney Conservatorium, offered assistance and took a selfie with Howard, who was described as a "complete gentleman." This incident contrasted with a recent challenge faced by Liberal MP Christopher Pyne to change a tyre on national television.

Tony Pulis acknowledges Joey Barton's claim that West Brom's players 's*** themselves' after losing 3-2 to Queens Park Rangers, admitting Barton probably had a point given the team's 2-0 lead. Pulis, however, credits his team's recent strong performances and defends his team's resilience against losing leads.

A Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought extinct for over 50 years, was captured in photographs in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Additionally, researchers discovered a new species of white-cheeked macaque in Tibet, identified by its unique penis shape, which had previously been misidentified.

Kim Kardashian and her family visited Armenia, the birthplace of her late father, for an eight-day trip. They stayed in Yerevan, the capital, exploring landmarks like the Yerevan Opera House and the Katoghiken church in Geghard Monastery. The visit highlights Armenia's cultural richness and its appeal to celebrities, despite its Soviet-era architecture and bustling modern atmosphere.

British expats Patrick and Valerie Jubb are trapped in southern Spain over a legal battle with the local town hall regarding alterations made to their luxury bed and breakfast. They wish to sell the property but face demolition due to alleged illegal additions, despite obtaining a certificate stating no infractions when they purchased it in 2008. The couple, who moved to the UK, is now financially tied to the estate and seeks to relocate.

Apple reported its best-ever quarterly results, with 61 million iPhones sold, accounting for over two-thirds of its $58 billion revenue and $13.6 billion profit. Despite a slight dip from the previous quarter, iPhone sales grew 40% year-over-year and outpaced other products like iPads and Macs. The strong performance, especially in China, underscores the iPhone's continued dominance and Apple's overall robust financial health.

A 3-year-old's recurring nightmares about a white van have led to speculation that her mother's fatal SUV crash in Virginia may have involved a hit-and-run incident. The child's father, Craig Tyler, noticed similar hit-and-run accidents involving a white delivery truck in the area, which he believes may be linked to his daughter's disturbing dreams.

Researchers found that the brain can better remember neutral events tied to emotion, contrary to the common belief that we remember emotionally charged events more easily. This study, focusing on the September 11 attacks, suggests that emotion enhances memory consolidation, affecting brain regions involved in emotional processing and new experience encoding. Sleep also plays a role in memory consolidation, with a 45-minute nap reportedly boosting recall by five times.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of 18-year-old Jackson Byrnes with a stage four brain tumour, has been caring for him since his diagnosis. They have raised over $80,000 for Dr. Charlie Teo's life-saving surgery, which is now set for Wednesday. Despite the surgery's potential to save his life, Byrnes will likely remain paralysed, requiring a long rehabilitation process.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back, is a target for Hull City amid the club's potential relegation. Onuoha, who has 15 months left on his contract, was in the starting lineup for QPR's recent win over West Bromwich Albion. Hull is also interested in West Bromwich Albion striker Victor Anichebe, who could be sold this summer.

Every state in the US has unique phrases that can sound strange to outsiders, as documented in a Yale University study through an interactive map. The research reveals regional variations in sentence structure, with some sentences like 'here's you a piece of pizza' being common in the South but rare in the North.

A Canadian man, Kalman Kallai, traveled 2,796 miles across Canada in a free green rocking chair, taking in the scenery and sharing the journey with his friend. Along the way, he posed for cameras, mimicked planes, and even danced with his father, creating a unique and humorous travel experience.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood humorously revealed his "win bonus" to Charlie Pye, a six-year-old fan who applied for the Villa job after Paul Lambert's dismissal. Sherwood sent Pye a Twix multi-pack, jokingly thanking him for the chocolate sent as a bonus for his previous application to Tottenham.

World boxing champion Kell Brook watched the Premier League Darts in Sheffield, where he received a hero's welcome. Dave Chisnall, who was introduced to the crowd, won both of his games in the 10th week, moving to 17 points and second place in the table. Brook is set to defend his title against Frankie Gavin on May 30.

Italian midfielder Marco Verratti praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic's crucial role for Paris Saint-Germain, both on and off the pitch, highlighting his help to young players and confidence boost for the team. Despite a suspension for the Champions League match, Ibrahimovic is set to return for the return leg against Barcelona.

The RAF's Aerodrome Manual, containing GPS coordinates and runway depth information, was accidentally published on the Ministry of Defence's website, exposing vital Falklands defense details. This could be used by Argentina to plan an invasion, prompting the MoD to disable the link but denying the information's sensitivity. Argentina is also considering leasing Cold War-era SU-24 bombers from Russia, which could pose a threat to Falklands defense.

Huddersfield Giants coach Paul Anderson aims to improve their offensive play to match their strong defensive record, currently ninth in Super League. After losing all three games since Easter, they face Catalans Dragons, who lead in defensive efficiency, in a crucial home game. A win could propel them to fourth place, while Widnes Vikings, who have only one point from five away games, aim to beat Castleford, who have a solid defensive unit.

Windsor planners approved two Costa Coffee shops less than 500 yards apart, including one replacing a cycle shop earlier this year. This brings the total to three Costas within a mile, with planners citing local trade benefits, despite one resident's concern about over-saturation of coffee shops.

The British Veterinary Association has withdrawn support for shooting free-running badgers in pilot culls due to lack of conclusive effectiveness and humane outcomes. The BVA still supports badger culling to control bovine tuberculosis in cattle, but opposes cage-trapping and shooting. The Environment Secretary pledged to expand culls if the Tories win, despite criticism and low efficacy in some pilot areas.

Portishead's Geoff Barrow criticizes streaming services for low royalties, arguing his band received just £1,700 for 34 million plays. He calls for fairer compensation for musicians, citing issues for young talent, while streaming companies defend their practices, offering artists a fair price. Artists like Jay-Z and Taylor Swift have launched their own services to provide better deals.

Fans of Game of Thrones leaked the first four episodes of its fifth season online before the official premiere. These episodes, titled "The Wars to Come," "The House of Black and White," "High Sparrow," and "The Sons of the Harpy," have been downloaded more than 550,000 times. The show, known for its high piracy rates, has been illegally downloaded over seven million times for its first four seasons, with Brazil and France leading in illegal downloads. HBO plans to combat international piracy with a simultaneous premiere in 170 countries.

Melbourne singer Daniel Buccheri composed an emotional song to use as his best man's speech at his brother's wedding, which included tributes to his brother and new wife. His unique performance, featuring a keyboard rendition of "Stay With Me," left guests in tears and has been viewed over 100,000 times online.

Zara Phillips, after the birth of her daughter Mia, regained her fitness by exercising on an exercise bike every morning before her daughter wakes up. She follows a strict diet and exercises regularly, aiming to qualify for Team GB in the 2016 Olympics, where she hopes to compete in eventing.

Raheem Sterling's interview expressing reluctance to sign a new contract at Liverpool was poorly received, potentially alienating fans. Sterling's situation has led to increased speculation about his future, with some fans now believing he should be allowed to leave. Liverpool fans maintain that no player is bigger than the club, but Sterling's departure is increasingly seen as a possibility.

Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola conversed at Barcelona during their time there, with Mourinho famously mocking Guardiola's future Barça coaching ambitions. Recent scans of old Barcelona training photos revealed more connections, including current PSG coach Laurent Blanc and Porto coach Julen Lopetegui, suggesting a network of former Barcelona players and coaches.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona, at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai, controversially named Paris Saint-Germain's Javier Pastore as the best player in the world, praising his creativity and passing ability over Messi and Ronaldo. Cantona's assessment was based on his observation of Pastore's performances, highlighting his unique skills and surprising abilities.

Lorenzo Simon was found guilty of murdering his tenant Michael Spalding by dismembering his body and dumping the parts in a canal. Simon, with his girlfriend Michelle Bird, hacked Spalding to death, dismembered his body, and hid the remains in two suitcases, which were later discovered by police.

Health experts warn that social isolation is as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day, leading to dementia and high blood pressure. Essex and Gloucestershire councils have developed 'loneliness maps' to identify areas with the highest risk of social isolation among elderly residents, using factors like age, living alone, mental health, and income. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends this approach for tackling the issue nationwide.

Judy Eddingfield, a 65-year-old waitress, celebrated her 50th anniversary at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she has worked since she was 15. She considers it her only job and the only one she's ever wanted, citing family tradition and fond memories, including serving celebrities like 'Leave It to Beaver' actors.

Former England captain Mike Gatting suggests Kevin Pietersen should not automatically return to the international team, even if he performs well for Surrey. Gatting believes Pietersen needs to show he's not just playing well, but better than those already in the team, and that Alastair Cook's poor form could lead to questions about his captaincy if he doesn't score runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old Californian student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos directly from their computer to Instagram, bypassing the app's mobile-only upload feature. The app, which he sells for $4.99, is currently generating $1,000 daily. Facebook, which owns Instagram, has warned Benn that his app violates their terms of service, but he refuses to comply, citing the app's legal gray area.

In South Korea, hoesik (company dinners) often involve intense drinking sessions, with pressure to participate. Drinking is seen as a way to get to know someone, and Koreans consider it rude to have an empty glass. Drinking etiquette includes turning away from seniors during the "one-shot" drinking ritual.

The Duke of Kent, 79, suffered a dislocated hip while visiting Balmoral estate and was hospitalized at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. He was discharged after a night's treatment and is expected to recover. This injury comes two years after he had a mild stroke, and despite his age, he continues to perform royal duties.

The 50-year-old Surfers Paradise Meter Maids, introduced to combat parking meter bad publicity, are facing criticism from local business leaders who argue they are outdated and irrelevant due to electronic parking meters. The group, now seen as a business, is violating anti-touting laws and is being labeled as a source of bad tourism reputation by the Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce. However, the Meter Maids defend their role as a beloved part of the Gold Coast experience.

Greece denies it will default on a £330 million IMF loan due on April 9, with Deputy Finance Minister Dimitris Mardas stating the country will make the payment. However, sources close to the Syriza party claim the government prioritizes paying wages and pensions over loans, potentially leading to a default if the eurozone does not agree to timely payments. Greek officials dispute reports of a planned parallel drachma currency and emphasize their commitment to meeting financial obligations.

Turkey blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing requests to remove images of prosecutor Mehmet Selim Kiraz, who was killed during a siege. The images upset the hostage's family, and the prosecutor's office demanded their removal, leading to the social media blocks.

Seven-year-old Colin Gilpatric, an aspiring Jedi, wrote to George Lucas asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucas responded, explaining that forming attachments can lead to the 'dark side' and that true Jedi values are important in marriage. Colin was thrilled to receive a letter from Lucasfilm, signed by 'Your friends at Lucasfilm', assuring him that Jedi can marry and that his values are key to avoiding the dark side.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky 71-64 to advance to the NCAA Final Four, ending Kentucky's 38-1 unbeaten streak. The Badgers, led by Frank Kaminsky, secured a spot in the final game against Duke, who won their semi-final 81-61 over Michigan State.

Vince Neil's performance of the national anthem before a football game was criticized, contrasting with Whitney Houston's Super Bowl performance and Jimi Hendrix's controversial psychedelic rendition. Michael Bolton's version, with incorrect lyrics, further highlights the mixed reactions to national anthem performances.

CCTV footage shows Barry Lyttle punching his brother Patrick, causing him to fall and suffer a severe head injury in Sydney. Patrick was hospitalized and nearly died; Barry pleaded guilty to grievous bodily harm and faces a potential jail sentence, with his fate to be decided in court.

Conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, born with disrosopus, died 19 days after birth. Their family set up a shrine at their gravesite in Sydney's Pinegrove Memorial Park, but upon visiting, found it cleared and their belongings discarded. The family was devastated and confronted cemetery staff, who claimed no prior notice was given for cleaning.

Britain's Supreme Court President, Lord Neuberger, suggests allowing Muslim women to wear full-face veils in court to show respect for their cultural customs. This comes amid uncertainty over the place of traditional dress in the legal system, following a 2003 trial where a Muslim woman refused to testify due to a face veil requirement. Lord Neuberger calls for judges to be sensitive to the 'artificial and intimidating' nature of courts, emphasizing the need for understanding and respect for diverse cultural backgrounds.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed in Missouri for killing Anthony Curtis in a fit of rage over child support 16 years ago. Cole became the third convicted killer put to death this year in Missouri, despite appeals claiming he was mentally ill and unfit for execution. His execution was marked by a day's inmate meal and no last statement, with Governor Jay Nixon emphasizing the importance of remembering crime victims.

Prince Harry will fly to Australia without meeting his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is now expected to give birth by Saturday, forcing Harry to miss the arrival. He had briefly returned to London to meet Prince George, but now must return to Australia for a month-long placement with the army.

Justin Jackson, a Florida man, has been accused of impersonating celebrities including Oprah Winfrey, Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager to obtain freebies, jobs, and luxury items worth $2.4 million. Jackson's schemes spanned eight years, including posing as Oprah herself and sending fraudulent job recommendations to hotels and jewelry companies. He was convicted for grand theft and faces lawsuits from Oprah's network and Reggie Love.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has valued Paulo Dybala at €50 million, sparking a bidding war with PSG, Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, and Juventus. Dybala, compared to Lionel Messi, is seen as a potential future star, and Palermo is determined to secure a high price for him, despite the interest from Italian clubs.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians are protesting against President Dilma Rousseff, criticizing her for an economic downturn and a Petrobras bribery scandal. Protesters demand her impeachment, while her supporters defend her and argue corruption is widespread. The Petrobras scandal has divided the country, with many voting for Rousseff initially but now joining the protests due to economic woes and corruption concerns.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has denied that his film "You and the Night" is pornographic, calling it "a piece of art." Despite containing racy scenes, Cantona insists it is not porn and defends the film's aesthetic qualities, praising its beauty and artistic value.

Psychologists found that certain types of music can enhance specific flavors in food and drinks, such as The Beatles' music enhancing the enjoyment of fish and chips. Research suggests that the intensity of Luciano Pavarotti's Nessun Dorma can highlight bitterness in coffee, while Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can emphasize autumnal flavors in pumpkin pudding. Professor Charles Spence from Oxford University explains that music can draw attention to certain notes in food and wine, potentially increasing enjoyment by up to 15%.

Liverpool's Raheem Sterling is holding off contract negotiations until the season ends, according to PFA chief Gordon Taylor. Sterling, who received an £100,000-a-week offer from Liverpool, has been linked with moves to Arsenal and Spanish clubs. Taylor defends Sterling's decision, noting it's common for players to consider their options, and suggests it's best to focus on football during the season.

La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, an Ohio woman, discovered her biological mother Francine Simmons works at the same company and lives just six minutes away. After accessing birth records released by the Ohio Department of Health, Mitchell-Clark connected with Simmons through social media and eventually met her, learning she has three younger sisters she didn't know about. Simmons, now in her 50s, had been trying to contact her daughter for years.

Oscar 'Papoo' Hernandez Jr., a gun trafficker for Aaron Hernandez, pleaded guilty to weapons charges. He sent three firearms to Hernandez a month before the semi-professional football player killed Odin Lloyd. Hernandez Jr. was 'awed' by Hernandez's fame but later faced legal troubles, including solitary confinement and a prison sentence.

33-year-old Joel Parker, after threatening and disrupting a bus driver, threw a Snickers bar at the driver's head during a ride in St Johns County, Florida, leading to his arrest for battery and a $250 bond, with a ban on future bus use.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with striker Saido Berahino, indicating he plans to keep the player beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, linked with a move to Champions League clubs, is likely to be with England's under-21 team until late June. Pulis praised Berahino's performance and attitude, noting he has shown a change in attitude and commitment since joining the club.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a project manager with Welthungerlife, was abducted in Pakistan in 2012 and later killed in a U.S. drone strike. He had worked on reconstruction projects following flooding in Pakistan and was passionate about helping others, despite being taken hostage and killed. His work and life were cut short, leaving a legacy of humanitarian efforts in disaster-stricken areas.

A photographer spotted a massive swarm of hundreds of sharks just 100 feet from a Florida beach, prompting widespread concern. The swarm, believed to be composed of Blacktip and Spinner sharks, was observed migrating to breed in shallower waters. The sighting was shared widely on social media, with experts speculating on the species.

An 11-year-old retired German Shepherd K-9 officer Zeus, who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years, was honored in a grand procession before being put down due to a severe hip disorder. The tribute included a procession through Ridgefield streets, with residents and fellow officers paying their respects, and Zeus was taken to the veterinary hospital for euthanasia.

Reports of child sex abuse cases have surged by over 60% since Operation Yewtree and the Rotherham scandal, with nearly 9,000 reports filed in 2014. Despite the increase, arrests for child sex abuse have fallen by 9%, prompting critics to accuse the government of failing victims. The rise in reports suggests growing public awareness, but the decrease in arrests has led to accusations that police are not adequately addressing the issue.

Iceland has become a popular filming location, with its stunning landscapes featured in numerous TV series and movies. Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Skaftafell National Park, Dettifoss waterfall, and Jökulsárlón lake are among the top filming spots, drawing productions like Game of Thrones, Interstellar, Prometheus, and Thor.

A blue and yellow bathing box on Melbourne's Brighton beach sold for $276,000, a record price over the original asking price. In Sydney, a 100-year-old grey-fronted mechanic's garage was sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home. An 1850s maximum security goal in Victoria is being sold for $2 million, with the owners claiming it is haunted.

Samantha Rawcliffe, 40, suffered a car crash in May 2022, losing control of her body and bladder. Diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND), a rare condition with unexplained neurological symptoms, she now relies on a mobility scooter and takes 32 medications daily. Symptoms include uncontrollable shaking and loss of bladder control, with no known cure or effective treatment plan.

Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created a controversial Lucille Ball statue in Celoron, New York, has admitted to being disappointed with his work. He has offered to remake the sculpture for free, citing it as "by far my most unsettling sculpture," and has pledged to create a new, more flattering version. The statue, based on Ball's famous drunk pitch scene, has been criticized as unflattering and frightening.

Bayern Munich's David Alaba, who had been recovering from a partial knee ligament tear, is out for around seven weeks with a new knee ligament injury. The 22-year-old, crucial for Bayern's treble ambitions, will miss the final stages of the season and is set to start rehabilitation in about a month. Alaba, who had been in excellent form, had helped Bayern stay on track for a Bundesliga title and Champions League quarter-final.

University College London student Beatrice Nokes, daughter of respected solicitors, faces charges of inciting prostitution with Scotland Yard detective Daniel Williams, who is accused of running the ring and hiding profits. Both are on bail and face multiple charges including controlling prostitution and voyeurism.

A firm called Sequester is offering NHS patient data for sale, including details of eating disorders, stress, and various health conditions for as little as 12p per person. This data, also including financial and intimate health information, has prompted investigations by regulatory bodies and concerns about the misuse of personal information.

Jordan Spieth, 21, won the Masters golf tournament, equalling Tiger Woods' record score. Reflecting on his victory, he expressed his deep love and support for his autistic sister Ellie, who was unable to attend. Spieth's triumph was shaped by Ellie's influence, providing perspective and support in his life.

Sunderland's new manager Dick Advocaat, learning from his mistake in underestimating the Old Firm derby during his first season at Rangers, emphasizes the importance of the Wear-Tyne Derby against Newcastle. He acknowledges that every game is crucial for avoiding relegation, but stresses the significance of the local rivalry, promising to get the home crowd behind the team.

A dispute erupted between Belinda Bartholomew and a butcher at a Bondi, Sydney shop over a chicken purchase. Bartholomew claims she was racially abused and treated rudely, while the butcher denies the allegations, stating she was being rude and calling her to go to an "Aussie butcher."

Cadbury has reduced the size of Freddo Frogs from 20g to 12g, a 20% decrease, while keeping the price the same. This follows previous cost-cutting measures like reducing the size of Dairy Milk blocks and Killer Python lollies. The move has sparked public backlash, with many consumers expressing anger over perceived price hikes.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met to outline their values and goals, avoiding mistakes from her 2008 campaign. The document emphasizes humility, discipline, and unity, aiming to secure a path to lasting prosperity for every American. Clinton's campaign will be called "Hillary for America," and she plans to launch on Sunday, starting with visits to Iowa and New Hampshire.

Kyli Wilfson, a 29-year-old, faced excruciating abdominal pain and was unable to eat for over a year due to chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition affecting less than 0.01% of people. Despite her desperate hunger, she lost 30 pounds and postponed her wedding as her illness progressed, requiring a feeding tube. She eventually found a support group on Facebook for chronic pancreatitis sufferers.

In response to the leaders' debate, various memes circulated online featuring images of UK party leaders, including David Cameron, Nick Clegg, Ed Miliband, Nicola Sturgeon, and Nigel Farage. Memes depicted them in unexpected roles, such as Christopher Steed and Stephen Webb from the TV show Gogglebox, or in pop culture references like a Rocky boxing scene.

Amir Khan, who has been eyeing a fight with Floyd Mayweather, now faces a new challenge against Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather, is reportedly set to face Pacquiao in a potential November or December fight in the UAE, with Khan's boxing skills and Pacquiao's box office appeal making the bout highly anticipated.

A 5ft wide two-bedroom home in Islington, London, sold for £750,000 despite its narrow dimensions, with a backyard squeezed between a fence and the house. Despite being only 8ft 8in wide at its widest, the home, described as 'well proportioned,' has garnered interest and is now under offer.

Nicola Sturgeon launches an SNP election manifesto with policies overlapping with Labour, including tuition fee reductions, NHS reforms, and cancellation of Trident. The manifesto aims to build a 'progressive alliance' for a potential power-sharing deal with Labour, potentially altering UK politics and constitutional dynamics.

Celtic's U17 team won the Glasgow Cup 2-0 against Rangers, with Josh Kerr scoring the opener and Mark Hill doubling the lead. Robby McCrorie's mistakes, including dropping a free kick and missing a corner, allowed Celtic to secure the victory.

West Bromwich Albion's Tony Pulis led his team to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, maintaining his distinctive style of wearing a cap, track suit, and white trainers throughout matches. Despite Palace's dominance, Pulis's team's resilience secured the win, moving West Brom to 36 points and virtually guaranteeing their Premier League safety.

Jameela Jamil spent £3,000 to replace her amalgam fillings with white ones after experiencing health issues for seven years, including puffy face, exhaustion, and fainting. Dental amalgam, used for fillings, contains mercury, which she believed triggered her symptoms, though experts argue the risk is minimal.

Rap mogul Suge Knight, awaiting trial for murder and attempted murder, was denied bail reduction. His attorney believes Mayweather will bail him out after Mayweather wins his upcoming fight, despite Knight's medical issues and frequent court collapses. Knight's trial is set to begin in July.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine, 35, revealed her feline friend Kimchi prefers human food over cat food, loving poppadoms, tortilla chips, and taramasalata. Erskine, known for her discerning palate, posed with Kimchi in a lavish cat magazine shoot featuring gourmet treats, including caviar and salmon roe.

Martin Springall, the father of a little girl photographed in Japan, found a mysterious black boot in one of his daughter's photos. Despite showing the image to his wife, he has no idea what the boots are or how they appeared. The photo sparked debate on Reddit, with some questioning its authenticity, but Springall insists it was taken candidly with no one else in the vicinity.

Tory plans include banning EU migrants from receiving benefits for four years, forcing them to pay £22,000 in taxes and national insurance before eligibility, and banning 'exporting' child benefit. The move aims to curb net migration to the UK, which hit 298,000 in the year ending September, from poorer EU countries.

Eight-year-old Cody Neatis, with Down's syndrome and other disabilities, has been sleeping on the floor in a hospital ward for seven nights due to a lack of a suitable high-sided bed. His mother, Lynne Neatis, 48, has slept with him on the mattress, fearing he might injure himself or pull out his oxygen tube. Cody has been in hospital since last Thursday with a chest infection, and his mother is demanding answers from the local health trust, noting this issue has persisted for years.

Sportsmail's Derek Lawrenson will cover the Masters, featuring Rory McIlroy's potential career grand slam, Ian Poulter forgetting his clubs, Henrik Stenson's flu, Tiger Woods' children playing, Gene Sarazen's albatross, and the par-three 16th hole's tradition.

Juventus has ruled out signing Manchester United's loan striker Radamel Falcao due to his high wages, but they are interested in Palermo's Paulo Dybala and PSG's Edinson Cavani. Falcao's wages are deemed 'beyond their means' by Juventus, who are also eyeing Dybala and Cavani for their forward line.

David Cameron plans to sell £4 billion worth of Lloyds Bank shares at a discount to the public if re-elected, offering up to £10,000 worth to individuals. This would be the largest privatization since the Thatcher era, with a loyalty bonus for long-term shareholders and a discount on the market rate.

Scientists warn that living near congested roads with high air pollution levels can lead to 'silent strokes,' causing brain damage and increasing dementia risk. Exposure to fine particulate matter, mainly from traffic and factories, alters brain structure and contributes to 29,000 deaths annually in Britain. Researchers found that higher PM2.5 levels are linked to a 46% higher risk of silent strokes in dementia-free individuals.

Jessica Ainscough, a 'wellness warrior' battling a rare cancer, died in February after choosing unconventional treatments. Her fiancé, Tallon Pamenter, revealed she began targeted radiation in her final weeks, integrating it with her natural healing regime. Despite complications, the treatment helped shrink her tumor, but Ainscough passed away, leaving Pamenter heartbroken and reflecting on her courage and grace.

A multi-vehicle crash on Brisbane's west side involved ten people, including four children, resulting in three patients being airlifted to hospital. Six others were taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries, while a man had hand lacerations and two females escaped unharmed. The highway was closed temporarily, with diversions in place south of Fernvale. Emergency crews used hydraulic cutting gear to free a trapped individual.

34-year-old Jason McDonald, a volunteer at the Colorado Gator Farm, walked a thin slackline over a pool containing over 50 alligators, some up to ten feet long. He described the experience as an interesting way to interact with the creatures, noting they were initially curious but eventually comfortable with the setup. McDonald, who has been handling alligators for over a decade, plans to expand his daring hobby, including walking over larger gators and albino specimens.

Abdul Hadi Arwani, a Syrian imam and Muslim Brotherhood member, was killed in London. Days before his death, he visited the area with his son, meeting a potential client who later became the suspected killer. The client asked Arwani to return another day, suggesting he might have been hired to kill the imam.

Hong Kong's Tsim Sha Tsui district sees a rush of tourists and locals buying Jenny's butter cookies at $9 each, leading to knockoffs and a black market. The original shop warns against buying 'fake' cookies, while vendors hire people to stand in line and resell them at a markup. This cookie craze, seen in other global food trends, highlights the allure and fleeting nature of food mania.

Kira Hollis, diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and depression, turned to bodybuilding to gain weight and overcome her struggles. Initially ordered to the gym by doctors, she found it transformed her life, giving her focus and purpose. Her daughter Olivia and boyfriend Michael Dennis supported her recovery, and her story gained widespread attention online.

18-year-old jockey Lewis Ferguson survived a spectacular fall from favorite Merrion Square at Wincanton, sustaining only a cut on his nose. Despite the incident, he returned to riding and is undeterred, attributing his survival to luck and the somersault being a "double." Ferguson, who has fallen a few times before, plans to continue racing and aims to compete in prestigious events like the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree.
