Hillary Clinton's campaign launch featured a video, new logo, and road trip aimed at rebranding and reframing her image. Critics dismissed her efforts, but her campaign may have successfully shifted from a self-absorbed "I" to an empathetic "we," appealing to voters' emotions and perceptions.

Over 1,700 Chinese high school freshmen took their first exam in a school playground in Yichuan, Shaanxi, due to lack of indoor space. The students organized the outdoor exam themselves, rotating their desks to avoid sun glare, and believe it helps broaden horizons and prevent cheating. The event was seen as a test of their organizing skills.

Sportsmail and Gillette are offering a prize pack including Joe Hart's signed Nike Magista Obra boots, a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor, and shaving gel to one lucky reader, closing the competition on April 19th. Hart is a goalkeeper for Manchester City and England.

Kecil, a one-year-old baby orangutan, was rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate mother before finding a loving home with Maggie, a 53-year-old orangutan at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. After 10 months of care, Kecil and Maggie have formed an inseparable bond, and Kecil will make his public debut this weekend following a successful integration into their new enclosure.

Noelle Baynham, 61, from Winchester, Hampshire, died from an accidental overdose of medication. Her pet dogs, a Jack Russell and Staffordshire Bull Terrier, discovered her body partially eaten after she had been locked in her house for days. The cause of death could not be determined due to the dogs consuming her vital organs.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic faces fraud charges for suspected match-fixing in a 2012 loss to Cesson-Rennes. He and 15 others were banned by the French league for betting on the match. Karabatic's lawyer plans to fight the charges, with a trial expected soon.

Six men were jailed for a total of 31 years for sexually abusing teenage girls, including luring them to under-18 parties and engaging in acts ranging from inciting sexual activity to rape. The victims, aged 13-16, were emotionally immature and lacked maturity, with one describing the parties as a place for young girls to be targeted by older boys. The case highlights the importance of victims' bravery in bringing perpetrators to justice.

Former New England Patriots player Aaron Hernandez faces multiple trials including murder charges for the deaths of Daniel de Abreu and Safiro Furtado in 2012. He also faces two civil lawsuits and an NFL grievance over unpaid bonus money, necessitating continued legal representation.

The Emirates Airline is set to rebrand the FA Cup as the Emirates FA Cup in a £30 million, three-year deal. This deal adds to Emirates' existing sports portfolio, which includes sponsorship agreements with Arsenal, AC Milan, and Hamburg, among others.

Michael Phelps, 18-time Olympic champion, aims to compete in his fifth Olympics in Rio next year but will miss the world championships due to a six-month suspension for a second DUI arrest. Phelps, who had already qualified for the world meet, is back in Arizona after rehab and alcohol treatment, expressing a desire to focus on Rio and not be a distraction for the US team.

Gareth Bale is a huge doubt for Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury, while Luka Modric is out for six weeks with a knee ligament strain. Real Madrid also have a goalless draw in the first leg against Atletico.

Scientists warn that older people are more susceptible to emotional decision-making in retirement investments, leading to poor outcomes during the 2007-08 financial crisis. Research shows that those who panicked and sold investments at the market's lowest point would have less than half the value today, while those who held onto their investments would have nearly twice as much. This comes as Britain is implementing reforms allowing retirees to access their pensions, potentially increasing emotional investment decisions.

Stuart Pearce supports Manuel Pellegrini at Manchester City, believing he deserves more time to turn the club around. City's poor form, including a defeat to Manchester United, has led to speculation about Pellegrini's future, but Pearce argues the manager should stay. Pearce attributes City's struggles to the fading influence of Yaya Toure, who has had a largely ineffective season.

Manchester United's stars, including Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera, and Robin van Persie, trained in sunny conditions ahead of their Premier League derby against Manchester City. Manager Louis van Gaal oversaw the final preparations, with United aiming to end City's recent 3-0 run at Old Trafford and move four points clear in the table.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona at home, with a late goal from substitute Mounir Obbadi securing the win. This defeat leaves Fiorentina nine points behind third-placed AS Roma and in sixth place, with their Europa League hopes dashed. The loss also means Fiorentina will face Dynamo Kiev in the Europa League quarter-finals.

Miley Cyrus, attending the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony, displayed visible armpit hair on social media, sparking debate about body hair visibility. While some users criticized her lack of shaving, others defended her choice, noting that men's armpit hair is generally accepted.

Barcelona's Messi, Neymar, and Suarez scored a combined 102 goals this season, surpassing the century mark in La Liga after a 6-0 win over Getafe. Messi leads with 49 goals, Neymar with 32, and Suarez with 21, all crucial inside the box. This achievement puts immense pressure on Real Madrid, who face Almería the following day.

44-year-old Andrea McVeigh was severely injured when hit by a cyclist riding on the pavement, sustaining two three-inch gashes to her forehead and other facial injuries. The cyclist fled the scene, prompting McVeigh's husband to chase him. Police are now seeking an arrest after issuing CCTV footage and appealing for public assistance to identify the suspect.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 and ordered to do 150 hours of unpaid work after admitting to fraudulently obtaining a blue badge by claiming he could only walk 200 meters, despite being a keen walker and mountaineering club member. He was exposed when officials discovered he had participated in a 191-mile hike and was attacked by cows during the trip, which was reported in a newspaper.

Apple has patented a facial recognition system for unlocking devices where the front-facing camera scans a user's face when the phone is moved into a specific position, automatically unlocking the device if the face matches a stored image. This feature, similar to Android's Trusted Face, aims to simplify unlocking without requiring the screen to be enabled.

Elizabeth Sedway, a cancer patient, was forcibly removed from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California due to lack of a doctor's note. Her family was also denied boarding after she expressed needing extra time to board due to her condition. The incident sparked outrage, with the family's emotional video going viral, highlighting the airline's treatment of the passenger.

Three people, including the owner of a $120,000 1973 E-Type Jaguar, were taken to hospital after a head-on collision with a Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The crash occurred at a traffic light intersection, with the classic car completely destroyed. Despite no injuries, the incident highlights the importance of road safety, as police warned of potential consequences for reckless driving during the Easter long weekend.

Google has established a team to enhance battery technology for phones, tablets, and electric cars, focusing on flexible and wearable designs. The team, led by former Apple expert Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj, works on solid-state, thin-film batteries and those that can function in extreme temperatures. Google also collaborates with AllCell Technologies on subfreezing temperature batteries for Project Loon.

The 223ft Explorer superyacht, designed by Tony Castro, features a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests, including car and jet ski storage. It costs approximately 40 million euros to build and is intended for ultra-wealthy individuals, offering amenities like a cinema, sauna, and wine cellar.

Labour leader Ed Miliband plans to impose rent controls despite warnings from experts, who argue it will discourage investment and lead to more evictions. Critics, including senior Tories and the Confederation of British Industry, say the plan will suppress house building and push up rents, while Labour supporters argue it will benefit 'forgotten' renters.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter, Ryan Dearnley, was removed from his role as a Reading mascot for the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal due to a video showing him wishing Arsenal would win. This decision came after Reading fans were outraged by his comments, with 85% of readers in a poll feeling he should not lead the team. The FA moved him to an England mascot role instead.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may explain the mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, a region 20% less dense than surrounding space. If confirmed, this would be the largest structure ever discovered by humanity, potentially caused by a void within a void that saps light energy, leading to a colder temperature.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn will display Abraham Lincoln's shot-in chair at Ford's Theatre on April 15 for the 150th anniversary of his assassination, following a sold-out lecture by historian Doris Kearns Goodwin. The chair, now on display for 85 years, has a dark stain believed to be blood but is actually oil from previous occupants. It was moved from the theater to the museum by Henry Ford, who also acquired Lincoln's law office courthouse nearby.

Jake Boys, a 19-year-old vlogger from Hailsham, booked flights to Dublin instead of Cardiff for a One Direction concert, mistaking the Welsh capital for the Republic of Ireland. His girlfriend Emily-Victoria Canham, a model, was surprised and dismayed by the error, leading to a humorous situation where the couple now plans to take a train to the correct venue.

Romanian company MB Telecom has developed the Roboscan 2M Aeria, a mobile X-ray scanner that can detect contraband, bombs, and weapons inside planes. While currently not safe for passengers, it can scan entire aircraft, including small private jets and medium-sized commercial planes, and is being used to check trucks at borders. The device aims to address gaps in aviation security at low-security airports.

Stephen Munden, a 54-year-old convicted paedophile with an obsession for young girls, has gone on the run after disappearing from a psychiatric unit. Last seen leaving a hospital near Hook, Hampshire, Munden was previously detained under the Mental Health Act for sexually touching a three-year-old girl. He is described as about 5ft 8ins tall, heavy-set, and may have shaved his beard. Officers are searching for him, believing he may have shaved off his beard before leaving.

Middlesbrough lead the Championship with four weeks to go, seven points ahead of second-placed Bournemouth. Their early lunchtime kick-off against Watford could give them a psychological edge, while Watford and Norwich face crucial matches. The promotion race is tight, with teams like Derby struggling without victory in seven games.

The trend of grey hair is gaining popularity, with women posting images on social media using the hashtag #grannyhair. This trend, embraced by both professionals and amateurs, is seen as a feminist statement or quirky fashion, offering an alternative to costly hair dyeing. Influenced by designer Jean Paul Gaultier's use of grey-haired models, the trend has gained traction, with celebrities like Rihanna, Lady Gaga, and Nicole Richie also adopting the look.

Randy and Jodi Speidel, struggling with chronic conditions and living without utilities, created online fundraisers but received no donations. They were found dead from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning from charcoal grills in their bedroom, two months after their pleas for help went unheeded. Their daughters, now orphaned, described their parents as "the hardest-working people" they knew.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to remain leader despite potential losses, emphasizing his optimism for the party's future. He stressed the need to prevent the Labour and Conservative parties from moving too far to the center, warning of economic risks. Clegg also hinted at a possible coalition with the Conservatives, though he acknowledged enduring criticism from the Labour Party.

A 79-year-old pensioner Terry Cooper was saved from a badger attack by his Jack Russell dog Sam, which dragged him indoors. The badger, unusually large and aggressive, was spotted in Cooper's garden, and the National Farmers' Union now advises residents on badger-proofing their properties.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto at their training ground while Real Madrid advanced to the Champions League semi-finals. Mourinho avoided the Madrid derby to watch his former club, Chelsea, face Fulham in a U21 Premier League International Cup match, where Fulham lost 3-0. Mourinho joked with Fulham's coach and his son was also present. Chelsea are closing in on their first Premier League title since 2010.

Andreas Christopheros, 29, was critically injured when corrosive liquid was thrown at him outside his home in Truro, Cornwall. He lost vision and facial scars. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, has been charged with perverting the course of justice, while her husband David Phillips, 48, was charged with grievous bodily harm with intent. Christopheros, a property developer, faces trial on June 8.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route is warning visitors against defecating along the famous path. Graphic signs with a squatting figure defecating in a red circle have been posted by Lastres residents, causing controversy as pilgrims often lack proper facilities. The signs, meant to discourage littering, have become an unexpected attraction for some pilgrims, who pose for photos with them.

A massive fire engulfed a building formerly housing a Flint, Michigan strip club on Wednesday afternoon, starting around 1pm. Only the building and a few nearby power lines were affected, according to local media. The site was not vacant, and a fire had occurred there before. An investigation into the cause of the blaze continues.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent, reached a $40,000 settlement after being strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport on 9/11 anniversary, where she was detained for hours. The incident occurred during a Frontier Airlines flight, involving armed TSA agents and two Indian-American men, leading to a federal lawsuit. The settlement aims to prevent future discrimination and improve airport protocols.

Twenty people were injured after an Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 made a crash landing and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, believed to have missed the landing point on the runway and spun 180 degrees after impact. The Airbus A320 had departed from Seoul, South Korea, and emergency services were at the scene, with injured passengers taken to hospital. The airport was closed as a result.

Made In Chelsea star Mark-Francis Vandelli, a wealthy Londoner, has a watch collection worth several thousand pounds. He buys a new watch each year, including a £32,000 Cartier Moonphase and a £6,500 Bulgari Chrono 42, showcasing his extensive collection. His most prized watch is a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, no longer produced, which he wears to avoid matching with other men.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is auctioning over 200 antiques, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt and a longbow, in a £100,000 sale after downsizing his home. The items, valued from £4,000 to £2,000, reflect Hardy's interest in military history and classic literature, with many dating back centuries.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook criticizing two women hugging on a train platform, sparking outrage. His post, cleverly mocking conservative views, went viral, highlighting public safety regulations and homophobia. Felippe's witty commentary exposed homophobia while subtly correcting a safety violation.

A 16-year-old English cricket fan named Jonathan Stevenson received a 1996 letter from Australian cricket legend Richie Benaud, offering detailed advice on left-handed leg spin bowling. Stevenson shared Benaud's response on Twitter as a tribute after Benaud's death, including a full sheet of notes on spin bowling techniques.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts virtual reality will revolutionize travel, allowing users to experience world's best locales from home via VR headsets. Zuckerberg envisions sharing 3D scenes and environments, similar to how photos and videos are currently shared. Facebook plans to support VR on its newsfeed, enabling users to explore locations virtually, with plans for more immersive experiences including those using Oculus Rift.

A bedridden 22-year-old girlfriend, diagnosed with bone cancer, had her birthday wish of wedding photos fulfilled by her loving boyfriend. Despite her condition, Dong Hui posed for photos in a beautiful wedding dress, with her husband-to-be, Guo Kai, arranging for professional photographers to come to the hospital. The couple, who met a year ago, exchanged rings and vows, making the special day full of happiness and meaning for both.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, under the influence, caused three separate DUI crashes in Houston, killing 6-year-old Joshua Medrano and a homeless man, Leonard Batiste, and injuring his mother. Boudreaux, with a history of DUIs, was charged with multiple offenses including intoxication manslaughter and failure to stop and render aid.

Microsoft launches a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time IT positions at its Redmond campus in Washington, partnering with Specialisterne, a nonprofit that trains autistic individuals for IT careers. This follows Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's apology for comments suggesting women should trust the system for raises, highlighting the company's focus on diversity.

Two deputies in Tulsa, Oklahoma, involved in the fatal arrest attempt of Eric Harris were reassigned due to threats against them. They were criticized for pinning Harris to the ground and were not charged but faced public criticism. Bates, 73, shot Harris accidentally with a handgun during a foot chase, leading to a manslaughter charge. The sheriff's office suspended drug unit operations and is reviewing the shooting amid allegations of training issues and bias.

Katie Prager, 24, diagnosed with cystic fibrosis and Burkholderia cepacia infection, needs a lung transplant but Kentucky Medicaid will not cover the $1 million out-of-state treatment at University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Her husband Dalton, who received a transplant, is desperate as Katie's health declines, facing a 60-day hospital stay before Medicaid coverage can resume. Dalton appeals for help to save Katie's life, fearing she may not survive without a transplant.

New data from Sleep Cycle app users reveals South Africans wake up earliest on Mondays at 6:09 am, while Americans wake up at 7 am on Tuesdays, the worst mood day of the week. Slovakia has the best sleep quality, with 58% of countries reporting their best sleep on Wednesdays, including the US. Americans sleep the latest on Fridays at 8:24 am, but report the best wake-up mood.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo wrote passionate love letters to Jose Bartoli, a Catalan artist, during her marriage to Diego Rivera. These 25 unpublished letters, written between 1946 and 1949, are expected to fetch up to $120,000 at auction, revealing details about her relationship with Diego and her feelings for Jose.

Trade union leader Len McCluskey, popular with activists, tours Wales to support Labour. However, his union's influence extends beyond popularity, wielding significant financial and organizational power within the Labour movement, potentially dragging Britain back to 1970s-style socialism. McCluskey advocates for increased public sector expansion, higher taxes, and more state spending, policies that critics view as disastrous for governance.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz filmed 30 hours of animals drinking water using a GoPro camera placed in their troughs at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv. The footage, culled down to four minutes, showcased unique drinking methods from a rhino almost kissing the water to a lemur delicately licking it, highlighting differences between carnivores and herbivores. Initially sceptical, animals eventually adapted to the camera's presence, with lions aggressively drinking and zebras humorously sipping.

A poll shows only 25% of voters think David Cameron is the hungriest to win the election, while 43% believe Ed Miliband is most up for the fight. Despite Cameron's efforts to appear passionate, he faces criticism for a dull campaign, with Miliband seen as more enthusiastic, and Ukip's Farage as the second most energized leader.

Zaur Dadaev, accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov, confessed to the murder but later retracted his confession, claiming he was beaten and pressured into confessing. Dadaev is one of five Chechen men accused of the crime, which occurred in February when Nemstov was shot four times near the Kremlin. Human rights activists and a judge have raised concerns about potential torture, while the state-funded network Russia Today disputes these claims.

A 4-month-old baby named Sonit Awal was pulled from rubble after a 7.8 magnitude earthquake in Nepal, killing over 5,000 people. Found alive after 22 hours buried under debris, Sonit was uninjured and taken to hospital; his rescue offers hope amidst the country's devastation.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narconon, is attempting to have a 40-acre property near Camp David in Maryland designated as historic to circumvent zoning laws and build a drug rehab center. The property, previously bought by a Scientology-affiliated real estate company, is currently zoned for resource conservation and cannot be used for medical purposes. Narconon claims the site has historical significance due to President Herbert Hoover's visit, while opponents argue it is a tactic to avoid legal restrictions and promote potentially dangerous treatments.

Kabul's population has swelled fivefold since NATO's arrival, but the city now faces economic hardship as English-speaking former contractors are blacklisted and jobless, sleeping in market stalls or avoiding family visits. Violence in provinces drives people to Kabul, turning once expensive foreign neighborhoods into empty streets.

One US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured in a pool accident at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia on Friday. The SEALs, part of Naval Special Warfare Group Two, were swimming laps without gear when the incident occurred. Both were from Naval Special Warfare Group Two, and were later taken to a civilian hospital where one died and the other was in critical condition.

NBC, holding live Premier League rights in the USA, expects US viewership to surpass British viewership in one season. NBC has more than doubled US interest in the Premier League in two years, with 32 million Americans watching last season. For the first time, NBC moved its entire production to England, including star anchor Rebecca Lowe at Turf Moor for Burnley vs Arsenal, alongside Robbie Earle and Kyle Martino. Lowe aims to enhance coverage and influence football choices among young Americans.

Boris Johnson, appearing on Andrew Marr Show, attacked Ed Miliband, accusing him of potentially betraying the country by forming a deal with SNP. Johnson claimed Labour could not govern without SNP support, likening Miliband to a "monkey" on their back, while Miliband dismissed the attack, joking it was "better than that."

A prisoner in Oregon, Dustin Irons, flashed a judge during a video court hearing despite being handcuffed, leading to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court. The incident occurred at Umatilla County Jail, where Irons, already serving time for assault, was known as a difficult inmate.

McLaren improved their pace significantly after starting the season poorly in Australia. In Malaysia, Jenson Button and Fernando Alonso showed the car was competitive with midfield teams, though they retired. Button hopes further progress will be made ahead of the Chinese Grand Prix, noting the team is now racing with Force Indias, Saubers, and Lotuses.

A hospital in Western Australia's Fiona Stanley Hospital, valued at $2 billion, was found to have blood and bone fragments on sanitised medical instruments. The hospital lost its medical service provider Serco after failing to return sterilising equipment by February, fined $60,000, and now faces ongoing issues with improperly sanitized instruments, damaging its public image and workforce morale.
Becca Litchfield and Dale, 29 and 30, from Nottingham, chose to forgo their dream wedding to fund IVF, winning a competition and conceiving twins Darci-Mai and Stanley after two failed IVF attempts.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography for nearly 24 hours starting at 5pm on Sunday. An employee clicked on a malicious link in an email, allowing hackers to take control and post inappropriate content, including adult cartoons, similar to what happened to Crayola and Delta Air Lines. Scooter's Coffee issued an apology and Facebook removed the content after hundreds of reports and contacting larger businesses.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center barked and squeaked after meeting a husky, causing amusement among onlookers who filmed the puppies conversing with each other, including high-pitched whines and yaps. The video shows the puppies' vocalization developing from grunts and whines at two-to-three weeks to stronger barks by seven-to-eight weeks, with some taking longer to vocalize.

Liam Plunkett, an England seamer, is preparing to bowl at the West Indies in the Caribbean. After recovering from an ankle injury, he aims to use his pace to dominate the West Indies batting line-up, competing with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood for a spot in the England Test side. Plunkett is eager to prove his worth in the upcoming series.

Paul Smith, a Liverpool boxer, faces a third challenge against reigning world super-middleweight champion Andre Ward, who sees Smith as a suitable warm-up opponent before potentially facing Carl Froch. The bout will be in Oakland, California, and Smith will be the elder of four Liverpool brothers in the ring.

Tyrus Byrd, the city's first black mayor, was sworn in as mayor of Parma, Missouri, but five of six police officers, the city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor resigned after her election. The reasons for their resignations, citing 'safety concerns,' remain unclear, overshadowing Byrd's victory. The small town, with a predominantly white population, has experienced recent break-ins, leading residents to question the necessity of such a large police force.

Yaya Toure, a key player for Manchester City, will not be forced out but is set to become available this summer. Despite City's interest in reshaping their squad, Toure is content at the club and unlikely to leave due to his high wages. Inter Milan is interested, but City is hesitant about the potential pay-cut. Meanwhile, City will not allow Valencia to block a transfer for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study found that over two-thirds of people taking antidepressants do not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. Researchers also noted that antidepressants are often prescribed for conditions like obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, and generalised anxiety disorder, with 38% not meeting these criteria either. The study suggests many antidepressant prescriptions may be unnecessary, as clinical depression is distinct from temporary sadness.

Doris Fuller, mother of mentally ill daughter Natalie, 28, who died by stepping in front of a train in Baltimore. Natalie suffered from bipolar disorder and psychosis, undiagnosed until her 20s, leading to multiple relapses despite medication. Fuller wrote about her daughter's struggles, describing her as the bravest person she knew, despite her condition worsening and ultimately leading to suicide.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest during a British Bulldog game in the school playground, collapsing and losing consciousness for 12 minutes. His heart stopped pumping blood, and despite CPR by teachers, he was revived by paramedics who administered two shocks with a defibrillator, saving his life.

Britain’s most senior female judge, Baroness Hale, advocates for divorce laws that remove blame and bitterness, suggesting couples sort out children and finances before divorce, and introducing a one-year cooling-off period. Current laws require citing adultery or unreasonable behavior, which critics say encourages recriminations. Lady Hale supports a move towards no-fault divorce, though Conservative MPs opposed this 20 years ago, and some still argue it undermines marriage.

Tottenham are considering a £400m stadium with a retractable pitch for an NFL London franchise, potentially sharing it with NFL teams testing game logistics at Wembley. The new stadium could better accommodate NFL squad sizes and allow games to be televised early in the US morning, with Spurs aiming to be ready for the 2018-19 season.

U.S. senators urge FIFA to remove Russia as 2018 World Cup host citing its role in Ukraine crisis and Crimea occupation. They argue allowing Russia to host bolsters Putin's regime and provides economic relief despite sanctions. England is considering a bid for Euro 2028 but unlikely for 2026 World Cup, with FA not bidding while Blatter remains president.

Universal announced "Fifty Shades of Grey" sequel will release on Feb. 10, 2017, with husband of author EL James, Niall Leonard, writing the script. James maintains creative control, but Sam Taylor-Johnson won't direct. Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan are renegotiating contracts for the sequel after its successful debut.

West Brom manager Tony Pulis faces a challenging return to Crystal Palace after seven seasons without a top-half finish in the Premier League. Despite his success at Stoke and Palace, Pulis has never led a team into the top half, with his current West Brom struggling to avoid relegation despite recent wins. His record is marred by his inability to secure a top-five finish, even with better financial resources than some of his predecessors.

Fenerbahçe, following a gun attack on their team bus during a Super Lig match, called for a championship suspension. The bus was attacked as it left a match in Rize, Turkey, injuring the driver. The club demanded justice and a suspension until the perpetrators are found, citing the attack as a violation of public opinion.

A massive snow avalanche hit Everest Base Camp, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens. The quake, which killed over 4,300 in Nepal, triggered the avalanche and left many climbers and local workers trapped at higher camps, complicating rescue efforts due to dangerous aftershocks and blocked icefall routes.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during WWII, fought Nazis and later found himself in another war in Ukraine. After surviving WWII, he settled in Donetsk, Ukraine, but was again caught in conflict. Now 87, he survived a missile attack in his home, leading his family to immigrate to Israel, where they felt safer despite ongoing tension.

John Carver, now fighting for Newcastle's head coaching position, recalls the 1999 Tyne-Wear derby where former manager Ruud Gullit's controversial selection of Duncan Ferguson and Alan Shearer left Newcastle 2-1 losers and Gullit out of a job. Carver knows a derby win could bolster his chances, as fans value such victories greatly.

Revered Al Sharpton attended a vigil in North Charleston for Walter Scott, a black man fatally shot by a white police officer. Sharpton preached at Charity Missionary Baptist Church, addressing the Scott case and police reform, alongside elected officials and police. He praised Mayor Keith Summey for firing the officer and called for a new tone in policing across the US.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the winger's controversial behavior, including video of him inhaling nitrous oxide and smoking a shisha pipe, led to a club investigation. Sterling scored the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United, but Rodgers emphasized the need to discuss his off-field behavior with the 20-year-old, who faces potential disciplinary action.

Labour received over £1.1 million in union donations during the final week of the election campaign, more than twice as much as the Conservatives, who received £492,512. Unions like Unison, Unite, and USDAW contributed significantly, with most donations coming from Ed Miliband's Labour party, while the Conservatives received most of their funds from wealthy individuals.

Police were called twice to a Qatar Airways flight diverted to Birmingham due to severe winds, where passengers became disruptive after being stranded for five hours. The incident caused a knock-on delay at Manchester, leading to further police intervention and complaints about inadequate passenger care and transport.

Canadian pop star Justin Bieber will accompany boxing champion Floyd Mayweather into the ring for his $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao in Las Vegas. The 21-year-old has been Mayweather's entourage member for years, joining him on stage and in the ring. Bieber's participation was initially reported as just accompanying Mayweather, but now he will lead the American's entourage, with the singer and Mayweather getting along well.

Corinthian Colleges, once a major for-profit college with over 70,000 students, announced its closure after being cut off from federal student aid. This move, part of a larger struggle to hold for-profit colleges accountable, affects about 1.3 million students, many of whom default on their loans, totaling nearly half of all defaults. Corinthian's aggressive recruitment tactics and reliance on federal student aid have led to widespread criticism, with some graduates joining a debt strike, and the Education Department considering loan forgiveness for affected students.

Bayern Munich boss Pep Guardiola denied a dispute with former doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt who quit the club after the Champions League quarter-final defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the medical staff was blamed for the loss, citing a damaged bond of trust. Guardiola blamed himself for the defeat, attributing it to injuries and a lack of available players, despite Muller-Wohlfahrt's resignation.

Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, 39, will defend his world titles against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden in New York. After winning Olympic gold in 1996, Klitschko became a hero overnight, and he reflects on how sport can change lives, including his own. Despite being 15 years into his career, Klitschko remains dominant, believing age is an advantage.

Jeremy Clarkson, fired from Top Gear after assaulting a producer, expressed his 'heartfelt thanks' for support but admitted missing the show. Former presenter Angela Rippon, 70, said she would like to return, while Lord Hall stated the BBC won't renew Clarkson's contract. The future of Top Gear remains uncertain, with suggestions for new presenters including a woman and a male presenter with 'safe hands'.

In a La Liga match between Barcelona and Celta Vigo, Celta striker Fabian Orellana was shown a red card and struck by a lump of grass thrown at him by Sergio Busquets during a heated final minute. Orellana's aggressive action led to a red card, while Busquets capitalized on the incident. The match ended 1-0 in favor of Barcelona, securing crucial points despite Real Madrid's 9-1 victory earlier.

In 2013, a pair of bombs exploded at the Boston Marathon finish line, killing 3 and injuring over 200. In 2018, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was convicted for the bombings. A federal judge warned a jury to avoid the Boston Marathon and related events during sentencing, which begins April 21.

Millions of Chinese marked the Qingming Festival by returning to ancestral villages to clean graves, honor the dead, and celebrate the start of spring. In Shaanxi, a grand ceremony was held in honor of Yellow Emperor Huangdi, featuring outdoor parades, traditional dances, and performances. The festival, celebrated for its 24 solar terms, includes rituals like burning fake money and offering food to ancestors, symbolizing the belief that the deceased need sustenance in the afterlife.

Paul Simon, 73, returns to the UK album chart top spot with "The Ultimate Collection," his first since 1990, outselling more contemporary artists like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. His recent tour with Sting is believed to have boosted the album's success, marking a comeback for the Grammy-winning singer.

Iker Casillas, Real Madrid's long-time goalkeeper, insists he will stay at the club until his contract ends, despite David de Gea's potential move from Manchester United. Casillas, 33, claims he will fight for the starting position and help Real Madrid defend their Champions League title, emphasizing his commitment to the team.

Britain saw its highest employment level in history, with 557,000 more people in work in the last year. This was praised by the International Monetary Fund and Chancellor George Osborne, who claimed the Conservatives had overseen a 'jobs miracle'. The UK's fiscal deficit was significantly reduced, and the economy is on course for strong growth, despite warnings from Osborne about Greece's potential impact on Britain's economy.

Korea's SsangYong is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli, starting at £12,950, offering value for money with European styling and features like seven airbags and a choice of engines. The SUV aims to compete with the Nissan Juke and is expected to boost SsangYong's UK sales, with the top model priced up to £19,000. Meanwhile, Citroen's Aircross, inspired by tough Tonka toys, features protective alloy bumps and is positioned as a larger version of the C4 Cactus.

Chef Sam Longhurst created a 10-inch tall, half-kilogram burger at Splendid Kitchen in Manchester, containing six forms of three different meats totaling 2,000 calories. The 'Whole Damn Farm' burger includes two beef patties, ham, bacon, chicken, pulled pork, and bacon rashers, described as a 'monster of a burger' by the chef.

Yeo Valley's Michelin-starred staff canteen offers high-quality, organic, locally sourced meals for as little as £2, including dishes like soft-poached quail egg and confit of tomato. The canteen, overlooking Blagdon countryside, serves 120 dairy workers and is now open to the public at higher prices, featuring daily menu changes with produce from nearby farms.

Legendary blues musician B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration due to Type II diabetes, but he recovered quickly and was back home with his family, thanking fans for their well-wishes. King, 89, has a history of health issues, including a canceled tour in 2022 after a similar incident.

Manhattan's Fifth Avenue hosted an Easter parade with bizarre hats, featuring everything from simple bunny ears to elaborate dioramas. The event included various religious groups, secular participants, and even puppet rabbits. Local hatmaker Mary Ann Smith created a ship-shaped bonnet, while others wore floral arrangements and industrial goggles.

Emergency crews in Essex dispatched two ambulances to Epping Forest after a caller reported a person run over by a car, only to discover the "victim" was a squirrel. The East of England ambulance service has released a list of 1,248 inappropriate calls, including a man who dropped a burger that "bleeded," a woman who claimed to be locked out, and a man who said his feet hurt from small shoes. Crews attended nearly half of these non-emergency calls, potentially delaying real emergencies.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake won an Audi-sponsored football challenge, defeating team-mates Loic Remy and Willian. In the final round, Willian accidentally smashed the wing mirror of an Audi with a long-range shot, causing damage. Hazard and Ake secured a 6-0 win, while Remy and Willian narrowly lost but redeemed themselves by causing a mishap.

Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, for allegedly manipulating the player. Sterling, who has two years left on his Liverpool contract, rejected a £100,000 a week extension and is facing Arsenal's interest. Rodgers believes Sterling enjoys playing for Liverpool and would be better off staying, despite outside influences.

Countdown host Nick Hewer struggled to keep laughing when contestants offered the eight-letter word 'erection' as part of a word game, embarrassing co-presenter Rachel Riley. This incident, along with others, highlights the show's history of unintentionally humorous moments involving rude words, including 'todgers' and 'm*nges'.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Manchester, tried to buy deadly poison online but was found to want to commit suicide. After pleading guilty, he was spared jail and sentenced to a 12-month referral order following an anti-terror operation. Officers tracked his covert communication on the dark web, which he used to express interest in purchasing the toxin.

Lianne Hindle, 37, died three hours after giving birth to her baby girl at North Manchester General Hospital, where three other babies and one mother had died in the previous months. The hospital, along with the Royal Oldham Hospital, faced an investigation after 10 deaths in eight months, prompting calls for action to prevent further tragedies. Hindle's partner Chris Barnes called for improved care, citing concerns about her treatment and lack of monitoring.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after training while eight months pregnant. The 32-year-old, who conceived with an IVF donor, plans to compete in the 2016 Rio Olympics and has been training right up until her final trimester. Her son Cornelis, seven years old, is the big brother to Emily.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats during a regatta in Dauphin Island, Alabama, killing at least one person and leaving four missing. Over 100 boats and 200 people were involved; the storm was so severe that boats were scattered across Mobile Bay.搜救人员在夜间继续搜索失踪者，包括一名男子被救起。

62-year-old comedian Roseanne Barr revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, eye diseases that progressively steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening, affecting both central and peripheral vision. While there is no cure, treatments can delay progression and protect against further vision loss.

A 17-year-old Oklahoma youth, Chancey Allen Luna, was convicted of first-degree murder for shooting and killing Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane during a jog in Duncan, Oklahoma. The jury recommended life in prison without parole, despite Luna firing from a passing car with no apparent motive, and his defense contended it was a reckless act by a 16-year-old.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger insists his 12-5-7 record against Jose Mourinho will not affect their top-of-the-table clash with Chelsea at the Emirates. Despite Wenger's 12 losses, he says the game is about performance, not past history. Wenger and Mourinho have a frosty relationship, but Wenger wants respect for Fabregas, who will play for Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal are 10 points behind Chelsea but aim to win at home.

Manny Pacquiao, born into poverty in the Philippines, rose to global fame through mega-fights including those against Oscar De La Hoya, Ricky Hatton, and Juan Manuel Marquez. He started boxing at 14 in Manila and became a boxing icon, facing Floyd Mayweather in the "Fight of the Century" on the Las Vegas Strip.

Jack Grealish, a top football player, was photographed using nitrous oxide, a legal but banned substance, during Aston Villa's FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool. This incident highlights the need for professional athletes to maintain their health and focus, as Grealish's future success depends on his choices.

Sam Barton, who underwent £55,000 of cosmetic surgery, was attacked with eggs by a group on Easter Monday in Sutton Coldfield, UK. The 22-year-old believes the attackers tracked him down via social media, targeting him for his appearance and celebrity look-alike efforts, including two nose jobs funded by the NHS.

An Indiana university was on lockdown after receiving a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the administration building. Police responded but found it a false alarm, confirming no injuries. The university advised students to shelter in place, with police and bomb squad arriving at the scene.

Luis Suarez and Edinson Cavani, Uruguay's most famous son and a striker known as El Matador, will face off in the Champions League quarter-final at Parc des Princes. PSG, without suspended key players Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Veratti, relies on Cavani to break through Barcelona's defense. Cavani has struggled with a goal drought but could be crucial for PSG's Champions League hopes.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title with a unanimous decision over Tony Luis in Liverpool. Luis was drafted in at the last minute after two fighters pulled out due to illness or visa issues. Mathews dominated early, but Luis showed aggression, resulting in a tight 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 decision in a thrilling fight.

Hull bounced back from a derby loss to defeat St Helens 28-20 at Langtree Park, securing a surprise win that ended St Helens' three-game losing streak. Hull's Jamie Shaul scored the opening try, and the match remained close until Saints' late penalty gave them a brief lead, but Hull's defense and kicking game proved decisive.

The U.S. immigrant population, including documented and undocumented, could reach 51 million by 2023, making up 14.8% of the population. By 2060, immigrants could account for 82% of all population growth, with one in five residents projected to be an immigrant. This growth is driven by net immigration expected to total 64 million over 45 years, with immigrants contributing to nearly 75% of future U.S. population growth.

Arsenal Under 21s lost 1-0 to Reading at the Emirates Stadium, with Jack Wilshere making his return from injury. Former Arsenal defender Martin Keown's son scored the only goal in the opening minutes. Wilshere and other injured first team players like Abou Diaby and Serge Gnabri played, but the game was dominated by Reading's youth team.

English golfer Justin Rose, struggling after a poor Florida swing, improved his form with a 69 at the Shell Houston Open, hitting 17 out of 18 greens. Rose's encouraging performance suggests his decline may be temporary, as he aims to regain his top 10 ranking ahead of the Masters.

A newly-built mansion in Mayfair, London, formerly a milking parlour, has gone on the market for £25 million. Originally a commercial depot, the site now features modern luxuries including a swimming pool, cinema room, and lift, while upstairs is a 14-place dining table and a master suite. The property, 8,139 sq ft, was constructed in 2011 after developers demolished the original structure.

Bayern Munich, without key players like Robben, Ribéry, and Schweinsteiger, showed unity in recent games against Dortmund and Leverkusen. Coach Guardiola expects a strong unit with Muller and Lewandowski to face Porto in the Champions League, despite the injury troubles. Porto, winners in the group stage, pose a physical challenge but also have individual quality.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes team-mates, visited Mercedes' Brackley base after Sebastian Vettel's victory in the Malaysian Grand Prix. They aim to improve their strategy for the upcoming China race. Mercedes was surprised by Vettel's win, attributing it to Ferrari's better tyre management in the hot conditions.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection is deemed unconstitutional or unavailable. The gas causes quick unconsciousness and death from lack of oxygen, though it's never been used in U.S. executions. Fallin supports the death penalty, citing the need for an effective and humane method, following Oklahoma's controversial 43-minute execution of Clayton Lockett.

Swansea's Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in a 3-1 win over Hull, topping this week's EA Sports' Performance Index with a Game Index score of 52.9. Gomis has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games. Charlie Austin of Queens Park Rangers is runner-up with a score of 52.2 after scoring and assisting in a 4-1 win against West Brom.

A Russian freezer trawler carrying 132 crew members sank in the Sea of Okhotsk off the Kamchatka Peninsula, killing at least 56 and injuring many more. The ship, Dalny Vostok, sank in just 15 minutes after a fishing net weighing 80 tons was pulled in, causing it to tip over. A massive rescue operation involving over 1,300 people is underway, with 63 survivors rescued and 13 still missing. Temperatures in the water are extremely low, leading to many deaths.

Men with advanced prostate cancer could benefit from a drug originally used for women. Clinical trials show olaparib, a PARP inhibitor, delays prostate cancer progression in up to 30% of men with DNA repair mutations, extending survival without disease worsening. The drug, already effective for women with BRCA mutations, targets cancer cells' inability to repair DNA damage, offering a new precision treatment option.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, reviews luxurious hotels, documenting experiences on her Instagram and website 'In Bed With'. With over 12,000 followers, she documents the best beds, pools, and room service, earning income from hotels and travel product companies. Taylor has reviewed properties worldwide, from Australia to Indonesia and the US, leveraging her travel photography skills.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was thrown into the air and dragged along the surface of water in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, South Africa, after being caught in a deadly fight between two adult males. The calf's mother, believing it safer to stay with her herd, watched helplessly as the attack occurred, and the baby died hours later.

The Football Association will investigate an incident at a Chelsea vs. QPR match where Branislav Ivanovic was hit by a cigarette lighter thrown by home supporters. QPR is unlikely to face disciplinary action but will review CCTV and ban those involved. Chelsea celebrated a win, but the match was marred by objects thrown onto the pitch, with QPR appealing for witnesses and promising to ban offenders.

LaTasha Gosling, 27, and her three children, Janyaa, 4, Jenika, 8, and Landen, 7, were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect, who was found dead hours later, was known to the family. Police are investigating, and the family is raising funds for funeral services.

Labour politician Emily Thornberry, despite opposing the right to buy policy for council tenants, owns three homes including a £1 million housing association property she bought eight years ago. Critics accuse her of hypocrisy, as she supports the policy for council tenants but not for housing association tenants, highlighting her contradictory stance and high-value property holdings.

Police dropped an investigation into a vicious assault on Mike Lane, 40, a huntsman, three months after it occurred. Despite a video and evidence, including names and car numbers, Wiltshire Police ceased inquiries due to insufficient evidence, leaving Lane and supporters disappointed and questioning the police's commitment to justice.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, insists he wants to stay at the club despite Premier League interest from Manchester United and Chelsea. Gomes, who has scored four times in 25 La Liga appearances since joining from Benfica, says he is happy and convinced he will remain at the Mestalla.

Australian teenager Audrey Pekin, 19, alleges she was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali by Henry Alafu, who lured her to his remote home and then attacked her in a taxi. Alafu escaped after the attacks, and Pekin claims Indonesian police failed to prevent him from returning to Nigeria. She sought help from passersby but was repeatedly followed and molested in a taxi.

Former Made In Chelsea star Ashley James, in a hard-hitting anti-fur campaign, posed with a fake skinned fox at Harvey Nichols, a department store that recently reintroduced fur products. PETA, with James' support, aims to highlight the cruelty of the fur industry through billboards, challenging Harvey Nichols' decision to re-introduce fur.

Chile enacted a new law recognizing civil unions between same-sex couples, joining several South American countries. The change, signed by President Michelle Bachelet, will take effect in six months and aims to end discrimination for common-law couples, giving them rights in property, health care, pensions, and inheritance. Around 2 million Chileans are estimated to benefit.

Chelsea are on track to break the Premier League record for most days at the top of the table in a single season, currently leading for 230 days. They are seven points clear of second-placed rivals with a game in hand, and their next three matches against QPR, Manchester United, and Arsenal could determine their title fate.

Cape Verde, a small island nation with a rich musical heritage, is leveraging its cultural resources to boost its economy. Despite lacking natural resources, the country is focusing on music, batuque, morna, and other styles to attract international artists and promote tourism. The Kriol Jazz Festival, celebrating its 7th edition, has brought global attention, showcasing Cape Verde's potential to use its cultural wealth for economic growth.

An old hoax video of a wave rider surfing in front of Sydney's Opera House has gone viral again, following heavy storms. Initially posted by Sydney radio duo Fitzy and Wippa, the video was quickly shared widely. Skeptics noted inaccuracies like rocks around the Opera House and the man's appearance, while experts argued it's impossible for waves to reach that far inside the harbor.

Reading lost to Birmingham 1-0 in a Sky Bet Championship match at the Madejski Stadium. Despite dominating the first half, Reading failed to capitalize on several chances and conceded a late goal from Clayton Donaldson, who scored his 16th goal of the season.

French champions Paris Saint-Germain face a major injury setback as David Luiz, a key defender, will miss the Champions League match against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained in the first half against Marseille. The Brazilian defender will be out for at least four weeks, potentially impacting PSG's title defense and Champions League campaign.

The return of Game of Thrones has sparked a surge in internet piracy with fans making over 100,000 illegal downloads per day. More than seven million episodes from seasons one to four were illegally downloaded between February and April, up 45% year-on-year. Piracy is highest in Brazil, with the show the most illegally downloaded globally, followed by The Walking Dead, Breaking Bad, and House of Cards. HBO launched a new streaming service to curb piracy and recapture revenue, but piracy remains a global issue.

Leicester City hosts West Ham United at King Power Stadium for a Premier League match. Leicester, fighting for survival, lacks key players Matt Upson and Dean Hammond, while West Ham welcomes back injured defender Winston Reid. The teams have a history of close matches, with West Ham having won 51 and drawn 29 against Leicester in league history.

Residents of Celoron, NY, are outraged at a statue of Lucile Ball, the town's icon, which they find unflattering. Based on a drunken pitch scene from 'I Love Lucy,' the statue has sparked a Facebook page with over 600 likes, calling for its removal. Artist Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has declined to comment, with some locals describing it as "monstrous" and "frightening."

Sharon Smith, a 43-year-old woman from Halesowen, West Midlands, lost nearly half her body weight from 18st 6lb to 9st 9lb after standing for an entire 11-hour flight due to her size, which had been as high as 20st. Her weight loss began when she joined Weight Watchers Online and quit her job to freelance, allowing her to exercise more.

Nicola Bonn, a 34-year-old London mother, started an online blog Upfront Mama to share her experiences raising 14-month-old Poppy. She found it challenging to navigate parenting advice, often feeling judged by others, and decided to stop justifying her decisions, sharing her frustrations and experiences with fellow new mothers.

17-year-olds Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, believed related to a convicted ISIS member, fled Britain to Syria. They reportedly boarded a flight to Turkey during Easter break, leaving families devastated and worried about their safety. Authorities fear the pair may have crossed into Syria, with families urging anyone with information to contact police.

Stephanie Scott, a school teacher, was brutally murdered just days before her wedding to childhood sweetheart Aaron Leeson-Woolley. Her body was found in bushland near her hometown, leaving her grieving family devastated. The couple had planned a wedding with 120 guests, but Stephanie's death left the venue as a memorial site. Her father is struggling with the loss, especially as Stephanie had much to look forward to.

Tonny Vilhena, 20, a Holland U21 international winger, wants to leave Feyenoord this summer. Southampton, led by Ronald Koeman, is interested in signing him and also monitoring midfielder Jordy Clasie. Southampton, currently 7th in the Premier League, is looking to strengthen its squad for potential European qualification.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, sparking controversy among heritage experts. The move aimed to encourage visitors to 'dwell' but was deemed misguided, leading to similar experiments at nine other venues. Art historian Bendor Grosvenor criticized the National Trust for patronizing visitors, suggesting better ways to engage them.

Former Prime Minister John Howard found himself with a flat tyre in Sydney, with his driver assisting. Felicity Waterford, waiting for her daughter at the Sydney Conservatorium, offered help and took a selfie with the former PM, who was initially standing on the footpath. This incident occurred weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television, highlighting contrasting views on public service.

Tony Pulis, West Brom manager, agrees with Joey Barton that his players 's*** themselves' after losing 3-2 to Queens Park Rangers despite being 2-0 up. Barton criticized West Brom's inability to finish games, recalling his own similar experience as a manager. Pulis acknowledges Barton's point but emphasizes West Brom's strong recent performances, hoping to continue them.

A Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought extinct for over 50 years, was discovered alive in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ntokou-Pikounda National Park. Primatologists Lieven Devreese and Gaël Elie Gnondo Gobolo captured the first-ever image of the species, proving it not extinct. Meanwhile, researchers in Tibet found a new white-cheeked macaque species with a distinctive penis shape, officially named Macaca leucogenys.

Kim Kardashian, Kanye West, and daughter North visited Armenia, the country of her father's birth, for eight days. They arrived in Yerevan, the capital, where they explored landmarks like the Yerevan Opera House and the Katoghiken church in Geghard Monastery. The visit included cultural experiences and security, with the family staying at the Armenia Marriott Hotel on Republic Square.

British expats Patrick and Valerie Jubb are trapped in southern Spain's Jimena de la Frontera amid a legal battle with the town hall over a luxury bed and breakfast they operated. They face losing their property due to illegal additions by a previous owner, despite obtaining a certificate stating no infractions when they bought it in 2008. The couple wants to sell the €680,000 estate but is tied up in a four-year-old dispute over its legality, now located in Los Alcornocales Natural Park.

Apple sold over 61 million iPhones in the first quarter, accounting for over two-thirds of its $58 billion revenue and $13.6 billion profit, up 40% from a year ago. Sales in China outpaced the US, with iPhone revenue contributing significantly to Apple's $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit.

A 3-year-old's recurring nightmares about a white van may link to a series of hit-and-run accidents involving a white delivery-style truck in Virginia, which occurred shortly after Natali Castellanos-Tyler's SUV crash that police ruled a tragic accident. The truck was linked to three incidents, including one that injured 17-year-old Caitlyn Thomas, raising doubts about the initial cause of the crash.

Researchers found the brain can better remember neutral events tied to emotion. This study, led by NYU, challenges the assumption that we remember emotionally charged events better. It highlights how emotion affects brain regions involved in memory, particularly the amygdala and hippocampus, and can strengthen memory consolidation over time.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of 18-year-old Jackson Byrnes with a stage four brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 from the community to fund his life-saving surgery by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo. Despite being paralysed and unable to dress himself, Jahnae has put her studies on hold to care for her boyfriend. The surgery, which is likely to save his life, will leave him paralysed for some time.

Nedum Onuoha, QPR's 28-year-old centre-back with 15 months left on contract, is sought by Hull City amid QPR's potential relegation. Onuoha played in the crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion. He is also of interest to Everton, West Ham, and Stoke, where his former manager Mark Hughes is now. Hull is also monitoring West Bromwich Albion striker Victor Anichebe for a potential summer move.

From 'here's you a piece of pizza' to 'this glass needs washed', every state has its own phrases that can seem odd to the rest of the world. Researchers at Yale University documented these patterns, creating an interactive map showing common phrases for each state, revealing significant regional differences in sentence structure.

A Canadian man, Kalman Kallai, traveled 2,796 miles across Canada in a free green rocking chair, taking breaks to watch planes, pose with cows, and even chase birds. He carried the chair on his head and waved at statues, sharing the journey with his father for a bonding experience.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood had fun during a press conference by revealing a Twix multi-pack as a 'win bonus' to six-year-old Charlie Pye, who wrote to the club after Paul Lambert was sacked and applied for the manager's job. Sherwood joked that Pye wanted his mum and dad as assistant managers and a chocolate bar.

World boxing champion Kell Brook watched the Premier League Darts in Sheffield, receiving a hero's welcome. Dave Chisnall, who was second in the Premier League table, won both of his games, including a 7-3 victory over world champion Gary Anderson and a 7-1 win over James Wade. Brook is set to defend his title against Frankie Gavin on May 30.

Italian midfielder Marco Verratti praises Paris Saint-Germain's Zlatan Ibrahimovic, saying the 33-year-old's off-field support is crucial, helping young players and exuding confidence. Despite a suspension for the Champions League match, Ibrahimovic is set to return for the return leg against Barcelona.

The RAF's Mount Pleasant aerodrome on the Falklands Islands had a secret Aerodrome Manual published on the MoD's website, containing GPS coordinates and runway depth info. This could be used by Argentina to plan an invasion, as the manual included vital technical details. The MoD disabled the link but acknowledged the document was available online, despite denying it was sensitive. Argentina is considering leasing Cold War-era SU-24 bombers from Russia, which could pose a threat to Falklands defences.

Huddersfield Giants, currently ninth in Super League, aim to improve their attack to match their strong defense. Coach Paul Anderson hopes to turn their season around after losing all three games since Easter. They face Catalans Dragons, who lead the league in defensive efficiency, in a crucial home game. A win could propel Huddersfield to fourth place, while Vikings coach Denis Betts expects a tough test against Castleford, who have a solid defense but can be competitive offensively.

Coffee lovers in Windsor will soon have two Costa cafes within less than 500 yards, with a third at a petrol station. This decision comes despite one resident's concern about too many fast food and coffee shops, while planners argue it boosts local trade.

The British Veterinary Association withdrew support for shooting free-running badgers in pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, citing lack of conclusive effectiveness and humane outcomes. The BVA still supports culling to control bovine tuberculosis in cattle, but opposes cage-trapping and shooting. The Environment Secretary promised to expand culls if the Tories win, despite criticism and low cull numbers in some areas.

Portishead's Geoff Barrow accuses streaming services of underpaying his band, receiving £1,700 for 34 million plays. He criticizes Universal Music and others for selling music cheaply, arguing it hurts young talent and threatens their ability to tour. Barrow supports Jay-Z's Tidal service, which promises higher artist royalties.

Game of Thrones fans leaked the first four episodes of its fifth season online before the official premiere. The episodes, titled The Wars to Come, The House of Black and White, High Sparrow, and The Sons of the Harpy, were leaked from HBO press review copies and have been downloaded over 550,000 times. The show is the most illegally downloaded program globally, with Brazil and France leading illegal downloads. HBO plans to combat piracy by streaming the premiere simultaneously in 170 countries.

Melbourne singer Daniel Buccheri, best man at his brother's wedding, composed an emotional song to use as his best man's speech, which included tributes to his brother and new wife, and was performed to the tune of "Stay With Me." The speech, which included personal stories and memories, went viral online, viewed over 100,000 times, and left guests in tears.

Zara Phillips, after giving birth to Mia, regained her fitness by exercising on an exercise bike every morning before her daughter wakes up. She now eats a balanced diet and aims to qualify for Team GB in the 2016 Olympics, focusing on eventing, a sport she hopes her daughter Mia will grow up around.

Following Raheem Sterling's interview saying he's not ready to sign a new contract, Liverpool fans are increasingly frustrated. Sterling's comments, while ill-timed, have soured many fans' opinions, potentially leading to his departure. Liverpool fans believe no player is bigger than the club, and Sterling's situation has sparked debate on whether he should be retained or sold.

Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola conversed at Barcelona training in 2015. This led to a photo becoming a 'guess the caption' hit. Recent scans revealed more Barcelona-era coaches from the same team, including Laurent Blanc and Julen Lopetegui, now at PSG and Porto respectively. The 1996-97 Barcelona team, managed by Bobby Robson, featured future managers and players who have since coached various clubs.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona, at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai, named Paris Saint-Germain's Javier Pastore as the best player in the world, praising his creativity and passing skills. Despite Pastore's impressive stats, Cantona's assessment was based on his unique ability to surprise with his play, contrasting with Messi and Ronaldo.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murdering his tenant Michael Spalding, 39, by hacking him to pieces, stuffing the body parts into suitcases, and dumping them in a canal in Smethwick, Birmingham. Simon, with girlfriend Michelle Bird's help, dismembered Spalding and hid the body parts in two suitcases, which were later discovered by police. Simon initially denied involvement but later admitted assaulting Spalding.

Health experts warn that social isolation is as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day, leading to dementia and high blood pressure. Essex and Gloucestershire councils have created 'loneliness maps' to identify areas with the highest risk of social isolation among elderly residents. These maps, based on public health factors and resident surveys, help local councils target support to vulnerable communities.

65-year-old Judy Eddingfield celebrated her 50th anniversary as a server at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she started working at age 15. She has worked there since 1965, serving customers including 'Leave It to Beaver' stars Jerry Mathers and Tony Dow. Eddingfield considers it her only job and says the restaurant is like her home, with her family tradition of service spanning generations.

Former England captain Mike Gatting suggests Kevin Pietersen should not automatically return to the international team, despite scoring runs for Surrey. Gatting believes Pietersen needs to show he's playing well, and other players like Gary Ballance and Ian Bell are performing well, potentially making Pietersen's return uncertain. Gatting also notes Alastair Cook's poor form, with questions likely if he doesn't score runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old Californian student Caleb Benn developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' for iOS, allowing direct photo uploads from computers. This app now faces a potential lawsuit from Instagram, which considers it a violation of its API terms. Benn earns $1,000 daily from the app, despite Instagram's demand for its removal by Monday.

South Korean companies often host weekly hoesik, or drinking dinners, for employees. Intense pressure to participate, especially for foreign workers, is common. Drinking is seen as a way to build relationships and understand colleagues, with traffic patterns in Seoul reflecting the city's drinking culture, particularly heavy traffic on Fridays.

The Duke of Kent, 79, suffered a dislocated hip while visiting Balmoral estate in Aberdeenshire and was hospitalized at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. He was discharged after a night's treatment and now uses a walking stick. The incident comes two years after he had a mild stroke, and he continues to perform royal duties despite his age.

The 50-year-old Surfers Paradise Meter Maids, introduced to combat parking meter bad publicity, are facing criticism from local business leaders who say they are outdated and irrelevant due to electronic meters. The Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president calls for their end, citing violations of anti-touting laws and lack of service, while the Meter Maids defend their role as a beloved part of the Gold Coast experience.

Greece denies it will miss a £330 million IMF loan repayment on April 9, despite reports of plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas confirms the payment will be made, while sources claim the government prioritizes domestic payments over loans. Germany's Der Spiegel quotes a finance ministry official as saying Greece may not pay, causing market concerns and potential eurozone exit risks. Greek officials deny these claims, emphasizing their commitment to timely payments and reforms.

Turkey blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing requests to remove images of prosecutor Mehmet Selim Kiraz, held hostage and later killed during an armed siege. The images, shared on social media, upset the hostage's wife and children, leading to the blocks by a Turkish court, despite attempts to prevent newspaper publication of the images.

Seven-year-old Colin Gilpatric, an aspiring Jedi, wrote to George Lucas asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucas allowed it, sending Colin a letter and Star Wars merchandise. Colin's request was based on the fear that forming attachments would lead to the 'dark side' as seen in Anakin Skywalker's story.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky 71-64 in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's 38-1 unbeaten streak and sending the Wildcats to the Final Four. Wisconsin's Frank Kaminsky was key with 20 points and 11 rebounds, securing a tense victory that advances them to play Duke in the final.

Vince Neil of Mötley Crüe famously botched the national anthem before a football game, drawing comparisons to past performances by Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton, showcasing the wide range of interpretations and reactions to singing "The Star-Spangled Banner."

CCTV footage shows Irishman Barry Lyttle punching his younger brother Patrick, causing him to fall and suffer a head injury in Sydney. Patrick was treated at the scene and later charged with grievous bodily harm. Barry pleaded guilty, and a court hearing is set to determine if Barry will serve prison time for his violent act.

Conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, born with disrosopus, died 19 days after birth. Their family set up a shrine at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney's west, leaving mementos weekly. Upon visiting their gravesite, parents found it cleared of all memorabilia, including their pink coffin and flowers, by cemetery staff. They were told it was routine cleaning, but found only 25% of their belongings in nearby bins.

Britain's Supreme Court President Lord Neuberger suggests judges should allow Muslim women to wear full-face veils in court to show respect for different customs. This follows a 2003 trial where a Muslim woman was sentenced for refusing to remove her veil, highlighting ongoing uncertainty about traditional dress in the legal system. Lord Neuberger calls for judges to be sensitive to cultural differences and the intimidating nature of courts, urging them to create a more welcoming environment for all.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri for killing Anthony Curtis in a fit of rage over child support 16 years ago. Cole became the third convicted killer put to death in Missouri this year, despite appeals claiming he was mentally ill and unfit for execution.

Prince Harry will fly to Australia without meeting his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is overdue for the birth of their second child. With Kate expected by mid to late April, Harry, now fifth in line to the throne, will return to Australia for a month-long placement with the army and a week-long tour of New Zealand.

Justin Jackson, a Florida man, impersonated celebrities including Oprah Winfrey, Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager to trick people into giving him freebies worth $2.4 million, jobs, and luxury items over eight years. Jackson sent fraudulent emails to hotels, jewelry stores, and clothing retailers, posing as Oprah and Love, and even claimed to be her nephew. He was sued by Oprah's network and Love.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini values Paulo Dybala at €50m, dubbing him 'the new Messi'. Dybala is sought by PSG, Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, and Juventus. Zamparini wants €50m, while PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi is willing to pay €40m. Dybala's future remains uncertain as he faces competition from top European clubs.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians protest against President Dilma Rousseff, calling for her impeachment due to an ongoing bribery scandal at state-run oil company Petrobras. The scandal implicates many of Rousseff's allies, including her own Workers Party, and has led to a plummeting approval rating and economic downturn. Protesters demand Rousseff clean up corruption, while her supporters defend her and argue she should not be impeached.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has denied claims he starred in a soft porn film, "You and the Night," insisting it is a work of art. The film, featuring racy scenes including Cantona on his hands and knees in underwear, has been both praised and criticized, with Cantona defending it as beautiful and not pornographic.

Psychologists found that certain music can enhance flavors in food and drinks, with The Beatles' music enhancing the enjoyment of fish and chips. Research shows specific musical tones can highlight flavors like bitterness, sweetness, and saltiness, improving dining experiences.

Liverpool player Raheem Sterling is holding off contract negotiations until the season ends, despite a £100,000-a-week offer from the club. Sterling's manager Brendan Rodgers called the offer "incredible," but Sterling insists he's not a "money grabber." PFA chief Gordon Taylor supports Sterling's decision, noting it's common for players to consider their options, even if it's untidy in the media spotlight. Sterling has been linked with moves to Arsenal and Spanish clubs.

Ohio woman La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark discovered her biological mother Francine Simmons works at the same company and lives six minutes away. After receiving birth records, she connected with Simmons on Facebook and eventually met her, learning she has three younger sisters she didn't know about. Simmons, now in her 50s, had been trying to contact her daughter for years.

Oscar 'Papoo' Hernandez Jr., a Florida man, pleaded guilty to weapons charges related to Aaron Hernandez's murder of Odin Lloyd. Hernandez, who was paid $15,000 by Hernandez to ship assault rifle and handguns, said he was 'awed' by the NFL star but unaware of the tragic consequences. Hernandez was sentenced to up to 30 months in prison for his role in the gun trafficking.

33-year-old Joel Parker, after threatening and disrupting a bus driver, threw a Snickers bar at the driver's head during a ride in St Johns County, Florida, leading to his arrest for battery and a $250 bond, with a ban on future bus use.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis discussed pre-season plans with striker Saido Berahino, indicating Berahino will likely stay beyond the summer transfer window despite interest from other clubs. Berahino is likely to be with England's under-21 team in the Czech Republic until late June, allowing Pulis to prepare for his return. Berahino has expressed a desire to play in European football's top leagues.
