Tony Pulis, West Bromwich Albion manager, conceded that Joey Barton's claim that his players "s*** themselves" during a 3-2 defeat to Queens Park Rangers in December was likely correct, recalling his own similar experience as a manager. Barton said West Brom were 2-0 up and lost 3-2, leading to Alan Irvine's near dismissal. Pulis admitted Barton had a point, noting West Brom's strong performances and solid defense since scoring first.

A Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought extinct for over 50 years, was captured in the Ntokou-Pikounda National Park in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Primatologists Lieven Devreese and Gaël Elie Gnondo Gobolo took the first-ever photograph of the species, proving it is not extinct. However, the monkeys are vulnerable to hunters in the commercial bushmeat trade, and their population is believed to be extremely small.

Kim Kardashian, Kanye West, and daughter North visited Armenia, the country of her father's birth, for eight days, arriving in the capital Yerevan with a rock star welcome. They explored local landmarks and cultural sites, including the Yerevan Opera House and the Katoghiken church in the World Heritage-listed Geghard Monastery, staying at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan.

British expats Patrick and Valerie Jubb are trapped in southern Spain amid a legal battle with the local town hall over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated. The couple purchased La Vina de Linan in 2008 and closed it a year ago, planning to sell it for €680,000. However, the town hall ruled that illegal additions made by a previous owner in 1994, including a swimming pool, are on the property. The Jubbs claim they obtained a certificate stating there were no infractions when they bought the estate, and the alterations were legalised by land registry officials in 2005. The property, located in Los Alcornocales Natural Park, is now on the brink of being demolished, with the Jubbs seeking to move back to the UK but unable to do so due to their financial ties to the property.

Apple reported its best-ever quarterly results, selling more than 61 million iPhones for $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit, up 40% from a year ago. Sales in China outpaced those in the US, with revenue from iPhones accounting for more than two-thirds of total revenue. iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer sales rose 2% to $5.6 billion.

A 3-year-old girl, Elisa Tyler, has been having recurring nightmares and daytime visions about a white van, which her father believes may be linked to her mother's death in a 2002 Ford Explorer crash in Virginia. Natali Castellanos-Tyler, 30, died in the accident, ruled a one-car collision due to poor road conditions, while Elisa emerged largely unscathed. The girl's disturbing dreams have coincided with reports of hit-and-run incidents involving a white delivery-style truck in the area, leading her father to suspect a connection.

Researchers at New York University found that the brain can more easily remember 'neutral' or boring events tied to emotion, challenging the common belief that we remember emotionally charged events better. This study, which also looked at how the September 11 terrorist attacks affect memory retention, suggests that emotion enhances the strength of memories, even for mundane details. Sleep can also boost memory consolidation, with a 45-minute nap reportedly improving recall by five times.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of 18-year-old Jackson Byrnes with a stage four brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 from the community to fund his life-saving surgery by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo on Wednesday. Despite the tumour being too deep and aggressive for initial safe operation, Jackson and Jahnae found Dr. Teo online and reached their fundraising goal, now needing an additional $45,000 for chemotherapy and other hospital fees.

Nedum Onuoha, 28, a QPR centre-back with 15 months left on contract, is wanted by Hull City amid QPR's squad streamlining. Onuoha played in the crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion and is also of interest to Everton and West Ham United. QPR are also considering Catania defender Nicolas Spolli and West Bromwich Albion striker Victor Anichebe for transfer.

From 'here's you a piece of pizza' to 'this glass needs washed', every state has its own phrases that can seem odd to the rest of the world. Researchers at Yale University documented these patterns by mapping common phrases across the US, revealing significant regional differences in sentence structure. The interactive map, based on nationwide surveys, shows how speakers in different states naturally use unique grammatical structures, with Southeners finding sentences like 'Here's you a water bottle' normal, while Northerners consider them alien.

A Canadian man, Kalman Kallai, travelled 2,796 miles from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia in a green rocking chair, taking breaks to watch planes, pose with cows, and even chase birds, sharing his journey on video. He bonded with his father during part of the trip, recounting stories from his youth.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood, after being passed over for the Villa manager position by Tim Sherwood when Paul Lambert was sacked, quizzed the media about a letter from six-year-old fan Charlie Pye who applied for the job. Sherwood revealed he had sent Pye a Twix multi-pack as a 'win bonus' for his letter, joking that Pye wanted his mum and dad as assistant managers.

World boxing champion Kell Brook watched the Premier League Darts in Sheffield, receiving a hero's welcome after his recent title defense. Dave Chisnall, who was second in the Premier League table, won both of his games, including a 7-3 victory over world champion Gary Anderson and a 7-1 win over James Wade. Brook is set to defend his title against Frankie Gavin on May 30.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic, saying the 33-year-old striker plays an essential role for the club, both on and off the pitch. Ibrahimovic, who has scored 17 Ligue 1 goals this season, helps young players and exerts confidence in the team. He was suspended for the Champions League match against Barcelona but will be available for the return leg.

The Ministry of Defence faced criticism after a secret RAF base on the Falklands Islands, containing GPS coordinates and runway depth information, was accidentally published on their website, potentially giving Argentine intelligence an invasion guide. The Aerodrome Manual, uploaded to a public section, could have been used to plan an attack on the islands, with Argentina considering leasing Cold War-era SU-24 bombers from Russia.

Huddersfield Giants, currently ninth in Super League, aim to improve their attack to match their strong defense after losing all three games since Easter. Coach Paul Anderson hopes to boost his team's offensive performance, which has been a weakness all season, with a home game against the top defensive team, Catalans Dragons. A win could propel Huddersfield to fourth place, while Vikings coach Denis Betts expects a tough challenge from Castleford, who have a solid defense but also a strong attack.

Planners in Windsor approved two Costa Coffee shops less than 500 yards apart, including one replacing a cycle shop earlier this year, adding to the existing one just a five-minute walk away. This decision contrasts with a resident's concern about too many fast food and coffee shops, but planners argue it will boost local trade.

The British Veterinary Association withdrew its support for shooting free-running badgers in pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, concluding that the first two years of culling had not demonstrated conclusively that 'controlled shooting' was effective and humane. The BVA still supports badger culling to tackle tuberculosis in cattle, but animal welfare campaigners criticized the ongoing support for cage-trapping and shooting. The Environment Secretary promised to roll out more culls if the Tories win the election, despite criticism from wildlife groups and a lack of expected benefits in Gloucestershire.

Geoff Barrow, Portishead's founder, criticized streaming services for paying his band just £1,700 for 34 million plays, arguing that it hurts young artists and threatens their ability to tour. Barrow called for higher royalties, while streaming companies defended their practices, offering a fair price in an age of easy music access.

Game of Thrones fans leaked the first four episodes of the fifth season online before its HBO premiere tonight, with the episodes downloaded more than 550,000 times. The leak occurred from press review copies and is believed to have originated from within HBO-approved groups, causing fans to face spoiler risks as the full season premieres over a month.

A 25-year-old Melbourne singer, Daniel Buccheri, composed an emotional song to use as his best man's speech at his brother's wedding, leaving guests in tears. Composing the tune to popular songs like Sam Smith and the Backstreet Boys, Daniel sang "Stay With Me" as his brother began to cry, then proceeded to share memories of his brother's courtship with his new wife Sarah, including his own childhood memories and how he always looked up to his older sibling. The speech, which has been viewed over 100,000 times online, documented the day his brother met Sarah and how he made his brother happy.

Zara Phillips, Queen's granddaughter, regained her fitness after giving birth to Mia Grace by exercising on an exercise bike every morning before her daughter woke up, aiming to qualify for Team GB at the 2016 Olympics. She eats a balanced diet and spends time with horses at her mother Princess Anne's stables, hoping to pass her love for eventing to her daughter.

Raheem Sterling, Liverpool's star player, said he was not ready to sign a new contract, angering Liverpool fans. Sterling's interview was ill-timed, and Liverpool fans now believe he should leave, despite the club's efforts to keep him. The club has a policy that no player is bigger than the club, and Sterling's departure is now seen as possible.

Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola engaged in a conversation during a Barcelona training session in 2016, with Guardiola hinting he would coach Barcelona and win the treble. This photo sparked interest, revealing other notable coaches from the same Barcelona team of 1996-97, including Laurent Blanc and Julen Lopetegui, who are now coaching PSG and Porto, respectively.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona, at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai, declared Paris Saint-Germain's Javier Pastore the best player in the world, praising his creativity and passing skills over Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Pastore, who cost PSG £29 million, has three goals and five assists this season, while Messi has 45 goals for Barcelona and Ronaldo 51 for Real Madrid.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murdering his tenant Michael Spalding, 39, by hacking him to pieces and dumping the body parts in a canal in Smethwick, Birmingham, after a four-week trial. Simon and his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, were cleared of murder but admitted assisting an offender.

Health experts warn that being socially isolated can be as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day, leading to dementia and high blood pressure. Two UK councils, Essex and Gloucestershire, have developed 'loneliness maps' to identify areas with the highest risk of social isolation among elderly residents. Gloucestershire used public health statistics and resident surveys to map vulnerable areas, prioritizing those over 65, living alone, or with mental health issues. The Campaign to End Loneliness now urges other councils to create similar maps to target support for the most isolated people.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary working at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she began her job at age 15 in 1965. Eddingfield, who has worked there since 1940, says it's the only job she's ever had and that her mother started working there 13 years earlier. She recalls a time when she spilled a shake on a customer's fur coat but was forgiven, and she has worked alongside many family members over the years. Eddingfield also mentions that she met her future husband at the restaurant and that the TV show 'Leave It to Beaver' actors once dined there.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not automatically return to the international team, despite scoring 170 runs for Surrey. Gatting argues that Pietersen would need to perform poorly to earn a place, noting that Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root are currently playing well. Gatting also suggests that Alastair Cook, England's Test captain, may face questions if he fails to score runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old Californian student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' for iOS, allowing users to upload photos directly from their computer to Instagram. The app, which he sells for $4.99, now faces a potential lawsuit from Instagram, as it allegedly violates the company's terms of service. Benn has reportedly made $1,000 a day from the app, despite Instagram asking him to 'fix' it by Monday.

South Korean companies frequently host hoesik, or official drinking dinners, where employees often consume multiple rounds of alcohol at various venues. For foreign business travelers, these events can be challenging, as drinking is deeply ingrained in Korean culture and seen as a way to build relationships and understand colleagues better. Traffic patterns in Seoul reflect the city's drinking culture, with fewer cars on the road on Mondays and Fridays, when hoesik are most common.

The Duke of Kent, 79, suffered a dislocated hip while visiting Balmoral estate in Aberdeenshire and was hospitalized at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. He was discharged after a night's treatment, using a walking stick, and continues to perform royal duties despite his injury.

The 50-year-old Surfers Paradise Meter Maids, started in 1965 by Gold Coast developer Bernie Elsey, are facing criticism from local business leaders who argue they are outdated and irrelevant due to electronic parking meters. Business owners claim the group violates anti-touting laws by selling branded merchandise and no longer perform a public service. Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president Peter Yared supports ending the tradition, while Meter Maids general manager Michael Yarwood defends their role as a beloved part of the Gold Coast experience.

Greece denied it would fail to repay a £330 million IMF loan due on April 9, with Deputy Finance Minister Dimitris Mardas stating the country will make the payment on time. However, sources close to the ruling Syriza party claimed the government prioritized paying wages and pensions over loans, potentially leading to a default if the eurozone does not agree to release bailout funds.

Turkey blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after the social media platforms refused to remove images of prosecutor Mehmet Selim Kiraz, who was held hostage and later killed during an armed siege. The images deeply upset the hostage's wife and children, and the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front (DHKP-C), considered a terrorist group, was behind the siege.

A young autistic boy Colin Gilpatric, 7, wrote to George Lucas, creator of Star Wars, asking if Jedi Knights could marry to avoid becoming a villain like Anakin Skywalker. Lucas responded, granting the request and sending Colin a letter and Star Wars merchandise, reassuring him that marriage is part of the Jedi path.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky 71-64 in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's 38-1 unbeaten season and bringing an end to their quest for an NCAA title. Frank Kaminsky scored 20 points and grabbed 11 rebounds for Wisconsin, who will face Duke in the final at Indianapolis's Lucas Oil Stadium. Kentucky's Karl-Anthony Towns missed a potential game-winning free throw, while Duke won 81-61 over Michigan State in the other semi-final.

Mötley Crüe's Vince Neil's performance of "The Star-Spangled Banner" at a Las Vegas Arena Football League game was criticized, with Neil's rendition described as a "butchering" of the song, following a long tradition of varying performances of the national anthem by famous figures, from Whitney Houston's acclaimed rendition to Jimi Hendrix's controversial psychedelic version.

CCTV footage showed Barry Lyttle, an Irishman from Belfast, punching his younger brother Patrick, causing him to fall and suffer a traumatic head injury in Sydney in January. Patrick was treated by paramedics and nearly died; he is now facing a possible jail term after pleading guilty to grievous bodily harm, with his fate to be decided in court.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, born with disrosopus, found their gravesite at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney's west completely bare after cemetery staff had cleared the baby section, leaving behind only a few flowers. The twins, who died 19 days after birth, had a small shrine set up with mementos and flowers, which was removed by staff without warning or notification.

Britain's Supreme Court President Lord Neuberger suggested Muslim women should be allowed to wear full-face veils in court, emphasizing judges should show respect for different customs. This came amid uncertainty over the veil's place in the legal system, following a 2003 trial where a Muslim woman refused to testify due to a court order to remove her veil. Last year, the European Court of Human Rights upheld a ban on wearing the veil in public, prompting debate on its role in the legal system.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri on Tuesday night for killing Anthony Curtis, a friend visiting his ex-wife, in a fit of rage over child support payments 16 years ago. Cole became the third convicted killer put to death in Missouri this year, despite appeals claiming he was mentally ill and unfit for execution.

Prince Harry will fly to Australia without meeting his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is now overdue for the birth of her second child, who will be fourth in line to the British throne. Harry had hoped to see the new royal baby but must return to Australia for a month-long army placement and a week-long tour of New Zealand.

A Florida man named Justin Jackson was accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager to trick people into giving him freebies worth $2.4 million, including jobs, clothes, and jewelry. Jackson allegedly contacted jewelry stores and hotel groups, sending forged emails and letters to get free items and job recommendations. He was convicted for grand theft and faces lawsuits from Oprah's TV network and Love.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini valued Paulo Dybala at €50 million (£36 million), warning PSG they would have to spend big to sign the player, who is also wanted by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and PSG. Dybala, likened to Lionel Messi, is being tracked by Palermo despite Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini's interest.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians protested against President Dilma Rousseff, calling for her impeachment due to an economic downturn and a massive bribery scandal at state-run oil company Petrobras, where executives and politicians allegedly received bribes for contracts. Rousseff's approval rating dropped to 13% after the protests, and the economy is expected to contract this year with high inflation and a 20% currency devaluation.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona denied claims he starred in a soft porn film, "You and the Night," insisting it is a "piece of art." The film, featuring racy scenes including Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear, has been both praised and criticized, with Cantona defending it as beautiful and not pornographic.

Psychologists found that certain types of music can enhance flavors in food and drink, with researchers suggesting that listening to The Beatles could improve enjoyment of a fish and chip supper. In Shanghai, fish and chips are served to a Beatles soundtrack, while in Spain, a commentary on Lionel Messi's footballing prowess accompanies a dessert. Music can also improve wine enjoyment by up to 15%, with specific pieces of music pairing well with certain wines and foods, according to behavioral psychologist Charles Spence.

Liverpool player Raheem Sterling, offered a £100,000-a-week contract by manager Brendan Rodgers, has put contract negotiations on hold until the season ends, with PFA chief executive Gordon Taylor defending his decision, citing the need to focus on football and avoid media scrutiny.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same company and lived just six minutes away. After receiving birth records for people born between 1964 and 1996, Mitchell-Clark connected with Simmons on Facebook and eventually met her. Simmons, who had always wanted to contact her daughter, was surprised to find Mitchell-Clark, who has three younger sisters she did not know about.

Oscar 'Papoo' Hernandez Jr., a Florida man, pleaded guilty to weapons charges connected to Aaron Hernandez, the former New England Patriots player. Hernandez shipped three firearms, including an assault rifle and handguns, to Aaron Hernandez a month before the semi-professional football player, Odin Lloyd, was killed in 2013. Hernandez, awed by Aaron's fame, sent the weapons for $15,000, unaware of the tragic consequences.

Joel Parker, 33, was arrested in St Johns County, Florida, after throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head during a ride, threatening and disrupting the driver, according to police. Parker was arrested for battery and posted $250 bond, receiving a trespass warning and being banned from using the bus.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis discussed pre-season plans with striker Saido Berahino, indicating he plans to keep the 21-year-old beyond the summer transfer window despite interest from other clubs, including a £20 million bid in January. Berahino is likely to be with England's under-21 team in the Czech Republic until late June, giving Pulis time to prepare.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a 28-year-old Italian project manager with Welthungerlife, was abducted in Pakistan in 2012 by armed men and later killed in a U.S. drone strike in Afghanistan, along with American hostage Warren Weinstein. Lo Porto worked on reconstruction projects following flooding in Pakistan, where his family called him Giancarlo, and was known for his humanitarian work and positive attitude.

A photographer named John Massung spotted hundreds of sharks, including Blacktips and Spinners, swarming just 100 feet from the beach at Sebastian Inlet, south Florida, on Thursday. The swarm was spotted by Massung and another photographer, who theorized it was a mix of Blacktip and Spinner sharks migrating to breed. The sighting was shared widely on social media, with the picture posted to Indian River by Air Facebook page, and the sharks were still present on Friday.

An 11-year-old retired German Shepherd K-9 officer Zeus, who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years, was honored in a heartwarming farewell procession in Connecticut on Wednesday before being put down due to a severe degenerative hip disorder. The tribute included a grand procession through Ridgefield streets, with residents lining the route and police departments across the state participating. Zeus assisted with over 250 narcotics arrests and helped track down 50 missing or wanted individuals during his career.

Reports of child sex abuse cases in England and Wales rose by more than 60% since 2011, with South Yorkshire experiencing a 577% increase. Despite a surge in reports, the number of arrests fell by 9%, prompting critics to accuse the government of failing victims. The NSPCC helpline saw an 81% increase in calls about sexual abuse after Operation Yewtree was launched in 2012.

Iceland has become a popular filming location, with 17 production services companies established nationwide. Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Skaftafell National Park, Vatnajökull, and Dettifoss have been used in productions like Game of Thrones, Interstellar, Prometheus, and Thor. Scenes from these films, including battle scenes in Game of Thrones and the beginning of time in Prometheus, have been filmed in Iceland's stunning landscapes.

A blue and yellow bathing box on Melbourne's Brighton beach sold for $276,000, a record price, after five bidders battled at auction. In Sydney, a 100-year-old grey-fronted mechanic’s garage built as a fire station in 1917 was sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home. An 1850s maximum security goal in Victoria was put up for sale for $2 million, with the owners claiming it is haunted.

40-year-old Samantha Rawcliffe, a mother from Morecambe, crashed her car after a rare brain disorder caused uncontrollable shaking and loss of bladder control following an accident in May. Diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) in September, she now relies on a mobility scooter and takes 32 medications daily, unable to walk or drive. FND is an umbrella term for neurological symptoms with no known cause, making it difficult to treat and manage.

Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created a statue of Lucille Ball in Celoron, New York, admitted to being disappointed in his work, describing it as "by far my most unsettling sculpture." Following a social media campaign, Poulin offered to remake the bronze statue for free, estimating the cost at $8,000 to $10,000, while residents described it as "monstrous" and "frightening."

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba, who had been sidelined for three months earlier this season, is out for around seven weeks with a torn knee ligament after being injured in Austria's 1-1 draw against Bosnia. Alaba, who had been in superb form for Bayern, is set to start rehabilitation in about a month and will miss the closing stages of the Bundesliga season and the Champions League quarter-finals.

University College London student Beatrice Nokes, 21, appeared in court accused of running a prostitution ring with suspended Scotland Yard detective Daniel Williams, 37, in Central London last year. Nokes faces three charges of causing or inciting prostitution, while Williams is charged with seven additional offenses including voyeurism and misuse of police resources. Both are on bail and will return to court.

A firm called Sequester, linked to Alchemy Direct Media, is offering details of over 43 health conditions, including eating disorders, stress, and impotence, for just 12p per person. The data includes sensitive personal information such as financial details, medical history, and credit card information. The revelations prompted investigations by the Information Commissioner’s Office, Direct Marketing Commission, and the General Pharmaceutical Council, highlighting the sale of private patient data without proper checks.

Jordan Spieth, 21, won the Masters golf tournament, equalling Tiger Woods' 1997 record score of 18 under par. He became the second-youngest winner and only the fifth to lead from start to finish. Spieth, whose younger sister Ellie was autistic, expressed his desire to bring her the green jacket as a present.

Sunderland's new manager Dick Advocaat, who previously underplayed the significance of the Old Firm derby, will lead Sunderland against Newcastle in the Wear-Tyne Derby. Advocaat, recalling his mistake from 1998 when he underestimated Celtic's victory, insists he will not repeat it. Sunderland, currently one point above the relegation zone, faces a crucial home game where they aim to win for the first time at their stadium this season.

A dispute erupted between Belinda Bartholomew, girlfriend of Roosters player Aidan Guerra, and a butcher at Sam the Butcher in Bondi, Sydney, when Bartholomew asked for a different chicken. She claims the butcher called her a "f***ing c***" and told her to "go to an Aussie butcher," while the butcher denies any abuse and says Bartholomew was being rude due to issues with his eftpos machine.

Cadbury reduced the size of Freddo Frogs from 20g to 12g, a 20% decrease, while keeping the price the same. The move was due to manufacturing cost increases, affecting the popular chocolate treat after a similar size reduction in family blocks of Dairy Milk. Consumer backlash was significant, with thousands voicing anger on social media, criticizing the company for making the product less affordable.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met in Brooklyn on Saturday, a day before her official announcement. Robby Mook, her campaign manager, distributed a "values statement" outlining goals and principles, aiming to avoid mistakes from her 2008 campaign. The document emphasizes humility, discipline, and unity, focusing on grassroots efforts and winning votes across states. Clinton plans to launch her campaign on Sunday, starting with visits to Iowa and New Hampshire.

A young woman, Kyli Wilfson, battled a rare condition called chronic pancreatitis for over a year and a half, unable to eat due to excruciating abdominal pain, despite feeling desperately hungry. Initially misdiagnosed with acute pancreatitis, she was finally diagnosed after a camera was inserted into her throat, leading to a permanent feeding tube and rapid weight loss to 80lbs.

Labour leader Ed Miliband was superimposed over London rapper Plan B in a meme, referencing his direct message to Prime Minister David Cameron to debate one-on-one. Other leaders, including Nicola Sturgeon and Nigel Farage, were featured in various memes, with Cameron and Nick Clegg appearing as characters from the TV show Gogglebox.

Amir Khan, seeking a fight with the best boxers, could face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after waiting for Floyd Mayweather. Khan, who has sparred with Pacquiao, is reportedly interested in the November or December fight in Abu Dhabi, where Khan would be a draw due to his popularity in the Muslim world. Khan's next fight is an interim bout with Chris Algieri in New York.

A tiny two-bedroom home, only 5ft wide in some areas, sold for £750,000 in Islington, north London. Located between two double-fronted properties, the 8ft 8in wide home, with a narrow 'galley kitchen', garnered interest despite its small size, selling for almost double its 2001 price.

Nicola Sturgeon, Scotland's First Minister, launches an election manifesto today, including policies that overlap with Labour, aiming to form a power-sharing deal. The SNP manifesto proposes slashing English tuition fees to £6,000, rolling back NHS competition, and cancelling Trident, while also increasing public spending on infrastructure. The SNP is expected to win a majority of seats in Scotland, potentially triggering constitutional changes similar to those after the 1910 election.

Celtic's Under-17 team beat Rangers 2-0 in the Glasgow Cup final at Hampden Park, with Josh Kerr scoring the opener and Mark Hill the second, as Rangers' Robby McCrorie made two costly mistakes. The match, played behind closed doors due to fan trouble, saw Celtic secure their fourth Glasgow Cup title in eight seasons.

West Bromwich Albion's Tony Pulis led his team to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, marking a crucial win for the Baggies' safety in the Premier League. Pulis, known for his distinctive cap-wearing style, insisted he would never change his on-field attire, insisting it keeps him close to the action. The win moved West Brom to 36 points, virtually guaranteeing their Premier League survival.

Jameela Jamil, a television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 to have all 10 amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after experiencing health issues for nearly seven years, including puffy face, exhaustion, and fainting. Her mercury levels were found to be high, leading to the conclusion that her amalgam fillings were the cause, though dental experts argue the risk is minimal.

Rap mogul Suge Knight, awaiting trial for murder and attempted murder, was denied a bail reduction to $5 million. Knight, who hopes Floyd Mayweather will bail him out, is set to face trial starting July 7. Mayweather, an undefeated boxer worth $420 million, is set to fight Manny Pacquiao on Saturday, and Knight's attorney believes Mayweather will win and help bail him out.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine, 35, showcased a lavish feast for her British shorthair cat Kimchi in a cat magazine shoot, featuring caviar, salmon roe, and seafood sculptures. Kimchi, known for its discerning palate, loves human food like poppadoms and tortilla chips, with taramasalata being his "death row dish." Erskine admits Kimchi is now on a diet due to overeating, while her new cat Ponzu, named after a Japanese dressing, has expensive tastes, including green curry.

Martin Springall, the father of a little girl photographed in Japan in 2014, posted an image online showing a mysterious black boot behind his daughter. Despite showing his wife immediately, Springall now claims he has no idea what the object is and insists it was not Photoshopped. The image sparked debate on Reddit, with some suggesting it could be samurai boots, while others questioned its authenticity. Springall confirmed there was no one else in the area.

The Conservative government plans to require EU migrants to pay £22,000 in taxes and national insurance before they can claim benefits, under plans to curb immigration and negotiate a new EU deal. Unemployed EU migrants will be banned from receiving state support for four years, while those in work will face a four-year waiting period before claiming benefits like housing and tax credits. The policy aims to limit migration from poorer EU countries and address concerns about net long-term migration to the UK, estimated at 298,000 in the year ending September 2014.

Eight-year-old Cody Neatis, with Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and tube feeding, has been sleeping on the floor in a cramped hospital room for seven nights due to a lack of a suitable high-sided bed. The Royal Preston Hospital in Preston, England, has not provided the specialized cot Cody needs to sleep safely, forcing his mother, Lynne Neatis, to sleep with him on the floor. Cody's father, Stephen Neatis, says they have been forced to sleep on the floor for nine days in August 2013, and Cody's mother claims this situation has persisted for years, with no resolution despite complaints.

Englishman Ian Poulter, World No. 1 Rory McIlroy, and Swede Henrik Stenson are among golfers attending the Masters, where McIlroy is aiming for a career grand slam, Stenson is recovering from flu, and Poulter forgot his clubs. Tiger Woods will play with his children and participate in a par-three tournament for the first time in over a decade.

Juventus, after ruling out a move for Manchester United loan striker Radamel Falcao due to his high wages, expressed interest in Palermo's Paulo Dybala and Paris Saint-Germain's Edinson Cavani, citing their need to strengthen the forward line. Juventus, who reached the Champions League semi-finals, claimed they cannot afford Falcao, who has struggled at Manchester United, and are interested in Dybala, valued at £35 million by his club.

David Cameron pledges to sell £4 billion worth of Lloyds Bank shares if re-elected, offering public shares at a 5% discount, with a maximum £10,000 purchase limit and a loyalty bonus. This would be the largest privatization since the Thatcher era, encouraging long-term investment.

Living near congested roads with high PM2.5 levels, a type of air pollution mostly from traffic fumes, can cause ‘silent strokes’ that lead to brain damage and increase dementia risk, according to a study. Researchers found that for every 10 micrograms per cubic meter increase in PM2.5, there was a 46% higher risk of silent strokes in over 900 people aged 60 and over without dementia or stroke history.

Jessica Ainscough, 30, died in late February from epithelioid sarcoma, choosing unconventional Gerson Therapy over chemotherapy and radiation. Her partner Tallon Pamenter revealed she began targeted radiation in her final weeks, a risky but brave decision. Despite treatment, complications arose, and Ainscough passed away, leaving Pamenter devastated and reflecting on her "wellness warrior" lifestyle and courage.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway, 2km south of Fernvale, on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in the first patients being flown out by rescue helicopter to Princess Alexandra Hospital, where a 40-year-old man and a five-year-old boy were taken for chest and shoulder injuries. A 27-year-old woman and a six-year-old girl were also flown out with arm and abdominal injuries. Six others, including an infant and two young girls, were taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries. A man suffered hand lacerations, and two females escaped injury. The highway was closed for a few hours with diversions in place south of Fernvale. Emergency crews freed one person trapped in their vehicle using hydraulic cutting gear before airlifting patients to hospital.

Jason McDonald, a 34-year-old volunteer at the Colorado Gator Farm, walked a 10-foot-wide slackline over a pool containing over 50 alligators, some up to ten feet long, at the farm in Aurora, Colorado. The alligators, which he had been handling for over ten years, appeared to be unbothered by the presence of the slackline. McDonald, who has never been bitten before, plans to attempt walking over the farm's largest and albino alligators in the future.

The son of slain Syrian imam Abdul Hadi Arwani, who was called to a job site in North West London, may have met his father's killer days before the murder. Arwani, 48, a Muslim Brotherhood member, was shot and killed in his car on a quiet street after being asked to return another day by a potential client. The client, described as black and speaking with an African accent, initially asked Arwani to return alone but then told him there was no need for his son to accompany him again. Scotland Yard investigates whether the client was a hired killer who postponed the hit because Arwani was not alone.

Hong Kong's Tsim Sha Tsui district saw a black market for $9 tins of Jenny's butter cookies, drawing tourists and locals who queued for hours. The original store warned against buying knockoffs, while knockoff bakeries sprang up, and resellers stood in line to buy the cookies at a 70% markup.

Kira Hollis, a 27-year-old from Tamworth, Staffordshire, diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and depression, gained weight and overcame her mental health issues by becoming a bodybuilder. Initially ordered to the gym to gain weight, she turned her life around, now a personal trainer and a mother to a six-year-old daughter, Olivia. Her story, shared online, has gone viral, inspiring others.

Jockey Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular double somersault fall from favorite Merrion Square at Wincanton on Wednesday, sustaining only a cut on his nose. The fall, caught on video and watched by hundreds of thousands online, left Ferguson undeterred, stating he would continue riding, aiming for the Cheltenham Festival and the Grand National.

Hillary Clinton launched her 2016 presidential campaign with a video, new logo, and road trip, aiming to rebrand herself and reframe her message from self-absorbed to empathetic. Critics dismissed her launch as vapid, but her team aimed to create an empathetic relationship with voters, projecting a more confident and forward-looking image.

More than 1,700 Chinese freshmen students from Yichuan, Shaanxi province took their first high school exam in a playground on Saturday due to lack of indoor space. The students organized the outdoor exam themselves, rotating their chairs and desks to avoid sun glare, and suggested it could help prevent cheating and broaden their horizons. The school saw it as a test of students' organizing capacity.

The winner of a Sportsmail competition will receive a pair of Joe Hart-signed Nike Magista Obra boots, a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor, and shaving gel, valued at £16.29, with Hart as England and Manchester City goalkeeper. The prize is part of a Gillette partnership and the competition closes April 19.

One-year-old baby orangutan Kecil, rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate, found a new surrogate mother, Maggie, 53, at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo after 10 months of care. Maggie, who has raised four of her own children, now has an inseparable bond with Kecil, who will make his public debut at the zoo this weekend.

A 61-year-old woman from Winchester, Hampshire, died after her pet dogs, a Jack Russell and Staffordshire Bull Terrier, ate her partially following an accidental overdose of medication. Noelle Baynham, who had run a bath and was found in her dressing gown, was discovered by a concerned friend who entered the house after failing to find her. The dogs, initially thought to have tried to wake her, were found eating her remains, and a pathologist could not determine the exact cause of death due to the dogs' consumption of vital organs.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, a multiple gold medalist, will stand trial for fraud over match-fixing allegations involving his brother Luka and 15 other players, including former Montpellier teammates. The case stems from a 2012 match where Montpellier, already champions, lost to Cesson-Rennes, with betting patterns suggesting match-fixing. Karabatic denies placing bets and faces up to five years in prison if convicted.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were jailed for a total of 31 years after being convicted of sexually abusing six teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. The defendants, who organized under-18s parties on social media, lured the victims to commit sexual offenses in cars, woods, or at their homes. The victims, aged 13 to 16, were described as emotionally immature and lacked friends, making them vulnerable to the gang's abuse.

Former New England Patriots player Aaron Hernandez, convicted of murder and other charges in the death of Odin Lloyd, faces another murder trial in July 2012 shooting deaths of Daniel de Abreu and Safiro Furtado in Boston. Hernandez's legal team will continue representing him in at least three more trials, including a civil suit filed by the families of de Abreu and Furtado, and a lawsuit by a man he allegedly shot in a Miami limousine.

The Dubai-based Emirates airline will rebrand the FA Cup, football's oldest knockout competition, as the Emirates FA Cup in a £30 million, three-year deal. The move adds to Emirates' growing portfolio of sporting sponsorships, which includes a £150 million deal with Arsenal Football Club and a £80 million deal with AC Milan.

Michael Phelps, 29, aiming for a fifth Olympic appearance in Rio, announced he will not compete in the upcoming world championships in Russia due to a six-month suspension from USA Swimming for a second DUI arrest in September. Phelps, who had already qualified for three events, expressed regret over missing the world meet but emphasized his desire to compete in Rio.

Gareth Bale, a key Real Madrid player, is a huge doubt for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury, after limping off in a 3-1 win over Malaga. Real Madrid also lacks Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who is expected to be out for six weeks with a knee ligament strain. Real were held to a goalless draw in the first leg against Atletico.

Scientists warned that older people are more susceptible to emotional decision-making in retirement investments, leading to losses. In the 2007-2008 financial crisis, 50% of pensioners panicked and sold investments, resulting in a £63,000 pot today compared to £141,000 if they had held onto them. This comes as Britain's pension reforms allow 55-year-olds to access their savings, increasing emotional risk for older investors.

Stuart Pearce, former Manchester City player and manager, believes Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to turn around Manchester City's Premier League fortunes, despite recent poor form including a 2-1 loss to Manchester United. Pearce criticized the club's reliance on Yaya Toure, who has had a largely ineffective season, and suggested City should look to freshen up their squad in the summer.

Manchester United's stars, including Wayne Rooney, trained in sunny conditions ahead of their Premier League derby against Manchester City on Sunday. The match is significant as United are one point behind City in the table and could move four points clear if they win. United's last home win over City was in 2011, when Rooney scored an overhead kick.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona at home, with substitute Mounir Obbadi scoring in the 90th minute, leaving Fiorentina nine points behind third-placed AS Roma and dropping to sixth in Serie A. Former West Ham midfielder Alessandro Diamanti missed a penalty, and coach Vincenzo Montella criticized his team's performance. The loss leaves Fiorentina in the Europa League quarter-finals after a 1-1 first leg against Dynamo Kiev.

Miley Cyrus, at the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, was photographed with visible armpit hair, causing a social media stir. Many users, including some fans, criticized her for not shaving, while others defended her choice, arguing that body hair is normal for both genders.

Barcelona's trio of Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez scored a century of goals this season, reaching 102 in all competitions after a 6-0 victory over Getafe, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi scored twice, Neymar netted once, and Suarez scored two, with Messi leading with 49 goals, Neymar with 32, and Suarez with 21.

Andrea McVeigh, 44, was left scarred for life after being knocked down by a cyclist riding on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London on April 14. The cyclist fled the scene, and McVeigh's husband chased him, leading to an appeal for the suspect's capture. McVeigh suffered two three-inch gashes to her forehead and other facial and hand injuries, and the police have issued CCTV footage and an appeal for information.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 and ordered to do 150 hours of unpaid work after pleading guilty to dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by falsely claiming he could only walk 200 metres, despite being a keen walker and mountaineering club member. The fraud was exposed when council officials read about his 191-mile hike in Cumbria, which featured him being attacked by cows, in a newspaper article.

Apple has patented a facial recognition system for unlocking devices that uses the front-facing camera. The system detects a user's face when the phone is moved into a specific position and unlocks automatically if the image matches a stored photo, a feature already available on Android devices.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, a cancer patient battling multiple myeloma, was forcibly removed from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California along with her family because she lacked a doctor's note, despite her request for extra time due to her condition. The Sedways were seated in the handicapped section and had to be forcibly removed from a packed plane, with one passenger noting they were being "removed as if they were a criminal or contagious because she has cancer."

Three people were taken to hospital following a head-on collision between a 1973 E-Type Jaguar, valued at over $120,000, and a Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night at a traffic light intersection on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney. The crash, which completely wrote off the classic car, was deemed a precautionary measure despite no injuries.

Google is setting up a four-person team to improve battery technology for phones, tablets, and electric cars, according to reports. The team works on flexible and wearable battery technologies, including solid-state, thin-film batteries for smartphones and implantable devices. Google began working on similar projects in 2012, led by former Apple battery expert Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj. Google also collaborates with AllCell Technologies to develop batteries for subfreezing temperatures, crucial for Project Loon balloons.

The 223ft Explorer, a superyacht designed by Tony Castro, comes with a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests, a helipad, helicopter storage, and submarine. It costs approximately 40 million euros to build and is intended for ultra-wealthy individuals. The yacht also features a large carrying capacity for toys and tenders, including a climate-controlled garage for a helicopter.

Labour leader Ed Miliband pressed ahead with controversial rent controls despite warnings from experts, who said the plans would slash investment in new housing and lead to more evictions, while Labour's own Generation Rent campaign group criticized the proposals as having loopholes.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter, Ryan Dearnley, was removed from his role as a Reading mascot for the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after a video surfaced showing him wishing Arsenal would win. This angered Reading fans, leading to a poll showing 85% of readers wanted him removed. The Football Association moved him away from the match to avoid a negative reception and offered him an England mascot role instead.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across, roughly spherical and possibly containing a substructure, may explain the mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, a 20% less dense region first discovered in 2004. If confirmed, this would be the largest single structure ever found by humanity, potentially caused by the void 'sapping' the energy of passing light, leading to a colder temperature.

The red, worn chair where Abraham Lincoln was shot in 1865 at Ford's Theatre in Washington D.C. will be displayed at the Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, on April 15 for the 150th anniversary of the assassination, following a 15-day open display. Historians say the dark stain on the chair's back is from oil, not blood, but many visitors believe it to be from Lincoln's injuries.

A 19-year-old boyfriend from Hailsham, Jake Boys, surprised his 18-year-old girlfriend Emily Canham with One Direction tickets for a Cardiff gig but booked flights to Dublin, mistaking the Welsh capital for the Republic of Ireland. Emily tweeted her dismay, and Jake is now planning to buy new train tickets.

Romanian company MB Telecom unveiled the Roboscan 2M Aeria, a mobile X-ray scanner capable of detecting contraband, bombs, and weapons inside planes. The device, costing €3 million, can scan entire small to medium-sized aircraft in about 20 minutes, addressing a gap in security at low-security airports. While currently not safe for passengers, it is being used to inspect trucks at borders in Eastern Europe, where it has helped seize 76,000 packs of illegal cigarettes.

A predatory convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, 54, with an obsession for young girls, went on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit near Hook, Hampshire. Last seen leaving the Winchfield hospital on Tuesday, Munden, who suffers from learning difficulties, was detained under the Mental Health Act for sexually touching a three-year-old girl. Officers launched a manhunt, releasing images of him with both facial hair and a clean-shaven face, as he may have shaved off his beard.

Middlesbrough lead the Championship with four weeks to go, seven points ahead of second-placed Bournemouth, who have won just one of their last seven matches. With a lunchtime kick-off against Watford on Monday, Boro's victory could secure their promotion, while Watford and Norwich face crucial matches against Bournemouth and Birmingham, respectively.

The #grannyhair trend gained popularity on social media, with women posting images of their silver locks under the hashtag. Instagram users shared photos of models and celebrities like Rihanna, Lady Gaga, and Nicole Richie embracing grey hair, viewing it as a feminist statement and a departure from traditional hair dyeing.

Randy and Jodi Speidel, a down-on-their-luck couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, struggling with chronic conditions, were found dead from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning in their bedroom, two months after creating online fundraisers on GiveForward.com and GoFundMe.com, which failed to attract any donations.

Liberal Democrats leader Nick Clegg vowed to remain party leader despite potential electoral losses, stating he would fight for his job 'in all circumstances.' Clegg emphasized his optimism for the party's prospects, warning of a risk to the country's economic recovery if Labour and Conservative parties move away from the center ground. He also hinted at a possible coalition with the Conservatives, saying he deserved credit for forming the Coalition while enduring criticism from the Labour Party.

A 79-year-old pensioner Terry Cooper was saved from a badger attack by his Jack Russell dog Sam, which dragged him back indoors after the huge badger, about the size of a pig, burst through a hedge with two cubs. The National Farmers' Union advised residents to protect their properties from badgers, citing gaps in fencing as a common entry point.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose 3-0 to Porto U21s at Fulham's training ground on Wednesday, avoiding Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final against Atletico Madrid. Mourinho was joined by his son Jose Junior, who plays for Fulham. Chelsea, who were knocked out of the Champions League, are closing in on their first Premier League title since 2010.

Andreas Christopheros, 29, was critically injured when corrosive liquid was thrown in his face outside his home in Truro, Cornwall. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, was charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court. David Phillips, her husband, was charged with grievous bodily harm with intent. Christopheros, a property developer, lost vision and suffered facial scars after the December attack.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has posted signs warning visitors not to defecate along the famous path, drawing both complaints from residents and amusement from some pilgrims. The signs, showing a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line, have become an attraction as some pilgrims pose for photos with them. Residents of Lastres, a parish in Santos, have complained about defecation outside their homes, while others note that pilgrims are generally polite and friendly.

A massive fire engulfed a building formerly housing a strip club, The Body Shop, in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon, starting around 1pm. Only the building and a few nearby power lines were affected, according to local media. The blaze is under investigation.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent, Shoshana Hebshi, reached a $40,000 settlement in a lawsuit after being strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport on the 10th anniversary of 9/11. The federal government, Frontier Airlines, the Transportation Security Administration, and Wayne County Airport Authority were named in the lawsuit. Hebshi, who was detained for hours, said she was ethnically profiled based on her dark complexion.

Twenty people were injured after an Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 made a crash landing and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, believed to have missed the landing point on the runway and spun 180 degrees after impact. The Airbus A320 had departed from Incheon International Airport in Seoul, and emergency services were at the scene, with injured passengers taken to hospital. The airport was closed as a result.

Made In Chelsea star Mark-Francis Vandelli, son of a multimillionaire, revealed his extensive watch collection, featuring 16 expensive timepieces worth several thousand pounds. He buys a new watch each year, including a £32,000 Cartier Moonphase and a £6,500 Bulgari Chrono 42, showcasing his taste and wealth.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his £100,000 antiques collection, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt and a longbow, in an auction of 238 lots at Dominic Winter auctioneers in Gloucestershire. Hardy, 89, is downsizing his home and studying medieval history, collecting items like books, furniture, and swords.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook criticizing a scene he witnessed on a train platform, expressing his disapproval of conservative attitudes. The image, which appeared to be a homophobic rant, was later revealed to be a spoof of public safety regulations. Felippe's post went viral, receiving thousands of comments praising his witty approach to combating homophobia.

A young English cricket fan named Jonathan Stevenson, aged 16, wrote to Richie Benaud, a legendary Australian cricket spin bowler, in 1996 for tips on left-handed leg spin. Benaud, who had a remarkable Test career, responded with a detailed letter and notes, including coaching advice for left-handers. Stevenson shared Benaud's response on Twitter as a tribute to the "great man" after Benaud's death.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicted the future of travel will involve sharing virtual reality environments, allowing users to experience world locations from multiple viewpoints. Facebook plans to support virtual reality on its newsfeed and film videos with multiple cameras to enable users to change their viewpoints, mimicking real-world exploration. Marriott hotels have already tested Oculus Rift for virtual tours.

A bedridden girlfriend, 22, with bone cancer wished to have her wedding photographs taken on her 22nd birthday. Guo Kai, her boyfriend, arranged for professional photographers to visit her hospital bed in Sichuan, China, despite their formal marriage being postponed due to her illness. They posed together, with Guo giving her a bouquet of red roses, and exchanged rings, marking a romantic gesture in her hospital room.

Police in Houston charged 34-year-old Blaine Boudreaux with intoxication manslaughter and other charges after he caused at least three separate DUI crashes within three hours, killing 6-year-old Joshua Medrano, injuring his mother, and killing a homeless man. Boudreaux, with a history of DUIs, was arrested after the first crash and later dozed off, leading to a fatal hit-and-run on a pedestrian.

Microsoft announced a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond campus in Washington, partnering with Specialisterne, a nonprofit that trains autistic individuals for IT careers. Mary Ellen Smith, Microsoft's Corporate VP of Worldwide Operations and mother of an autistic son, made the announcement. Last year, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella apologized for saying women should trust the system to pay them well, highlighting the company's focus on diversity.

Two deputies in Tulsa, Oklahoma, involved in the fatal arrest of Eric Harris were reassigned due to threats against them and their families. Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris during an attempt to arrest him, leading to criticism for his actions. Bates is charged with second-degree manslaughter, while Sheriff Stanley Glanz apologized to Harris' family but defended the department's standards.

Katie Prager, 24, diagnosed with cystic fibrosis and Burkholderia cepacia infection, needs a lung transplant but her Kentucky Medicaid insurance will not cover the $1 million out-of-state treatment at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Her husband Dalton, who received a lung transplant, pleaded for help as Katie's health declines, stating she is running out of options and facing a life-threatening situation.

From a Sleep Cycle app study, South Africans wake up earliest on Mondays at 6:09 am, while Americans rise at 7 am on Tuesdays, the worst mood day of the week. Slovakia had the best sleep quality, with 58% of countries reporting the best sleep on Wednesdays, including the US. Americans sleep the latest on Fridays at 8:24 am, waking up happiest.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo, married to Diego Rivera, wrote 25 passionate love letters to Jose Bartoli from 1946 to 1949, which are expected to fetch up to $120,000 at auction in April. The letters, saved by Jose until his death in 1995, reveal Kahlo's secret romance and her relationship with Diego, including her pregnancy and feelings for Jose.

Trade union leader Len McCluskey, head of Unite, campaigned for Labour in Wales with a warm demeanor but wielded significant influence, including 1.42 million members, potentially dragging Britain back to 1970s-style socialism. His union's ties to Labour's structure and finances raise concerns about potential disastrous governance, despite his calls for more radical policies.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz filmed 30 hours of animals drinking water using a GoPro camera at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv. He captured unique perspectives, from a rhino almost kissing the water to a lemur delicately licking it. Some animals initially sceptical, but eventually adapted, with lions drinking aggressively and zebras humorously bare-teethed.

A poll reveals that only 25% of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, compared to 43% who believe Ed Miliband is most up for the fight. Despite criticism of a dull campaign, Cameron insisted he was working "bloody hard" to secure a majority, while voters perceive Miliband as more enthusiastic about the contest.

A man charged with assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov, Zaur Dadaev, told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Initially confessing in March, Dadaev later retracted his confession, claiming he was abducted and tortured. Four other Chechen men are also accused of the killing, which occurred on a bridge near the Kremlin in February, sparking a protest march of over 20,000 people.

A 4-month-old baby named Sonit Awal was pulled from under the rubble of the Nepal earthquake, becoming the defining image of the disaster that killed over 5,000 people. Sonit was buried alive for 22 hours in Muldhoka, Bhaktapur, until rescuers found him on Sunday morning, his eyes still closed, and he was uninjured.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narconon, is trying to have a 40-acre property near Camp David, Maryland, designated as historic to build a drug rehab center. The property, previously bought by a Scientology-backed real estate company, is currently zoned for resource conservation and cannot be used for medical purposes. Narconon claims the site has historic significance due to President Herbert Hoover's visit, while opponents argue it is a tactic to circumvent zoning laws and create a potentially dangerous program.

In Kabul, Afghanistan, five English-speaking former NATO workers, fired and blacklisted, face isolation and fear as the city swells with returning Afghans, now unemployed and wary of the U.S. presence. Violence in the provinces and security warnings have emptied many Western-owned businesses, leaving streets littered with abandoned vehicles and equipment from America's longest war.

One US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured on Friday during pool training at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia. The two SEALs, assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two, were swimming in lap lanes without gear when they were found at the bottom of the pool. Navy spokesman Lt. David Lloyd said they were working out, not diving. Both were taken to a civilian hospital; the critically injured SEAL is listed in critical condition.

NBC expects to have more people watching Premier League matches live in the USA than in Britain in one season. In 2012-13, 13 million Americans watched at least one top-flight game, rising to 32 million last season. NBC moved its entire production to England this weekend, where star anchor Rebecca Lowe, former USA midfielder Kyle Martino, and Robbie Earle provided coverage, including the Burnley vs Arsenal match.

Boris Johnson, appearing on the Andrew Marr Show, attacked Ed Miliband, accusing him of potentially betraying the country by forming a deal with the SNP. Johnson claimed Labour could not govern without SNP support, likening Miliband to a "monkey crouching on his back," while Miliband dismissed the attack, saying Johnson was "better than that."

A prisoner in Oregon, Dustin Irons, flashed a judge during a video court hearing, leading to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court. Despite being handcuffed, Irons, who has been in prison since December for assault and mischief, exposed himself to the judge, angering the court. The incident occurred at Umatilla County Corrections Center, and Irons faces another disciplinary investigation.

McLaren driver Jenson Button believes his team has made significant progress since starting the Formula One season poorly in Australia, racing competitively alongside midfield cars in Malaysia. Button hopes this momentum will help McLaren challenge Red Bull and other top teams in this weekend's Chinese Grand Prix.

A hospital in Western Australia, Fiona Stanley Hospital, was found to have blood and bone fragments on medical instruments after failing to return sterilizing equipment by February, leading to its medical service provider, Serco, being fined $60,000. Australian Medical Association WA president Michael Gannon reported that some instruments contained blood and human matter, damaging the hospital's public image and morale.

Becca Litchfield, 29, and her partner Dale, 30, from Nottingham, chose to have IVF treatment instead of a wedding, spending £5,500 on two failed rounds. They won a wedding competition and later gave birth to twins Darci-Mai and Stanley, achieving both their dreams of a family and a wedding.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email, locking out staff for almost 24 hours. The hacker posted adult cartoons instead of usual images, similar to what happened to Delta Air Lines and Crayola. Scooter's Coffee apologized, saying they were only able to regain control of the page after contacting larger businesses, who then removed the inappropriate content.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center caused amusement by attempting to bark at a husky, making high-pitched squeaks and yappy barks, causing the husky to whine and other onlookers to laugh. The puppies, around 7-8 weeks old, vocalized more intensely as they conversed, with the Shibu Inu eventually running to get closer to the husky.

England seamer Liam Plunkett, back in Test contention after a minor ankle complaint, aims to use his pace to lead England against the West Indies. He played 18 wickets in four Tests last summer and is fighting for a spot in the first Test in Antigua, competing with Chris Jordan and uncapped Mark Wood.

Paul Smith, having lost to Arthur Abraham twice, faces a third fight against Andre Ward, a reigning world champion, in Oakland, California. Smith, a Liverpool boxer, is seen as a warm-up opponent for Ward, who wants to avoid a rematch with Carl Froch. The bout is part of the WBA's plan to unify the super-middleweight titles, with Ward scheduled to fight Froch in London, though Froch prefers to stay in the UK.

Residents of Parma, Missouri, were shocked when five of its six police officers and several top officials resigned after the city's first black mayor, Tyrus Byrd, was elected. The officials cited 'safety concerns' in their resignations, leaving Byrd to find replacements for the city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor. The community, which is 41% black, 57% white, and has 713 residents, has faced recent break-ins, prompting residents to rally behind Byrd.

Yaya Toure will not be forced out of Manchester City but the club will make him available this summer. Sportsmail reported City will listen to offers, though Toure is content at the club and unlikely to leave due to his wages. Inter Milan is interested but doubts exist over a potential move. City will resist Valencia's attempt to block a £24m deal for Alvaro Negredo, who has scored only five goals for Valencia since joining on loan.

More than two-thirds (69%) of people taking antidepressants in the U.S. did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder, according to a study. The research found 38% did not meet criteria for other psychiatric disorders like obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, or generalised anxiety disorder. SSRIs, commonly prescribed antidepressants, are used in the absence of clear evidence-based indications, a study in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry concluded.

Doris Fuller, mother of Natalie, 28, who killed herself in Baltimore, Maryland, revealed her daughter's struggle with undiagnosed bipolar disorder and psychosis. Natalie's condition worsened, leading to her death, and Fuller wrote about how her illness, untreated until her 20s, drove her daughter to suicide. Fuller described Natalie as the bravest person she had ever known, despite her struggles.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest during a British Bulldog game at his school playground, collapsing and losing consciousness for 12 minutes. His heart stopped pumping blood, and he was revived by CPR from teachers and defibrillation by paramedics, who later diagnosed him with a condition similar to that of footballer Fabrice Muamba.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, called for divorce laws in England and Wales to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame, aiming to reduce marital disputes' bitterness. Current laws require couples to cite one of five reasons for divorce, with unreasonable behavior being the most common. Hale proposed a one-year cooling-off period before divorce and encouraged couples to resolve arrangements for children and money before obtaining a divorce.

Tottenham are considering a £400 million stadium with a retractable pitch to host a new NFL London franchise, potentially sharing the venue with up to 70 NFL players. The new stadium, due for completion in 2018, could be better suited for American football than Wembley, which hosts NFL games but lacks the artificial pitch beneath a moveable grass surface.

U.S. senators, including John McCain and Robert Menendez, wrote to FIFA urging Russia's removal as 2018 World Cup host due to its involvement in the Ukraine crisis and Crimea occupation. They argue this would condemn Putin's regime and reduce economic support. England is considering a bid for Euro 2028 but unlikely for 2026 World Cup, as the FA has decided not to bid while Blatter remains president.

Universal announced "Fifty Shades Darker" sequel will release on Feb. 10, 2017, with husband of author EL James, Niall Leonard, writing the script. The second film, "Fifty Shades Freed," is set for Feb. 9, 2018. Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan are negotiating higher pay for the sequel after the first film's $568.8 million worldwide earnings. Sam Taylor-Johnson, who directed the first film, is not returning.

West Brom manager Tony Pulis, 57, faces a challenging return to Crystal Palace after seven seasons in the Premier League, where he has never finished higher than 11th. Despite his success at Stoke City and Palace, Pulis has not led any team into the top half, and his current West Bromwich Albion team is stuck on 33 points, with four tough final fixtures.

Fenerbahce called for a championship suspension after a gun attack on their team bus during a Super Lig match in Turkey, injuring the driver and damaging the vehicle. The attack occurred on the way back to Istanbul from Rize, following a 5-1 win.

A massive avalanche hit Everest Base Camp, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens in Nepal's earthquake, with 4,300+ people dead overall. The quake struck Saturday, causing climbers to flee, and helicopters rescued those stranded in higher camps. The Khumbu Icefall, damaged by aftershocks, complicates rescue efforts.

87-year-old Gregory Margolin, a WWII Jewish veteran, found himself in another war in Ukraine. He fought as a sniper and rose to command, but Alzheimer's now hampers his memory. After a missile attack in Donetsk, he and his family fled to Israel, fearing another war. Margolin, among 600 Ukrainian Jews brought to Israel by the International Fellowship of Christians and Jews, now lives in the quietest place for him.

John Carver, now fighting for the Newcastle head coach position, faces a daunting challenge in a Tyne-Wear derby against Sunderland, recalling how former manager Ruud Gullit's controversial selection in 1999 led to his dismissal after a 2-1 loss. Carver knows a victory could bolster his chances, while a defeat might jeopardize his future at the club.

Revered Al Sharpton appeared in North Charleston on Sunday, addressing the Walter Scott case and police reform, alongside elected officials and police. Sharpton praised Mayor Keith Summey for firing officer Michael Slager, who killed Scott, and called for a new tone in policing across the US.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the winger was caught smoking a shisha pipe and allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide before scoring the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Rodgers said Sterling faces a club investigation and potential disciplinary action, and will speak to the 20-year-old about professionalism. Sterling, who could have scored a second goal, expressed disappointment at not getting a hat-trick.

Labour received £1.1 million in donations from unions in the second week of the election campaign, more than twice as much as the £492,512 received by the Conservatives. Unions like Unison and Unite gave over £700,000 to Labour, while the Conservatives received most of their donations from wealthy individuals, with Christopher Rokos contributing £170,000. Labour's union donations equate to £1.22 per second, compared to £0.38 for the Lib Dems and £0.08 for Ukip.

Police were called twice to a Qatar Airways flight diverted to Birmingham Airport due to severe winds, where passengers became disruptive after being stranded for five hours. Some passengers were left waiting for transport to Manchester, causing further delays, while a Qatar Airways spokeswoman apologized for the delay, stating it was due to crew exceeding flying hours.

Canadian pop star Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring for his $300 million Las Vegas fight against Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. The two have been close friends for years, with Bieber accompanying Mayweather on numerous occasions. Bieber confirmed he will be part of Mayweather's entourage, despite earlier reports suggesting he would only accompany Mayweather into the ring.

Corinthian Colleges Inc., once enrolling over 70,000 students, announced it would shut down all 28 campuses, marking a positive step in holding for-profit colleges accountable. These schools, which often offer dubious degrees and high debt, received 86% of their funding from federal student loans, leading to nearly half of all student loan defaults. Corinthian's closure follows a Department of Education ban on federal aid, and hundreds of its graduates have joined a debt strike, with Education Secretary Arne Duncan signaling potential loan forgiveness for those with no job prospects.

Bayern Munich boss Pep Guardiola denied a dispute with former doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after the Champions League quarter-final defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the medical staff was blamed for the loss, citing a damaged bond of trust. Guardiola blamed himself for the defeat, attributing it to a lack of available players, despite having 30 operations among his players in the past two years.

Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, 39, will defend his world titles against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden in New York, recalling his Olympic gold win in 1996 that catapulted him into Ukrainian hero status. Klitschko, now a year short of 40, has maintained his dominance, believing age is an advantage, and is preparing for his first US title defense in seven years.

Jeremy Clarkson, 54, has finally spoken out about his sacking from Top Gear, admitting he will 'miss' fronting the BBC2 show after being fired in March for attacking a producer. Former presenter Angela Rippon, 70, said she would be keen to return if invited back, while Clarkson thanked supporters but noted he would 'miss being there'.

Barcelona striker Fabian Orellana was shown a red card and struck in the neck by a lump of grass thrown at him by Sergio Busquets during a La Liga match against Celta Vigo, leading to Busquets' red card. The incident occurred in the closing stages of a 1-0 Barcelona victory, despite Real Madrid's 9-1 win earlier.

In 2013, a pair of bombs exploded at the Boston Marathon finish line, killing three and injuring over 200; Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was convicted in 2015 for the bombings. Federal Judge George A. O'Toole warned a jury beginning the sentencing phase of Tsarnaev's case not to attend the 2013 Boston Marathon or related events, due to start April 21.

Millions of Chinese people marked the Qingming Festival by traveling home to ancestral villages, honoring deceased family members with tomb cleaning, burning paper money, and leaving offerings. A grand ceremony was held in Shaanxi Province in honor of the Yellow Emperor Huangdi, considered the founding father of the Chinese nation. The three-day festival, celebrated on the first week of April, includes outdoor celebrations and parades across China.

Paul Simon, 73, returned to the UK album chart's top spot with "The Ultimate Collection," his first since 1990, outselling albums by younger artists like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. His recent tour with Sting is believed to have contributed to the success of his greatest hits record, which includes hits from his 50-year career, including "Mrs. Robinson" and "The Only Living Boy in New York."

Iker Casillas, Real Madrid's longtime goalkeeper, insists he will stay at the Bernabeu until his contract ends, despite David de Gea's transfer to Manchester United, claiming he will fight for the starting position. Casillas, 33, has been at Real Madrid since 1996 and hopes to fulfill his commitment until the end of the season, focusing on defending the Champions League title.

Britain saw its highest employment level in history, with 31 million people in work, according to official figures. Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy won praise from the International Monetary Fund, with Rolls-Royce announcing a £6 billion order for Emirates. IMF chief Christine Lagarde and German finance minister Wolfgang Schaeuble endorsed Osborne's 'wonderful job' of managing the economy, reducing the deficit significantly.

Korea's SsangYong is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli, priced from under £13,000, aimed at frugal drivers.
