The Tivoli, with engines ranging from 1.6 litre petrol and diesel, offers features like six-speed manual and automatic transmissions, seven airbags, and a choice of front-wheel drive or 4x4. It comes in three trim levels with SE, EX, and ELX options, priced from £12,950 to £19,000. SsangYong expects the Tivoli to double its UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 annually. Meanwhile, Citroen's Aircross, inspired by tough Tonka toys, features protective alloy bumps for added durability.

A chef named Sam Longhurst created a 10-inch tall, half-kilogram burger at Splendid Kitchen in Manchester, containing six forms of three different meats totaling 2,000 calories. The burger includes two beef patties, ham chunks, a whole fried chicken thigh, barbecued pulled pork, and bacon, described as a "monster of a burger" by the chef. The dish was created after a customer challenged the restaurant to make a burger with three types of meat.

Yeo Valley, a yogurt maker, offers a Michelin-starred staff canteen with organic, locally sourced meals for as little as £2, including dishes like soft-poached quail egg and confit of tomato, overlooking the Blagdon countryside in North Somerset. The canteen, run by executive chef Paul Collins, serves 120 dairy workers and has been praised as the world's best staff canteen, now open to the public at higher prices.

Legendary blues musician B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration due to Type II diabetes, but he was "much better" and back home with his grandchildren, according to his daughter. King, 89, had previously canceled his tour in 2022 after a similar incident.

Manhattan's Fifth Avenue was adorned with bizarre Easter hats as thousands participated in the annual parade, featuring everything from simple bunny ears to elaborate dioramas inspired by Mayor Bill de Blasio. The event included various religious groups, with some churchgoers wearing more conservative clothing, while others opted for more flamboyant designs.

Emergency crews in Essex dispatched two ambulances to Epping Forest after a caller reported a squirrel had been run over, only to discover the "victim" was a person. The East of England ambulance service has released a list of 1,248 "bizarre and irritating" calls, with front-line crews responding to almost half, potentially endangering lives. Calls included a man claiming his burger was bleeding, a woman saying she was locked out, and a man reporting lethargy after dieting.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake won a head-to-head challenge against teammates Loic Remy and Willian in an Audi-sponsored football competition, scoring 6-0 in the final round. However, Willian accidentally broke the wing mirror of an Audi while attempting a long-range shot, causing a humorous mishap.

Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, after Sterling rejected a £100,000-a-week contract extension and said Arsenal was interested. Rodgers said he had sat with Sterling, advising him to stay at Liverpool, despite the player's two-year deal expiring. Rodgers defended Liverpool as the best place for Sterling's development, noting he enjoys playing for the club.

Countdown host Nick Hewer struggled to keep laughing during an episode when contestants offered the eight-letter word 'erection' as a word game answer, embarrassing co-presenter Rachel Riley. This incident followed similar mishaps, including 'todgers' from Hairy Biker Dave Myers and 'm*nges' from an English teacher, in the 26-year-old show's history.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who tried to buy deadly poison on the dark web was spared jail after pleading guilty at Manchester Youth Court. The teenager, unaware his online requests were being tracked by anti-terror officers, expressed a desire to commit suicide. Officers raided his homes and arrested him in February, but he was sentenced to a 12-month referral order instead.

Three hours after giving birth to her baby girl, 37-year-old Lianne Hindle, a mother-of-four, died at North Manchester General Hospital, where three babies and one mother had died in the previous eight months. Ms Hindle, who was 35 weeks pregnant, suffered a cardiac arrest after being taken to the hospital instead of her scheduled hospital. Her family called for action to prevent further tragedies, citing concerns about the care she received, including being left alone with a student midwife.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after posting a video of herself training while eight months pregnant. The 32-year-old, who had previously given birth to son Cornelis in 2006, plans to compete in the 2016 Rio Olympics and Beijing World Championships. Emily was born at a healthy 3.1 kilograms on Monday.

At least one person died and four were missing after a powerful storm capsized several sailboats in the Dauphin Island Regatta in Mobile Bay, Alabama. The storm, which hit around 4 p.m., caused widespread damage and loss of life, with crews searching for missing individuals into the night. Mayor Jeff Collier confirmed at least one death, and the mayor reported scattered boats from Dauphin Island Bridge to Fort Morgan.

Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, eye diseases that can lead to vision loss. Doctors have not provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening, with macular degeneration affecting central vision and glaucoma peripheral vision. Barr uses marijuana to relieve glaucoma pressure, though the combination of both diseases is unusual but not unheard of.

An Oklahoma jury convicted 17-year-old Chancey Allen Luna of first-degree murder for shooting and killing Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane during a jog in Duncan, Oklahoma, in 2013. The jury recommended life in prison without parole, despite defense claims that Luna meant only to scare Lane. Luna did not testify, and his mother testified he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger insists his 12-0-7 record against Jose Mourinho will not affect their top-of-the-table clash with Chelsea at the Emirates on Sunday. Wenger, who lost 2-0 to Mourinho's Chelsea in October, says the result will be decided by performance, not past history. The game features former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas returning to the Emirates for Chelsea for the first time. Wenger emphasizes the importance of the match, despite Chelsea's 10-point lead, and hopes to nullify Chelsea's strengths in counter attacks and set pieces.

Manny Pacquiao, now 36, has become a global boxing icon after mega-fights against notable opponents like Oscar De La Hoya and Juan Manuel Marquez. He rose from poverty in the Philippines, fighting in the Far East before his breakthrough in 2001 against Lehlo Ledwaba in Las Vegas. Pacquiao is set to face Floyd Mayweather in the "Fight of the Century" on the Las Vegas Strip, a chance to avenge a 2008 loss.

Jack Grealish, a top flight footballer, was photographed using nitrous oxide, a legal but banned substance, during Aston Villa's FA Cup semi-final win against Liverpool at Wembley. This incident, seen as a drug use, may help keep Grealish grounded as he becomes a prominent player.

Sam Barton, who underwent £55,000 of cosmetic surgery, was attacked with eggs by a group of men on Easter Monday in Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands, after checking in at a pub on Facebook. The 22-year-old believes the attackers tracked him down online, targeting his appearance. He had previously moved houses due to online abuse.

An Indiana university was on lockdown after receiving a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the administration building, leading to police and bomb squad response. The university advised students to shelter in place, but no injuries were confirmed.

Luis Suarez and Edinson Cavani will face off in the Champions League quarter-final as Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain compete. Cavani, known as El Matador, faces pressure to break through Barcelona's defense after PSG lost key players Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Veratti. Cavani has struggled with a goal drought, missing seven matches, and was involved in a controversial altercation with coach Laurent Blanc.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title by unanimous decision over Tony Luis in Liverpool, after Richar Abril and Ismael Barroso pulled out due to illness or visa issues. Mathews, who threw a right punch and landed an uppercut, saw Luis come forward aggressively but ultimately lost a tight 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 decision.

Hull KR beat St Helens 28-20 at Langtree Park, surprising the home side who had lost to rivals Wigan and were injury-hit. Jamie Shaul scored the winning try for Hull, while Saints nearly equalized through Louie McCarthy-Scarsbrook but failed to convert a potential try.

By 2023, the documented and undocumented immigrant population in the United States could reach 14.8% of the population, with immigrants accounting for 82% of all population growth by 2060, according to a report from the Center for Immigration Studies. This growth could mean one in five U.S. residents will be an immigrant by 2060, with immigration population growing almost four times faster than the native-born population.

Jack Wilshere made his return from injury as captain for Arsenal Under 21s, but the team lost 1-0 to Reading's youngsters at the Emirates Stadium. Former Arsenal defender Martin Keown's son Niall scored the only goal in the 8th minute, and Wilshere, along with long-term absentee Abou Diaby, managed to play despite injuries.

English golfer Justin Rose, struggling with form after three missed cuts and a 55th-place finish, improved significantly with a 69 at the Shell Houston Open, hitting 17 out of 18 greens. Rose, who has been in the world's top five for three years, attributes his turnaround to correcting faults in his swing and putting, aiming to regain his form for the Masters.

A mansion in Mayfair, London, that was once a milking parlour for cows has gone on the market for £25 million. Originally a commercial depot, the site was demolished in the 19th century and rebuilt as a modern luxury home with features like an indoor swimming pool, cinema room, and lift. The property, 8,139 square feet, now includes four bedrooms and a dining room that can seat 14.

Bayern Munich, without key players Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba, showed unity in recent games against Dortmund and Leverkusen, scoring 3-0 against Eintracht Frankfurt. Coach Pep Guardiola expects strong performances from Muller and Lewandowski in the Champions League quarter-final against Porto, despite injuries. Porto, twice winners, advanced to the round of 16 with an open game style and physical midfielders.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes team-mates, visited Mercedes' Brackley base after Sebastian Vettel beat them and Ferrari at the Malaysian Grand Prix. Vettel won by 8.5 seconds, with Hamilton four seconds behind and Rosberg another four behind. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff was surprised by Vettel's victory, citing Ferrari's better tyre management in the heat.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection is deemed unconstitutional or unavailable. The gas causes unconsciousness within 8-10 seconds and death from lack of oxygen, according to supporters. Critics, including the Death Penalty Information Center's Robert Dunham, argue this mirrors past hasty execution methods in Oklahoma. The state has been on hold for executions while the U.S. Supreme Court reviews lethal injection methods.

Swansea's Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in a 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday, topping this week's EA Sports' Performance Index with a Game Index score of 52.9 after scoring four goals in six Premier League games. Charlie Austin of Queens Park Rangers was runner-up with a score of 52.2 after scoring and assisting in a 4-1 win against West Brom.

A Russian freezer trawler, carrying 132 crew members, sank in the Sea of Okhotsk off the Kamchatka Peninsula, killing at least 56 crew members in 15 minutes. A massive rescue operation involving over 1,300 people is underway, with 63 survivors rescued and 13 still missing. Temperatures in the water can drop to -2°C, leading to hypothermia deaths.

Men with advanced prostate cancer could benefit from a drug originally used for women, as clinical trials show olaparib delays disease progression. The drug, already effective for women with BRCA gene mutations, helped 16 out of 49 men in a London trial, extending disease control for many longer than expected. Olaparib is the first cancer drug targeting inherited genetic mutations, and its approval for ovarian cancer opens new possibilities for prostate cancer treatment.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, turned her photography skills into a business by launching 'In Bed With', a website that reviews luxurious hotels worldwide. With over 12,000 Instagram followers, she documents the best beds, pools, and room service, earning income from both hotel stays and professional photos. Taylor has stayed at exclusive properties like the Mineral Springs Hotel in Australia and Than Sanctuary in Bali, generating income from featured hotels and travel product companies.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was thrown into the air and dragged along the surface of water in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, South Africa, after getting caught in a fight between two adult males. The calf's mother, who stayed with her herd, watched helplessly as the attack occurred, and the baby died hours later. Tour operator Stacey Farrell witnessed the incident.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea after a cigarette lighter thrown by home supporters struck Branislav Ivanovic on the head during a Chelsea 1-0 victory at Loftus Road. QPR unlikely to face disciplinary action but will review CCTV and ban those involved. Chelsea players celebrated the win, but the match was marred by objects thrown from the crowd. QPR promises to ban those responsible and appeal to witnesses.

A young mother and her three children, LaTasha Gosling, 27, and her daughters Janyaa, 4, and Jenika, 8, and her son Landen, 7, were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect, a man who lived with the family, was found dead hours later, but his cause of death was not specified. The victim's sister described the family as 'very, very devastating' and the community has started a GoFundMe page to help with funeral costs.

Labour politician Emily Thornberry, who opposed right-to-buy for council tenants, was criticized for renting a housing association property worth almost £1 million, highlighting her hypocrisy. Thornberry, who lives in a £3 million home, previously lost her frontbench job for a tweet mocking a council property.

Police dropped an investigation into a January 24 assault on Mike Lane, 40, a huntsman, by protesters armed with iron bars, despite evidence and a video. Lane, beaten and hospitalized, said police could have made more effort; the case was shelved pending further information, angering Lane and supporters.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer, despite being linked with Manchester United and Chelsea. Gomes, who has scored four goals in 25 La Liga appearances since joining from Benfica, says he is happy at Valencia and denies being contacted by Chelsea.

Australian teenager Audrey Pekin, 19, alleged she was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali by Henry Alafu, who had met her earlier. Alafu lured her to his remote home and then attacked her in a taxi as she tried to flee. Despite her illness, she felt unwell during the taxi ride and was unable to escape. Alafu followed her and allegedly raped her again in the taxi. Indonesian police failed to prevent Alafu from escaping back to Nigeria.

Former Made in Chelsea star Ashley James posed with a fake skinned fox to protest Harvey Nichols' reintroduction of fur products, joining animal rights group PETA in a campaign against the department store's ten-year anti-fur policy. Harvey Nichols, which previously banned fur, now sells products including coyote fur, raccoon fur, and rabbit pelts, prompting James to urge customers to question the authenticity of fur items and make informed purchasing decisions.

Chile enacted a new law recognizing civil unions between same-sex couples, becoming the latest South American country to allow such unions, following Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay. The law, signed by President Michelle Bachelet, will take effect in six months and grants legal recognition to cohabiting relationships, including those between men and women, ending discrimination faced by common-law couples. Around 2 million Chileans are estimated to benefit from the change in rights and privileges.

Chelsea are on track to break the Premier League record for most days at the top of the table in a single season, currently leading for 230 days since August 30, 2022, with a potential 12-day margin to surpass Manchester United's record of 262 days from the 1993/94 season.

Cape Verde, a small island nation with 500,000 people, seeks to leverage its rich musical heritage to boost its economy, which lacks conventional natural resources. The country's cultural diversity, shaped by the transatlantic slave trade and pirate history, has produced unique musical styles like batuque and morna. Prime Minister Jose Maria Neves and the ministry of culture support this strategy, aiming to transform music and culture into a key sector for economic growth. The Kriol Jazz Festival, celebrating its seventh year, attracts international artists and has become a major event in Cape Verde, contributing to the country's cultural identity and tourism.

A hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of Sydney's Opera House trended on social media again, following heavy storms. Originally posted by Sydney resident Darren Johnson in June 2012, the video was quickly retweeted by popular radio duo Fitzy and Wippa. Skeptics noted inaccuracies, including rocks around the Opera House and a cardboard-like appearance of the surfer, while wave experts dismissed it as impossible.

Reading lost to Birmingham 1-0 in a Sky Bet Championship match at the Madejski Stadium, with Clayton Donaldson scoring the winner in the 87th minute. Reading dominated the first half but failed to capitalize on several chances, while Birmingham held firm defensively.

French champions Paris Saint-Germain suffered a major setback as David Luiz, a key defender, suffered a hamstring injury during a match against Marseille, likely missing both legs of their Champions League quarter-final against Barcelona for at least four weeks.

The return of Game of Thrones sparked a surge in internet piracy, with fans making over 100,000 illegal downloads per day. More than seven million episodes from seasons one to four were illegally downloaded between February and April, up 45% year-on-year. Brazil led illegal downloads, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO launched a new streaming service, HBO Now, to curb piracy and recapture revenue, though it is only available in the US.

Leicester City, fighting for survival, face West Ham United at King Power Stadium on Saturday. Leicester loses Matt Upson and Jeff Schlupp due to injury, while West Ham welcomes back Winston Reid from injury. Leicester's squad includes Schlupp, Albrighton, and Mahrez, while West Ham's squad features Song, Amalfitano, and Kouyate. The teams have met 82 times, with West Ham winning 51 and Leicester 39. Leicester has not won at home in 10 Premier League matches, and West Ham has not won away in 7 games.

Residents of Celoron, N.Y., have protested a statue of Lucile Ball, the hometown icon, since 2009, criticizing its unflattering depiction of the actress as unrecognizable from her beloved TV character. The statue, based on Ball's drunken pitch for a health tonic, has sparked a Facebook page with over 600 likes, calling for its removal. Artist Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has declined to comment, while locals argue it should be replaced due to its perceived monstrous appearance.

A 43-year-old woman from Halesowen, West Midlands, Sharon Smith, who weighed almost 20 stone, lost nearly half her body weight to 9 stone 9 pounds after standing for 11 hours on a flight due to her fear of crushing a woman in the seat next to her. She joined Weight Watchers Online and later started running to maintain her new healthy weight, now a size 10.

Nicola Bonn, 34, from London, started an Upfront Mama blog to share her experiences raising 14-month-old daughter Poppy, detailing the challenges and often conflicting advice she received from others. Her post "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves" went viral, highlighting the overwhelming opinions new mothers face, such as criticism of breastfeeding and night-time feeding.

Hassan Munshi, 17, and Talha Asmal, 17, feared to have crossed into Syria to join ISIS, are believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 for terrorism in 2006. The boys, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, traveled to Turkey on March 31 and have not been in contact with their families for several days. Their families are in shock and deeply worried about their safety, urging anyone with information to contact police.

Stephanie Scott, a school teacher from Leeton, was murdered just days before her wedding to childhood sweetheart Aaron Leeson-Woolley, attended by 120 guests. Her body was found in nearby bushland, and her fiancé was later arrested. The couple had planned a wedding with yellow balloons and flowers, but Stephanie's remains were discovered the day before her planned ceremony.

Tonny Vilhena, 20-year-old Feyenoord winger, wants to leave this summer, prompting Southampton to make inquiries. Vilhena, a Holland U21 international, is set to join Southampton, who are also interested in midfielder Jordy Clasie and winger Eljero Elia, aiming to strengthen their squad for potential European qualification. Southampton is currently seventh in the Premier League, exceeding expectations despite losing key players last summer.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library at Ickworth House, Suffolk, angering heritage experts who called it misguided. The move, part of a planned experiment at nine other venues, sparked controversy, with art historian Bendor Grosvenor criticizing it as patronizing. National Trust director Simon Murray defended the experiment, stating it was a short-term arrangement and part of presenting each house in context.

Former Prime Minister John Howard found himself with a flat tyre in Sydney, standing on the footpath as his driver, Felicity Waterford, helped change it. Waterford, waiting for her daughter at the Sydney Conservatorium, offered assistance and was surprised to see Howard, who agreed to a selfie. The incident occurred weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television, earning him the nickname 'The Fixer'.

Tony Pulis, West Bromwich Albion manager, conceded Joey Barton had a point when Barton claimed his players 's*** themselves' after a 2-3 loss to Queens Park Rangers in December. Barton said West Brom went 2-0 up and lost 3-2, suggesting they failed to finish games. Pulis recalled his own experience of leading 2-0 and losing in a play-off final, admitting he cannot claim invincibility with leads. Pulis praised his team's recent performances, hoping to continue their good form against QPR.

A Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought extinct for over 50 years, was discovered alive in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ntokou-Pikounda National Park. Primatologists Lieven Devreese and Gaël Elie Gnondo Gobolo captured the first-ever photograph of the species, proving it not extinct. However, the monkeys are vulnerable to hunters in the commercial bushmeat trade, and their population is believed to be extremely small.

Kim Kardashian and her family visited Armenia, a country her father fled, from Yerevan, the capital. They stayed at the Armenia Marriott Hotel and explored landmarks like the Yerevan Opera House and the Geghard Monastery, experiencing a city described as a "city on permanent holiday" by Lonely Planet.

British expats Patrick and Valerie Jubb are trapped in southern Spain amid a legal battle with the local town hall over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated. They face losing their property due to illegal additions by a previous owner, despite obtaining a certificate stating no infractions when they bought it in 2008. The couple, who want to return to the UK, have a €680,000 deal to sell the estate but face demolition due to a four-year-old ruling. Located in Jimena de la Frontera, the property is in Los Alcornocales Natural Park and is marketed as a secluded, panoramic mountain-view home.

Apple reported its best-ever quarterly results, selling more than 61 million iPhones for $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit, accounting for over two-thirds of its total revenue. Sales in China outpaced those in the US, with iPhone sales up 40% year-over-year, despite a 40% decline from the previous quarter.

A 3-year-old girl, Elisa Tyler, has recurring nightmares about a white van, which her father believes may be linked to her mother's death in a 2002 Ford Explorer crash in Virginia. Natali Castellanos-Tyler, 30, died in the accident, ruled a one-car collision due to poor road conditions. Elisa's night terrors have sparked interest as three hit-and-run incidents involving a white delivery-style truck have occurred in the area, with one Facebook user claiming to have been side-swiped by the truck.

Researchers at New York University found that the brain can more easily remember 'neutral' events tied to emotion, contrary to the assumption that only emotionally charged events are remembered well. This study, influenced by the September 11 attacks, suggests emotion enhances memory by affecting brain regions involved in emotional processing and experience encoding, such as the amygdala, striatum, and hippocampus. Sleep also plays a role in memory consolidation, with a 45-minute nap reportedly boosting recall by five times.

Jahnae Jackson, 18, a psychology student from northern NSW, has been caring for her paralysed boyfriend Jackson Byrnes, 18, with a stage four brain tumour. They raised over $80,000 from community support for Dr. Charlie Teo's life-saving surgery at Sydney's Prince of Wales Hospital, which is likely to save his life but will leave him paralysed.

Nedum Onuoha, 28, a QPR centre-back with 15 months left on contract, is wanted by Hull City, who are considering streamlining their squad. Onuoha played in QPR's crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion. He is also being targeted by Everton, West Ham United, and Stoke City. QPR have discussed a move for Catania defender Nicolas Spolli, while Hull City are interested in West Bromwich Albion striker Victor Anichebe.

From 'here's you a piece of pizza' to 'this glass needs washed', every state has its own phrases that can seem odd to the rest of the world. Researchers at Yale University documented these patterns by mapping common phrases across the US, revealing regional differences in sentence structure. The study found that presentative sentences like 'Here's you a water bottle' were normal in the South but rare in the North.

A Canadian man, Kalman Kallai, travelled 2,796 miles from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia in a green rocking chair, taking breaks to watch planes, pose with cows, and even chase birds. He carried the chair on his head and waved at statues, sharing the journey with his father for a bonding experience.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed a Twix multi-pack as a 'win bonus' during a press conference, referencing a letter he received from six-year-old fan Charlie Pye who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert's dismissal.

World boxing champion Kell Brook watched the Premier League Darts in Sheffield, receiving a hero's welcome. Dave Chisnall, who was second in the table after 10 weeks, won both of his games, including a 7-3 victory over world champion Gary Anderson and a 7-1 win over James Wade. Brook is set to defend his welterweight title against Frankie Gavin on May 30.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic, saying the 33-year-old striker plays an essential role for the club, both on and off the pitch, helping young players and exuding confidence. Ibrahimovic missed the Champions League quarter-final first leg against Barcelona due to suspension but will return for the return match.

The Ministry of Defence faced criticism after a secret RAF base on the Falklands Islands, containing GPS coordinates and runway depth information, was published unencrypted on their website, potentially giving Argentine intelligence an invasion guide. The manual, uploaded accidentally, could have been accessed by Argentine spies and could cripple British defenses. Argentina is preparing to lease 12 Russian SU-24 bombers, which could pose a threat to the islands.

Huddersfield Giants, currently ninth in Super League, aim to improve their attack after losing all three games since Easter. Coach Paul Anderson hopes to boost the team's offensive efficiency, currently ranked best defensively. A win against Catalans Dragons could move them to fourth place, while Vikings coach Denis Betts expects a tough challenge from Castleford, who have the league's best defensive record.

Windsor planners approved two Costa Coffee shops less than 500 yards apart, including one replacing a cycle shop earlier this year, despite one resident's concern about too many coffee shops. The new shop will be in Dedworth, formerly without such businesses, and planners deemed there was no legal reason to refuse.

The British Veterinary Association withdrew its support for shooting free-running badgers in pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, concluding that the culls had not demonstrated conclusively their effectiveness and humaneness. The BVA still supports badger culling to combat bovine tuberculosis in cattle, but animal welfare campaigners criticized its ongoing support for cage-trapping and shooting. The Environment Secretary pledged to expand culls if the Tories win the election, despite criticism from wildlife groups and a lack of expected benefits in Gloucestershire.

Portishead's Geoff Barrow accused streaming services of underpaying his band, saying they received £1,700 in royalties for 34 million plays, while artists like Taylor Swift and Radiohead have pulled their music from Spotify. Barrow supports Jay-Z's new Tidal service, which aims to offer musicians a better deal, charging $9.95 for standard sound quality or $19.99 for 'lossless high fidelity sound quality.'

Online pirates leaked the first four episodes of Game of Thrones' fifth season, scheduled to premiere tonight, before their official release. The episodes, titled The Wars to Come, The House of Black and White, High Sparrow, and The Sons of the Harpy, were downloaded more than 550,000 times by early Sunday morning. HBO, which approved the leak, is investigating the breach. The series is the most illegally downloaded program worldwide, with Brazil and France leading illegal downloads.

Melbourne singer Daniel Buccheri, 25, composed an emotional song to use as his best man's speech at his brother Adrian's wedding, which was sung to the tune of "Stay With Me." The unique speech, performed at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke, east of Melbourne, went viral online, viewed over 100,000 times, and included tributes to his brother and new sister-in-law, Sarah.

Zara Phillips, Queen's granddaughter, regained her fitness after giving birth to Mia Grace by exercising on an exercise bike every morning before her daughter wakes up, aiming to qualify for Team GB at the 2016 Olympics. She eats a balanced diet and does additional workouts like swimming and cycling, with her goal to compete in eventing.

Raheem Sterling, Liverpool's star player, said he was not ready to sign a new contract, angering Liverpool fans. Sterling's interview was ill-timed, and many fans now believe he should leave the club. Liverpool fans support the mantra "no player is bigger than the club," and Sterling's departure is now widely accepted.

Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola conversed during a Barcelona training session in 2015, sparking a social media guessing game. This photo led to discovering other notable coaches from the same Barcelona team of 1996, including current PSG coach Laurent Blanc and Porto coach Julen Lopetegui, who were all part of the squad that won the Spanish Super Cup.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona said Javier Pastore from Paris Saint-Germain is the best player in the world, praising his creativity and passing skills. Pastore, who cost £29 million, has three goals and five assists this season, compared to Messi's 45 goals for Barcelona and Ronaldo's 51 for Real Madrid. Cantona, who won the Ballon d'Or in 1993, made the controversial claim despite Barcelona forward Lionel Messi being overlooked.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murdering Michael Spalding, 39, by hacking him to pieces and dumping the body parts in a canal in Smethwick, Birmingham, after a four-week trial. Simon and his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, were cleared of murder but admitted assisting an offender.

Health experts warn that social isolation is as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day, leading to dementia and high blood pressure. Essex and Gloucestershire county councils have created 'loneliness maps' to identify areas with the most vulnerable elderly residents, using factors like age, living alone, mental health, and income. Gloucestershire surveyed residents to pinpoint those at risk, with the most vulnerable areas marked in red, aiming to target help where needed.

65-year-old Judy Eddingfield celebrated her 50th anniversary working at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she was trained by her mother and has served for over 60 years. Eddingfield, who started at 15, says her job is her home and the only one she's ever had, recalling her first day's mishap but no firing. She has worked alongside family members for generations, including her first husband, and has even met celebrities like 'Leave It to Beaver' actors.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not be recalled to the international team, even if he scores runs for Surrey, citing rebuilding bridges and competition from other players. Gatting suggests Pietersen would need to perform poorly to secure a spot, noting Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root have shown good form. Gatting also expresses concerns about Alastair Cook's captaincy if he fails to score runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old Californian student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' for iOS, allowing users to upload photos directly from their computer to Instagram. The app, which he sells for $4.99, now faces a potential lawsuit from Instagram, as it allegedly violates the company's terms of service. Benn, who earns $1,000 a day from the app, refused to comply with Instagram's request to 'fix' the app, citing its legal gray area and potential for abuse.

South Korean companies frequently host hoesik, or official eating/drinking fests, where alcohol is consumed multiple times at various venues. Foreign business travelers face intense pressure to participate, as drinking is seen as a way to get to know someone. Traffic congestion in Seoul peaks on Fridays, reflecting the city's heavy drinking culture, with fewer cars on the road as workers head out for the night.

The Duke of Kent, 79, suffered a dislocated hip while visiting Balmoral estate in Aberdeenshire and was hospitalized at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. He was discharged today with a walking stick, having been treated for the injury. The Duke, a former Army officer and international trade ambassador, has a history of health issues, including a mild stroke in 2013.

The 50-year-old Surfers Paradise Meter Maids, introduced in 1965 by Gold Coast developer Bernie Elsey, are facing criticism from local business leaders who say they are outdated and irrelevant due to advancements in parking meter technology. The group, now seen as a business, is violating anti-touting laws by selling branded merchandise. Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president Peter Yared supports ending the tradition, calling it a "terribly ill-informed position" and stating the Meter Maids are no longer providing a public service. Surfers Paradise Meter Maids general manager Michael Yarwood counters, arguing the group is a quintessential part of the Gold Coast experience, cherished by tourists.

Greece denied it would fail to repay a £330 million IMF loan due on April 9, with Deputy Finance Minister Dimitris Mardas stating the country will make the payment on time. However, sources close to the Syriza party claimed the government prioritized paying wages and pensions over loans, potentially leading to a default if the eurozone does not agree to pay the next portion of its bailout deal.

Turkey blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after the social media platforms refused to remove images of prosecutor Mehmet Selim Kiraz, who was held hostage and later killed during an armed siege. The images deeply upset the prosecutor's wife and children, and the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front (DHKP-C) was blamed for the attack.

Seven-year-old Colin Gilpatric, an aspiring Jedi Knight with autism, wrote to George Lucas, creator of Star Wars, asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucas replied, granting Colin's request, assuring him that forming attachments is a light side value and not a path to the dark side. Colin was thrilled to receive a letter from Lucasfilm with Star Wars merchandise and a supportive response.

Wisconsin beat Kentucky 71-64 in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's 38-1 unbeaten season and bringing an end to the Wildcats' bid for an NCAA record. Wisconsin will play Duke in the final, while Kentucky, now 38-1, joins the 1991 UNLV team as the latest team to lose in the semifinals despite an undefeated record.

Vince Neil of Mötley Crüe famously botched the American national anthem before a Las Vegas Arena Football League game, drawing criticism and comparison to earlier controversial renditions by Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton, each of whom had previously made national headlines with their performances or mishaps.

CCTV footage released showed Barry Lyttle, an Irishman from Belfast, punching his younger brother Patrick, causing him to fall and suffer a traumatic head injury in Sydney. Patrick, who had only recently reunited with his brother in Australia, was treated by paramedics and nearly died. Barry pleaded guilty to grievous bodily harm, and a court hearing is set to determine if he will serve a prison term.

Conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, born with disrosopus, died 19 days after birth. Their family laid them to rest at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney. After visiting the gravesite, the parents found it cleared of all mementos and thrown in the rubbish, leaving only a few flowers. They were told the site was being cleaned, but found their daughters' belongings in nearby bins.

Britain's Supreme Court President Lord Neuberger suggested Muslim women should be allowed to wear full-face veils in court, emphasizing judges should show respect to different customs. This comes amid uncertainty over the veil's place in the legal system, following a 2003 trial where a Muslim woman refused to testify due to a face veil ban. Last year, the European Court of Human Rights upheld a French ban on the niqab in public.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri on Tuesday night for killing Anthony Curtis 16 years ago over child support payments. Cole became the third convicted killer put to death this year in Missouri, despite appeals claiming he was mentally ill and unfit for execution.

Prince Harry will fly to Australia without meeting his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is now overdue for the birth of her second child, expected by mid to late April. Harry, fifth in line to the throne, had hoped to see the new royal baby but will return to Australia for a month-long army placement and a week-long tour of New Zealand.

A Florida man named Justin Jackson was accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager to trick people into giving him freebies and jobs worth $2.4 million. Jackson allegedly contacted a New York City jeweler in 2007, pretending to be Madonna's manager, and obtained items worth $2.4 million, which he then sold. He also sent letters to hotels and jewelry companies, claiming to be Oprah and her representatives, and even suggested Oprah would make a personal appearance at the hotels. Jackson was later convicted for grand theft.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini valued Paulo Dybala at €50 million (£36m), urging PSG to outbid rivals for the Argentine forward. Dybala is sought by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and PSG, with Zamparini expecting a bidding war. Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini watched Dybala play, and PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi is considering the transfer.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians protest against President Dilma Rousseff, calling for her impeachment due to an ongoing bribery scandal at state-run oil company Petrobras, where many implicated politicians belong to her Workers Party. Rousseff denies involvement but faces plummeting approval ratings and an economic downturn, with inflation and currency losses exacerbating public frustration.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona denied claims he starred in a soft porn film, "You and the Night," insisting it is a "piece of art." The film, featuring racy scenes including Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear, has been both praised and criticized. Cantona said it is beautiful and not pornographic, attributing its aesthetic quality to the director.

Psychologists found that certain types of music can enhance flavors in food and drink, with researchers suggesting that The Beatles' music can improve enjoyment of a fish and chip supper. In Shanghai, fish and chips are served with The Beatles playing, and in Spain, scented meringue is paired with commentary on Lionel Messi's actions, which highlights citrus flavors. Music can also enhance wine enjoyment by up to 15%, with specific pieces of music complementing certain wines and foods.

Liverpool player Raheem Sterling, offered £100,000-a-week by manager Brendan Rodgers, has put contract negotiations on hold until the season ends, with PFA chief Gordon Taylor defending his decision, citing the need to focus on football and avoid media scrutiny.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, works at the same company and lives six minutes away. After receiving birth records for people born between 1964 and 1996, Mitchell-Clark connected with Simmons on Facebook and eventually met her. Simmons, who had always wanted to contact her daughter, now has three biological daughters she didn't know about.

Oscar 'Papoo' Hernandez Jr., a gun trafficker for Aaron Hernandez, pleaded guilty to weapons charges. Hernandez shipped three guns, including a rifle and handguns, to Aaron Hernandez in April 2013, a month before the NFL player killed Odin Lloyd. Hernandez, blinded by fame, was sentenced to life in prison without parole for his role in Lloyd's murder.

Joel Parker, 33, was arrested in St Johns County, Florida, after throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head during a ride, threatening and disrupting the driver, according to police. Parker was charged with battery and given a $250 bond, with a trespass warning and ban on future bus use.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis discussed pre-season plans with striker Saido Berahino, indicating he plans to keep the 21-year-old beyond the summer transfer window despite Berahino's desire to play in Champions League football. Pulis said Berahino is happy at the club and has been working well, though the striker is likely to be away with England's under-21 team until late June.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a project manager with German aid group Welthungerlife, was abducted in Pakistan in 2012 by armed men and later killed in a U.S. drone strike in Afghanistan, along with American hostage Warren Weinstein. Lo Porto worked on reconstruction projects following flooding in Pakistan, where he was killed while aiding victims of another flood in 2011.

Photographer John Massung captured images of hundreds of sharks, including Blacktips and Spinners, swarming just 100 feet from a beach in Sebastian Inlet, Florida, last Thursday. The swarm was spotted by Massung and another photographer, who theorized it was a mix of Blacktip and Spinner sharks migrating to breed. The sighting was shared widely on social media, with more than 2,000 views by Sunday.

An 11-year-old retired German Shepherd K-9 officer Zeus, who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years, was honored in a heartwarming farewell procession in Connecticut on Wednesday before being put down due to a severe hip disorder. The tribute included a procession through Ridgefield streets, with residents lining the route and police departments from across the state participating. Zeus assisted with over 250 narcotics arrests and helped track down 50 missing or wanted individuals during his career.

Child sexual abuse reports surged by over 60% since Operation Yewtree, initiated by Jimmy Savile's abuse, with nearly 9,000 reports in 2014. Despite a rise in cases, arrests fell by 9%, prompting critics to accuse the government of failing victims. South Yorkshire saw a 577% increase in reported cases, with 501 investigations in 2014 compared to 74 in 2011.

Iceland has become a popular filming location, with 17 production services companies established nationwide. Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Skaftafell National Park, Vatnajökull, and Dettifoss are key locations used in productions like Game of Thrones, Interstellar, Prometheus, and Thor: The Dark World. Scenes from these films, including battle scenes and the beginning of time, were filmed in Iceland's stunning natural landscapes.

A blue and yellow bathing box on Melbourne's Brighton beach sold for $276,000, a record price, after five bidders battled at auction. Meanwhile, a 1917 grey-fronted fire station in Sydney's Paddington sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home. In Victoria, a couple sold an 1850s maximum security prison goal for $2 million, claiming it to be haunted.

40-year-old Samantha Rawcliffe, a mother from Morecambe, crashed her car after a rare brain disorder caused uncontrollable shaking and loss of bladder control. Diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) in September, she now relies on a mobility scooter and takes 32 medications daily, unable to walk or drive. FND is an umbrella term for neurological symptoms with no known cause, making it difficult to treat and manage.

Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created a statue of Lucille Ball in Celoron, New York, admitted to being "disappointed" in his work, calling it "by far my most unsettling sculpture." The statue, based on Ball's famous drunk pitch for Vitameatavegamin, has been nicknamed "Scary Lucy" and has caused shock among residents. Poulin offered to remake the statue for free, estimating a cost of $8,000 to $10,000, and promised to create a new, more flattering version.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba, 22, will miss the rest of the season with a torn knee ligament, ruling him out for around seven weeks after an injury sustained in Austria's 1-1 draw against Bosnia on Tuesday. Alaba, who had been in excellent form for Bayern, had been sidelined for three months earlier this season. He is set to start rehabilitation in about a month. Bayern, top of the Bundesliga, faces Porto in the Champions League quarter-finals.

University College London student Beatrice Nokes, 21, appeared in court accused of running a prostitution ring with suspended Met police detective Daniel Williams, 37, in Central London last year. Nokes faces three charges of causing or inciting prostitution, while Williams faces seven additional charges including controlling prostitution and using police computers to spy on clients. Both are on bail.

A firm called Sequester, linked to Alchemy Direct Media, is offering details of over 43 health conditions, including eating disorders, stress, and impotence, for just 12p per person. The data includes sensitive personal information such as financial details, medical history, and credit card information. The revelations prompted investigations by the Information Commissioner’s Office and other bodies, highlighting the sale of private patient data without proper checks.

Jordan Spieth won the Masters golf tournament, equalling Tiger Woods' 1997 record, becoming the second-youngest winner and only the fifth to lead from start to finish. Reflecting on his victory, he expressed his love for his autistic 14-year-old sister Ellie, who could not attend the tournament, and how she provides perspective on life's challenges.

Sunderland's new manager Dick Advocaat, who previously underplayed the Old Firm derby's significance, will lead Sunderland against Newcastle in the Wear-Tyne Derby. Advocaat, who lost a similar match in 1998, now emphasizes the game's importance, acknowledging Sunderland's precarious position in the league. The match is crucial for both teams, with Sunderland needing points to avoid relegation, and the home crowd expected to play a significant role.

A dispute erupted between Belinda Bartholomew, girlfriend of Roosters player Aidan Guerra, and a butcher at Sam the Butcher in Bondi, Sydney, when Bartholomew asked for a different chicken. She claims the butcher called her a "c***" and told her to "go to an Aussie butcher," while the butcher denies any abuse, saying Bartholomew was rude and slow, and there are eight butchers in Bondi.

Cadbury reduced the size of Freddo Frogs from 20g to 12g, losing 20% of their weight, to combat manufacturing cost increases. The move was announced without fanfare, but sparked anger from consumers who had previously complained about Cadbury reducing the size of its family blocks by one row.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met in Brooklyn on Saturday, a day before her official announcement. Robby Mook, her campaign manager, distributed a "values statement" outlining goals and principles, avoiding mistakes from her 2008 campaign. The document emphasizes humility, discipline, and unity, stating the campaign will win on the ground in states. Clinton plans to launch her campaign on Sunday, focusing on Iowa and New Hampshire.

A 29-year-old woman, Kyli Wilfson, battled chronic pancreatitis for over a year and a half, unable to eat due to excruciating abdominal pain, despite feeling desperately hungry. Initially misdiagnosed with acute pancreatitis, she was finally diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis after a camera was inserted into her throat, leading to a permanent feeding tube. Her weight dropped to 80 lbs, and she postponed her wedding as she spent time in hospitals.

Labour leader Ed Miliband was superimposed over London rapper Plan B in a meme, referencing his direct message to David Cameron. Other leaders were depicted in various humorous images, such as Nicola Sturgeon with a sceptical face and David Cameron and Nick Clegg superimposed over Gogglebox commentators. Farage was left out, as both Cameron and Clegg were featured in a meme with characters from the TV show Gogglebox.

Amir Khan, seeking a fight with Floyd Mayweather, now faces Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, UAE, after Mayweather turned down the "Fight of the Century." Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather, could face Pacquiao in November or December in Abu Dhabi, where Khan would be a draw due to his popularity in the Muslim world.

A tiny two-bedroom home, only 5ft wide in some areas, sold for £750,000 in Islington, London. Located between two double-fronted properties, the home, 8ft 8in wide at its maximum, features a narrow 'galley kitchen' and a garden. Despite its small size, it sold for almost double its 2001 price, prompting interest from buyers despite the cramped living space.

SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon launches an election manifesto in Scotland, including policies that overlap with Labour, such as reducing tuition fees to £6,000 and rolling back NHS competition, aiming to form a 'progressive alliance' with Labour MPs. The manifesto totals £180 billion in spending over five years, funded by borrowing, and could give the SNP a majority in Westminster, potentially leading to constitutional turmoil similar to 1910.

Celtic's under-17 team beat Rangers 2-0 in the Glasgow Cup final at Hampden Park, with Josh Kerr scoring the opener and Mark Hill the second, as Celtic secured their fourth consecutive title in eight seasons. Robby McCrorie's mistakes allowed Celtic to win, despite Rangers' early efforts and late equalizing chance.

West Bromwich Albion's Tony Pulis led his team to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, claiming he will never change his pre-game attire of cap, track suit, and white trainers. The win moved West Brom to 36 points, virtually guaranteeing their Premier League safety, while Pulis defended his unique sideline style.

Jameela Jamil, a TV presenter, spent £3,000 to replace all her amalgam fillings with white ones after experiencing health issues for seven years, including puffy face, exhaustion, and fainting. Dental amalgam, used for fillings, contains mercury, which she believed triggered her symptoms, though experts say the risk is minimal.

Rap mogul Suge Knight, awaiting trial for murder and attempted murder, was denied a bail reduction to $5 million. Knight, who hopes Floyd Mayweather will bail him out after Mayweather wins his next fight, was wheeled out of court in a wheelchair. Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Ronald Coen set 16 days for the trial, which will begin on July 7 unless a motion is made to continue. Knight, 48, has been hospitalized due to medical issues since his arrest in January.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine, 35, showcased a lavish feast for her British shorthair cat Kimchi in a cat magazine shoot, featuring caviar, salmon roe, and seafood sculptures. Kimchi, known for its discerning palate, loves human food like poppadoms and tortilla chips, with taramasalata being his "death row dish." Erskine admits Kimchi is overweight and has expensive tastes, including green curry. She also recently adopted a new cat named Ponzu.

Martin Springall, 38, photographed his unnamed daughter in Zushi, Japan, in 2014. A mysterious black boot appeared in one of the photos, sparking debate on Reddit. Springall insists no one else was in the photo and it was not Photoshopped, despite skepticism.

Foreign workers in the UK will face a £22,000 tax bill before they can claim benefits under Tory plans, including a four-year ban on receiving state support and a six-month job requirement for those in work. Home Secretary Theresa May announced these measures as part of a new deal with Europe, aimed at curbing EU migration and addressing concerns over net long-term migration to the UK, estimated at 298,000 in the year ending September 2014.

Eight-year-old Cody Neatis, with Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and tube feeding, has been sleeping on the floor in a cramped hospital room for seven nights due to lack of a suitable high-sided bed. The Royal Preston Hospital has a mattress on the floor for him, while his mother, Lynne Neatis, 48, has slept with him since his admission last Thursday. Cody's developmental age is around 12 months, and his mother fears he might injure himself or pull out his oxygen. Cody has been in hospital since August 2013, and his mother claims the hospital has failed to provide a suitable bed for him despite previous promises.

Englishman Ian Poulter forgot his golf clubs at his rental home as he arrived at Augusta for the Masters. Henrik Stenson, recovering from flu, looks to defy expectations at the tournament. Tiger Woods will play with his children, and the Masters celebrates its 80th anniversary with a par-three tradition.

Juventus ruled out signing Manchester United's loan striker Radamel Falcao, citing his high wages, after Falcao struggled at Old Trafford and is expected to leave in the summer. Juventus instead expressed interest in Palermo's Paulo Dybala and Paris Saint-Germain's Edinson Cavani.

David Cameron pledges to sell £4 billion of Lloyds Bank shares if re-elected, offering up to £10,000 worth to individuals at a 5% discount, with a loyalty bonus for long-term holders. This would be the largest privatization since the Thatcher era, encouraging investors to hold onto their shares.

Living near congested roads with high PM2.5 levels can cause ‘silent strokes,’ leading to brain damage and dementia, researchers found. The study, involving over 900 people aged 60 and over, linked increased PM2.5 exposure to a 46% higher risk of silent strokes, contributing to brain shrinkage and other damage.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old 'wellness warrior' battling epithelioid sarcoma, died in February after refusing chemotherapy and radiation. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, revealed she began targeted radiation in her final weeks, a risky decision she embraced despite scientific lack of support for Gerson Therapy. The treatment helped shrink her tumor but led to complications, with Pamenter saying Ainscough displayed courage and grace throughout their seven-year fight.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale, 2km south of Fernvale, on Wednesday afternoon. Three patients, including a 40-year-old man and a 5-year-old boy, were flown to Princess Alexandra Hospital with serious injuries. Six others, including an infant and two young girls, were taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries. The highway was closed for a few hours with diversions in place south of Fernvale.

34-year-old Jason McDonald, a gator farm manager in Colorado, walked a thin slackline over a pool containing over 50 alligators, some up to ten feet long, at the Colorado Gator Farm. He said the reptiles were initially wary but eventually seemed unbothered by the presence. McDonald, who has been volunteering at the farm for over ten years, plans to walk over the farm's largest and albino gators in the future. He has never been bitten before but was clamped by an 8-foot alligator last month.

The son of slain Syrian imam Abdul Hadi Arwani, who was called to a job site in London, may have met his father's killer days before the murder. Arwani, 48, a Muslim Brotherhood member, was shot and killed in his car near Wembley on a quiet street after being asked to return another day. The man, identified as black and speaking with an African accent, asked Arwani to return alone, suggesting he was a hired killer. Scotland Yard investigates whether the man was a hired assassin who postponed the hit due to Arwani's son being present.

Hong Kong's tiny Jenny's cookie shop in Tsim Sha Tsui became a black market hit, with tourists and locals queuing for hours to buy $9 tins of cookies, leading to knockoffs and a 70% markup for resellers. The frenzy spread globally, with other foods like cronuts and ramen burgers also causing similar manias before fading.

Kira Hollis, a 27-year-old from Tamworth, Staffordshire, overcame anorexia, depression, and borderline personality disorder by becoming a bodybuilder. Diagnosed at 6st, she gained weight and improved her mental health through gym workouts, turning her life around and now working as a personal trainer. Her daughter Olivia and boyfriend Michael Dennis supported her recovery. Her story went viral after she shared her journey online.

Jockey Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular double somersault fall from favorite Merrion Square at Wincanton on Wednesday, sustaining only a cut on his nose. The fall, caught on video, has been viewed by hundreds of thousands online. Ferguson, who was mucking out the stables as usual, said he was undeterred and plans to return to racing, including the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree.

Hillary Clinton launched her 2016 presidential campaign with a video, new logo, and road trip, aiming to reframe herself as empathetic and relatable. Critics dismissed her launch as vapid, but her team aimed to change how voters feel about her, similar to Apple's reframe strategy, which shifted how consumers experienced the brand.

More than 1,700 Chinese freshmen students took a high school exam in a playground in Yichuan, Shaanxi province on Saturday, due to lack of indoor space. The students organized the outdoor exam themselves, rotating their chairs and desks to avoid sun glare, and believed it would help prevent cheating and broaden their horizons.

Sportsmail offers a prize to a lucky reader including signed Nike Magista Obra boots by England and Manchester City goalkeeper Joe Hart, a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor, and shaving gel, closing the competition on April 19. Hart is the No. 1 for Manchester City and England.

One-year-old baby orangutan Kecil, rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate, found a loving home with 53-year-old surrogate mother Maggie at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. After 10 months, Kecil and Maggie have formed an inseparable bond, with Kecil crying briefly when separated but quickly returning to Maggie. Kecil will make his first public appearance this weekend.

A 61-year-old woman from Winchester, Hampshire, died after her pet dogs ate her body parts following an accidental overdose of medication. Noelle Baynham, a former jeweller, was found in her dressing gown with a bath run just before her death. Her two dogs, a Jack Russell and Staffordshire Bull Terrier, were initially thought to have tried to wake her but became desperate for food, leading to her partial consumption. Detectives found no evidence of foul play, but a pathologist could not determine the exact cause of death due to the dogs' consumption of her organs.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, a multiple gold medalist, will stand trial for fraud over match-fixing allegations involving his brother Luka and 15 other players, including former Montpellier teammates. The case stems from a 2012 match where Montpellier, already champions, lost to Cesson-Rennes, leading to an increase in betting and a police investigation. Karabatic denies placing bets and faces up to five years in prison.

Six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were jailed for a total of 31 years after being convicted of sexually abusing 13-16-year-old girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. Hassan-Sule and Saleh received nine and four years' imprisonment respectively, while others received sentences of three to nine years. The victims described the offenders as a group that targeted vulnerable young girls at under-18 parties they organized.

Aaron Hernandez, former New England Patriots player, was convicted of murder and faces three more trials: one criminal for killing two men and wounding another in July 2012, and two civil actions. He is also being sued by the NFL Players' Association over an unpaid $3.3 million signing bonus. Hernandez's lawyers will represent him in the civil cases.

The Dubai-based Emirates airline will rebrand the FA Cup, football's oldest knockout competition, as the Emirates FA Cup in a £30 million, three-year deal. The move adds to Emirates' growing portfolio of sporting sponsorships, which includes a £150 million deal with Arsenal Football Club and a £80 million deal with AC Milan.

Michael Phelps, 29, aiming for a fifth Olympic appearance in Rio, confirmed he will compete in the Olympics but won't participate in the world championships in Russia this summer due to a six-month suspension from USA Swimming for a second DUI arrest in September. Phelps, who had already qualified for three events, said the ban was punishment for removing him from the last major international meet.

Gareth Bale, a key Real Madrid player, is sidelined with a calf injury and a muscular lesion in his soleus muscle, likely missing Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday. Real Madrid also lacks Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who is out for six weeks with a knee ligament strain.

Scientists warned that older people are more susceptible to emotional decisions in retirement, leading to poor investment choices. In the 2007-2008 financial crisis, 50% of pensioners panicked and sold investments, losing £37,000 compared to £141,000 had they held onto them. New pension reforms allow Britons over 55 to access their savings, but experts caution that cognitive decline in old age can impair emotional regulation in the stock market.

Stuart Pearce, former Manchester City player and manager, believes Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to turn around City's Premier League fortunes, despite recent poor form including a 2-0 loss to Manchester United. Pearce criticized Yaya Toure's fading influence and suggested City should look to freshen up their squad in the summer, not replace Pellegrini.

Manchester United trained in the sunshine ahead of their Premier League derby against Manchester City on Sunday, with Wayne Rooney and Robin van Persie back in action. The match is crucial for both teams, with United aiming to move four points clear of City in fourth place, following their last three visits to Old Trafford where City won 6-1, 2-1, and 3-0.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona at home, conceding a late goal from substitute Mounir Obbadi, dropping nine points behind third-placed AS Roma and leaving them in sixth place. Former West Ham midfielder Alessandro Diamanti missed a penalty in the 65th minute, and Alberto Gilardino's penalty was saved by Verona's Rafael. The defeat leaves Fiorentina in the Europa League quarter-finals after a 1-1 first leg against Dynamo Kiev.

Miley Cyrus, at the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, displayed armpit hair, causing a social media stir. Users criticized her for not shaving, while others defended her choice, noting that men's armpit hair is generally accepted.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez scored 102 goals together this season, including 6-0 victory over Getafe, taking their combined tally to 102 in all competitions. Messi scored 49, Neymar 32, and Suarez 21, with all but nine of their goals coming from inside the box. This milestone boosts Barcelona's La Liga goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid.

44-year-old pedestrian Andrea McVeigh was left scarred for life after being knocked down by a cyclist riding on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London on April 14. The cyclist fled the scene, prompting McVeigh's husband to chase him. She suffered two three-inch gashes to her forehead and other facial and hand injuries. The Met Police issued CCTV footage and an appeal for the cyclist, who allegedly knew he was causing significant damage.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 and ordered to do 150 hours of unpaid work after pleading guilty to dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by claiming he could only walk 200 metres, despite being a keen walker and mountaineering club member. The fraud was exposed when council officials read a newspaper article about his 191-mile hike in Cumbria, which showed he had also walked in Wales shortly before applying for the badge.

Apple has patented a facial recognition system for unlocking devices, which would scan a user's face with the front-facing camera when the phone is moved into a specific position. The system, filed in 2011 and awarded this year, aims to automatically unlock the device if the scanned face matches a previously stored image, eliminating the need for PINs, passwords, or fingerprints. Android already offers a similar feature called Trusted Face.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, a cancer patient battling multiple myeloma, was forcibly removed from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California along with her family because she lacked a doctor's note. The Sedways were seated in the handicapped section and initially told they were fine, but were later asked to leave due to concerns about their health during the eight-hour flight.

Three people, including the owner of a $120,000 1973 E-Type Jaguar, were taken to hospital after a head-on collision with a Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night at a traffic light intersection in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney. The classic car was completely destroyed, while no one was injured. NSW police are investigating, warning that the crash occurred despite motorists being on high alert during the Easter long weekend.

Google is setting up a four-man team to develop and test battery technologies for phones, tablets, and electric cars, including flexible and wearable options. The team, led by former Apple battery expert Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj, has been working on solid-state, thin-film batteries since 2012. Google also collaborates with AllCell Technologies to create batteries that function in subfreezing temperatures, crucial for Project Loon balloon internet projects.

The 223ft Explorer, a superyacht designed by Tony Castro, comes with a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests, including car and jet storage. It costs approximately 40 million euros to build and is intended for the ultra-wealthy, who can purchase it for around £29 million/$43 million.

Labour leader Ed Miliband plans to impose rent controls despite warnings from experts, who say it will slash investment in new housing and lead to more evictions, while senior Tories and the Confederation of British Industry criticize the proposal, calling it economically illiterate and likely to suppress house building and push rents up.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter, Ryan Dearnley, was removed as a Reading mascot for the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after he said he hoped Arsenal would win, sparking outrage from Reading fans. The Football Association moved him to an England mascot role instead, offering him tickets but he declined.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may explain a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, discovered in 2004. The supervoid, if confirmed, would be the largest structure found by humanity and could account for the 20% less matter in a region 10,000 fewer galaxies than surrounding areas. Researchers from the University of Hawaii suggest the supervoid 'saps' light energy, causing it to lose energy and appear colder.

The red, worn chair where Abraham Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre in 1865 will be displayed at the Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, on April 15 for the 150th anniversary of the assassination, two days after renowned historian Doris Kearns Goodwin delivers a lecture there. The museum, founded by Henry Ford, has housed the chair since 1930, despite a dark stain on the back believed by visitors to be blood, which historians say is oil from previous occupants.

Jake Boys, 19, from Hailsham, booked plane tickets to Dublin instead of Cardiff for a One Direction concert, mistaking the Welsh capital for the Republic of Ireland. Emily Canham, 18, from Kettering, was surprised to learn her boyfriend had booked flights to Ireland, leading to a humorous mix-up.

Romanian company MB Telecom unveiled the Roboscan 2M Aeria, a mobile X-ray scanner that can detect contraband, bombs, and weapons inside planes. The device, costing €3 million, is being used to inspect trucks at borders in Eastern Europe and can scan an entire plane in about 20 minutes. While currently not safe for passengers, it aims to fill a security gap for low-security airports, where aircraft arrive without thorough inspections.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, described as having a 'fanatical obsession' with young girls, went on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit near Hook, Hampshire. Last seen leaving a hospital on Tuesday, Munden, who suffers from learning difficulties, was last seen without his beard. He was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl on a bus. Officers launched a manhunt, releasing images of him with and without facial hair.

Middlesbrough lead the Championship with four weeks to go, seven points ahead of second-placed Bournemouth. With a lunchtime kick-off against Watford, Boro's buffer over Watford and Norwich is a point, and their victory over Wigan on Good Friday suggests they can secure promotion. Watford and Norwich, who host Sheffield Wednesday, could change the top two if they win and Bournemouth fail against Birmingham. Boro's captain Jonathan Woodgate, who missed recent matches due to a broken toe, has won five of his last eight appearances.

Grey hair has become a trend, with women posting images on social media using the hashtag #grannyhair. Instagram is filled with beauty shots featuring models and selfies of grey-haired individuals, with over half a million views on a dedicated page. The trend, embraced by both men and women, is seen as a feminist statement or quirky fashion, offering an alternative to costly hair dyeing.

Randy and Jodi Speidel, a down-on-their-luck couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, struggling with chronic conditions, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning in their bedroom, two months after creating online fundraisers on GiveForward.com and GoFundMe.com, which failed to attract donations. They had been living without gas, water, and electricity, and were forced to limit their food intake to one meal a day.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to stay as party leader despite potential loss of seats, stating he would fight 'in all circumstances' and warned of Labour and Conservative vacating the center ground. He called for a coalition with Conservatives, saying he deserved credit for forming the Coalition while enduring 'five years of constant bile' from Labour.

A 79-year-old pensioner Terry Cooper was saved from a badger attack by his Jack Russell dog Sam, which dragged him back indoors after the badger, described as the size of a pig with six-inch teeth, burst through a hedge. The National Farmers' Union advised residents to protect their properties from badgers, warning that gaps in fences or hedges can be as small as 7.5 centimeters wide for badgers to enter.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose 3-0 to Porto U21s on Wednesday, avoiding Real Madrid's Champions League match against Atletico Madrid. Mourinho, joined by his son Jose Junior, visited Fulham's training ground and joked with Fulham's goalkeeping coach. Chelsea are closing in on their first Premier League title since 2010, with six games remaining.

Andreas Christopheros, 29, was critically injured when corrosive liquid was thrown at him outside his home in Truro, Cornwall; Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, has been charged with perverting the course of justice over the December attack that left him scarred and blind in one eye.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has posted signs warning visitors not to defecate along the famous path, drawing both complaints from residents and amusement from some pilgrims. The signs, showing a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line, have become an attraction as some pilgrims pose for photos with them. Residents of Lastres, which attracts thousands of pilgrims annually, have complained about defecation outside their homes, leading to the installation of the signs.

A massive fire engulfed a building formerly housing a strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon, starting around 1pm. Only the building and a few nearby power lines were affected, according to local media. The site was not vacant, and a fire had occurred there before. An investigation into the cause of the blaze continues.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent, Shoshana Hebshi, reached a $40,000 settlement in a lawsuit after being strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport on the 10th anniversary of 9/11. The federal government, Frontier Airlines, the Transportation Security Administration, and Wayne County Airport Authority were named in the lawsuit. Hebshi, who was detained for hours, said she was ethnically profiled and the settlement gives her some peace of mind.

Twenty people were injured after an Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 made a crash landing and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, believed to have missed the landing point on the runway and spun 180 degrees after impact. The Airbus A320 had departed from Incheon International Airport in South Korea, and emergency services were at the scene with injured passengers taken to hospital.

Made In Chelsea star Mark-Francis Vandelli, a 26-year-old son of a multimillionaire industrialist, revealed his extensive watch collection, featuring 16 expensive timepieces worth several thousand pounds. He has been collecting watches since his teens, buying a new one each year. His most expensive watch is a Cartier white gold Moonphase, costing £32,000, while a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, bought on holiday in Italy, can be found secondhand for £6,500. Vandelli prefers a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, no longer made, and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual for raves, as similar versions cost around £9,000.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his £100,000 antiques collection, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt and a longbow, in an auction of over 200 items at Dominic Winter auctioneers in Gloucestershire. Hardy, 89, a military historian and Tolkien student, is downsizing his home and reflects on the sadness of parting with his cherished possessions.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on Facebook criticizing a scene he witnessed on a train platform, expressing his disapproval of conservative attitudes. The image, which appeared to be a homophobic rant, was later revealed to be a clever spoof of public safety regulations. Felippe's post went viral, receiving thousands of comments praising his witty approach to combating homophobia.

A 16-year-old English cricket fan named Jonathan Stevenson, who wrote to Richie Benaud in 1996 for tips on left-handed leg spin bowling, shared Benaud's detailed 1996 response on Twitter after Benaud's death. Benaud, a renowned cricket legend, provided notes on coaching differences between left-handed and right-handed bowlers, including specific delivery tips.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts the future of travel will be virtual, with users able to experience world locations through 3D scenes and VR headsets. Facebook plans to support virtual reality on its newsfeed, allowing users to explore locations from multiple viewpoints, mirroring how photos and videos are currently shared. Marriott hotels have already tested VR tours of American hotels.
