A bedridden 22-year-old girlfriend, Dong Hui, had her wedding photographs taken by a team of professional photographers, despite her serious bone cancer diagnosis and hospitalization. Her boyfriend, Guo Kai, arranged for the photos to be taken while Dong wore a beautiful wedding dress and posed with a bouquet of red roses. Guo has been by her side every day, turning her every hour to prevent joint dysfunction.

Police in Houston charged 34-year-old Blaine Boudreaux with intoxication manslaughter and other charges after he caused at least three separate DUI crashes within three hours, killing 6-year-old Joshua Medrano and a homeless man, Leonard Batiste, and injuring his mother. Boudreaux, with a history of DUIs, was arrested after the first crash and later dozed off while driving, leading to a fatal collision with a mother and her 2-year-old child.

Microsoft announced a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond campus in Washington, partnering with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit that trains autistic individuals for IT careers. Mary Ellen Smith, Microsoft's Corporate VP of Worldwide Operations and mother of an autistic son, highlighted the importance of expanding opportunity and having a diverse workforce. Last year, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella apologized for suggesting women should trust the system to receive raises, emphasizing the company's focus on diversity.

Two deputies involved in fatally arresting Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, were reassigned due to threats against them and their families. Bates, 73, shot Harris with a handgun after calling for a Taser, leading to criticism for his actions. Bates is charged with second-degree manslaughter and has apologized, while Sheriff Stanley Glanz apologized to Harris' family and said the FBI cleared the agency of civil rights violations.

Katie Prager, 24, diagnosed with cystic fibrosis and an infection called Burkholderia Cepacia, needs a lung transplant but her Kentucky Medicaid insurance will not cover the $1 million out-of-state treatment at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Her husband Dalton, 23, who already received new lungs, pleaded for help as Katie's health continues to decline, fearing she may not live long enough for a transplant.

South Africans wake up earliest on Mondays at 6:09 am, while Americans rise at 7 am on Tuesdays, the worst time of the week for their mood. Slovakia had the best sleep quality, with 58% of countries reporting the best sleep on Wednesdays, including the US. Americans sleep the latest on Fridays, rising at 8:24 am, but report the best wake-up mood.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo, married to Diego Rivera, wrote passionate love letters to Jose Bartoli, a Catalan artist, from 1946 to 1949. The 25 letters, expected to fetch up to $120,000, were saved by Jose until his death in 1995 and will be auctioned at Doyle New York on April 15.

Red-haired trade union leader Len McCluskey, head of Unite, campaigned for Labour in South Wales with a warm demeanor but revealed the union's sinister influence on British politics, including its potential to impose socialist policies reminiscent of the 1970s. McCluskey, with a claimed 1.42 million members, is intertwined with Labour's structure, MPs, and finances, and has threatened illegal action against a Tory government's strike restrictions.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz filmed 30 hours of animals drinking water using a GoPro camera placed in their troughs at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv. The footage, cut down to four minutes, revealed unique drinking methods, from a rhino almost kissing the water to a lemur delicately licking it. Initially, some animals were sceptical but eventually adapted, with lions drinking aggressively and zebras humorously bare-teethed while sipping.

Just a quarter of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, while 43 per cent believe Ed Miliband is most up for the fight. Cameron, criticized for a dull campaign, appeared without a tie or jacket to show he is working 'bloody hard' for a Tory victory, despite voters believing Miliband is more passionate about winning.

A man charged with assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov, Zaur Dadaev, has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Dadaev initially confessed but now says he was coerced into making that statement. He is one of five Chechen men accused of killing Nemstov, who was shot four times on a bridge near the Kremlin in February. Dadaev had previously confessed but later retracted his confession, and human rights activists claim he showed signs of torture.

A 4-month-old baby named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of the Nepal earthquake, becoming the defining image of the disaster that killed over 5,000 people and injured at least twice that number. Sonit was buried alive for 22 hours in Muldhoka, Bhaktapur, until rescuers found him on Sunday morning, his eyes still closed despite being exposed to the cold.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narconon, is attempting to have a 40-acre property near Camp David, Maryland, designated as historic to circumvent zoning laws and build a drug rehab center. The property, previously bought by a Scientology-backed real estate company for $4.85 million, is currently zoned for resource conservation and cannot be used for medical purposes. Narconon claims the site has historical significance due to President Herbert Hoover's fishing trip there, while opponents argue it is a tactic to bypass regulations and create a potentially dangerous program.

Five English-speaking former NATO workers in Kabul, Afghanistan, are jobless and blacklisted, fearing reprisals and unable to support their families, as the city's population has swelled fivefold since NATO's arrival, leaving many businesses and neighborhoods abandoned.

One US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured on Friday during pool training at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia. The SEALs were swimming in lap lanes without gear when they were found at the bottom of the pool by another service member. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two. Navy spokesman Lieutenant David Lloyd said an investigation is ongoing.

One season from now, NBC expects more Americans to watch Premier League matches live than in Britain. In the past two years, US interest in the league has more than doubled, from 13 million to 32 million viewers last season. NBC moved its entire production to England this weekend, including star anchor Rebecca Lowe, who was at Burnley's match against Arsenal, alongside Robbie Earle and Kyle Martino.

Boris Johnson, appearing on the Andrew Marr Show, launched a personal attack on Ed Miliband, accusing him of potentially harming the country more than his brother David did. Johnson claimed Labour could not govern without SNP support, likening Miliband to a "monkey crouching on his back," while Miliband dismissed the attack, saying Johnson was "better than that."

A prisoner named Dustin Irons flashed a judge during a video court hearing, despite being handcuffed, and was sentenced to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court. The unamused judge, from Umatilla County Corrections Center, noted Irons' difficulty as a prisoner who needed constant supervision.

McLaren driver Jenson Button believes his team has made significant progress ahead of the Chinese Grand Prix, with Button and team-mate Fernando Alonso finishing the Malaysian Grand Prix in competitive positions. Despite retiring, they discovered the car was now faster compared to midfield rivals, though Button acknowledges further improvements are needed.

A hospital in southwest Perth, Fiona Stanley Hospital, was found to have blood and bone fragments on medical instruments after failing to return sterilizing equipment by February, leading to a $60,000 fine and Department of Health audits. Australian Medical Association WA president Michael Gannon reported concerns about ongoing issues, damaging the hospital's public image and morale.

Becca Litchfield, 29, and her partner Dale, 30, from Gotham, Nottingham, chose to forgo their dream wedding to fund one final attempt at IVF, which led to their pregnancy and birth of twins Darci-Mai and Stanley. After two failed IVF rounds, the couple won a wedding competition, allowing them to finally marry and celebrate their successful pregnancy.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email, locking staff out for almost 24 hours. The page was taken over by an 'unknown third party' posting adult cartoons similar to those on Delta Air Lines and Crayola's hacked pages. Scooter's Coffee issued an apology, stating the images were similar to those seen in other recent breaches of major brands, and Facebook only responded after larger businesses reported the issue.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center caused amusement by attempting to bark at a husky, making high-pitched squeaks and yappy barks, causing the husky to respond with whines. The video, captured during a playtime session, shows the puppies conversing and running towards each other, with people and staff laughing at their antics.

Liam Plunkett, 29, an England seamer, is set to bowl against the West Indies in the Caribbean, aiming to use his pace to 'rough them up.' He returned to the England Test team last summer but missed more due to an ankle injury. Now recovered, Plunkett is competing with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood for a spot in the first Test in Antigua on April 13.

Paul Smith, having lost to Arthur Abraham twice, faces a third fight against Andre Ward, a reigning world champion, in Oakland, California, before potentially facing Carl Froch. Ward, who is ranked among the top five pound-for-pound boxers, sees Smith as a suitable warm-up opponent, possibly before a rematch with Froch.

Residents of Parma, Missouri, were surprised when five of its six police officers and several top officials resigned after the city's first black mayor, Tyrus Byrd, was elected. The officials cited 'safety concerns' in their resignations, but Byrd still doesn't know the reason, according to the outgoing mayor. The city, with a population of 713, has suffered recent break-ins despite a large police force.

Yaya Toure will not be forced out of Manchester City but the club will make him available this summer, despite Sportsmail revealing they will consider offers. Toure is content at the Etihad Stadium but is fighting for his future, while his wages are a stumbling block for potential moves. Inter Milan is interested, but doubts exist about the club's ability to afford Toure's salary.

More than two-thirds (69 per cent) of people taking antidepressants in the U.S. did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder, according to a study. The research also found that 38 per cent did not meet the criteria for other psychiatric disorders like obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, or generalised anxiety disorder. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, suggests many antidepressant prescriptions may be unnecessary.

Doris Fuller, the mother of Natalie, 28, who killed herself last month, revealed in a Washington Post article that Natalie suffered from bipolar disorder and psychosis, undiagnosed until her early 20s. Fuller wrote how her daughter's illness worsened, leading to her death when she stepped in front of a train in Baltimore. Natalie, a poet and artist, had a famously close relationship with her mother but struggled with psychotic episodes, often seeming fine while medicated but relapsing into severe mental distress.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder suffered a cardiac arrest and collapsed during a British Bulldog game in the school playground, losing consciousness for 12 minutes. He was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as former footballer Fabrice Muamba. Teachers performed CPR until paramedics arrived and used a defibrillator to save his life.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, called for divorce laws to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. Current laws require couples to cite one of five reasons for divorce, with unreasonable behavior being the most common. Lady Hale proposed a one-year cooling-off period and encouraged couples to resolve arrangements for children and money before obtaining a divorce, as part of an overhaul.

Tottenham are considering a new £400 million stadium with a retractable pitch to potentially host an NFL London franchise, including extra-large changing rooms for up to 70 players, and could be ready for the 2018-19 season. The NFL is within five years of securing a permanent London franchise, with teams testing logistics at Wembley, which has a lower capacity and fewer sightline issues.

U.S. senators, including top Democrats and Republicans, wrote to FIFA urging Russia to be removed as host of the 2018 World Cup due to its involvement in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. They argue this would condemn Putin's regime and align with international sanctions. FIFA president Sepp Blatter announced Russia as the host, and the senators' letter was released on Wednesday. England is considering a bid for Euro 2028 but unlikely for 2026 World Cup, with the decision on 2026 tournament to be made in 2017.

Universal announced "Fifty Shades of Grey" sequel will debut on February 10, 2017, with husband of author EL James, Niall Leonard, writing the script. Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan are negotiating higher pay for the film after the first film's massive worldwide earnings of $568.8 million. Sam Taylor-Johnson, previously directing the sequel, is not returning.

West Brom manager Tony Pulis, 57, will face a hero's welcome at Crystal Palace but faces an uphill battle to avoid relegation. Despite his success at Stoke City and Palace, Pulis has never finished higher than 11th in the Premier League, with his current West Brom team stuck on 33 points and facing tough fixtures.

Fenerbahce called for a championship suspension after their team bus was attacked with gunfire near Trabzon, Turkey, following a Super Lig match. The bus driver was wounded, and the club said the attack must be solved to satisfy them and the public.

A massive avalanche hit Everest Base Camp, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens in Nepal's earthquake, with 4,300+ people dead overall. German climber Jost Kobusch recorded a harrowing two-minute video showing panicked climbers fleeing the snowfall, with many stuck at higher camps awaiting rescue.

87-year-old Gregory Margolin, a Jewish war veteran from the Soviet Red Army, found himself in another war in Ukraine. After surviving World War II, he fought in the conflict in Eastern Ukraine, where his daughter Ira was killed by a missile. Margolin, now suffering from Alzheimer's, moved to Israel with his family, feeling it was the safest place after the war in Ukraine.

John Carver, now fighting for the head coach position at Newcastle, relives the 1999 Tyne-Wear derby where former manager Ruud Gullit's controversial selection of Duncan Ferguson and Alan Shearer left Newcastle 2-1 losers and Gullit out of a job. Carver knows a victory against Sunderland on Sunday could be crucial for his chances, recalling how Gullit's decision to leave out key players led to his dismissal.

Revered Al Sharpton appeared in North Charleston on Sunday, addressing the Walter Scott case and police reform, alongside elected officials and police. Sharpton praised Mayor Keith Summey for firing officer Michael Slager, who killed Scott, and called for unity to reform policing nationwide.

Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the Liverpool forward was caught smoking a shisha pipe and allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide before scoring the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Rodgers said Sterling faces a club investigation and potential disciplinary action, with the manager planning to speak with the 20-year-old about professionalism.

Labour received £1.1 million in donations from unions in the second week of the election campaign, more than twice as much as the Conservative party's £492,512, with unions giving over £700,000 to Ed Miliband's Labour. Most donations came from Unison and Unite, totaling £724,355, while the Tories received £460,000 from wealthy individuals, including £170,000 from Christopher Rokos. This funding gap exposed Labour's financial advantage over the Conservatives, with Labour receiving 14 times more union donations than the Liberal Democrats combined.

Police were called twice to a Qatar Airways flight at Birmingham Airport after passengers became disruptive, waiting five hours for refuelling and a new crew. Some passengers were stranded for up to 24 hours, leading to complaints about inadequate transport and staff support, while a Qatar Airways spokeswoman apologized for the delay caused by strong winds.

Canadian pop star Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring for his $300 million Las Vegas fight against Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. The two have been close friends for years, and Bieber has accompanied Mayweather on numerous occasions. Despite initial reports that Bieber would only accompany Mayweather, he confirmed he will be part of the entourage, including leading out the American boxer.

Corinthian Colleges Inc., once enrolling over 70,000 students, announced its closure of all 28 campuses, marking a positive step in holding for-profit colleges accountable. These schools, which often offer dubious degrees and high debt, received federal student aid until the U.S. Department of Education curtailed their access last summer. With about 1.3 million students enrolled in for-profit colleges, many of which default on loans at rates higher than subprime borrowers, Corinthian's closure is part of efforts to close the remaining predatory institutions and forgive the debts of those unable to find employment or transfer to legitimate schools.

Pep Guardiola denied claims of a dispute with former Bayern Munich doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after the Champions League quarter-final defeat by Porto, blaming the medical staff for the loss. Muller-Wohlfahrt cited the bond of trust being damaged, while Guardiola said the defeat was not due to the medical staff and blamed himself for the result. Bayern had just 14 fit players available for the match.

Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, 39, will defend his world titles against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden in New York on Friday, recalling his Olympic gold medal win in 1996 that catapulted him into Ukrainian hero status. Despite being just a year shy of his 40th birthday, Klitschko, who has not shown signs of decline, believes age is an advantage and is confident in his peak performance.

Jeremy Clarkson, 54, has finally spoken out about his sacking from Top Gear, admitting he will 'miss' fronting the BBC2 show after being fired in March for attacking a producer. Former presenter Angela Rippon, 70, said she would be keen to return if invited back, while Clarkson thanked supporters but noted he would 'miss being there'.

Celta Vigo striker Fabian Orellana was shown a red card and struck by a lump of grass during a La Liga match against Barcelona, leading to a 1-0 win for Barcelona. Orellana threw the grass at Barcelona midfielder Sergio Busquets, who was injured, and was subsequently sent off.

Boston Marathon organizers and spectators faced tragedy in 2013 when three people died and over 200 were injured in a pair of bombs at the finish line. In 2018, a jury convicted Dzhokhar Tsarnaev of the bombings, and a sentencing phase begins April 21, with a federal judge warning jurors not to attend the marathon or related events.

Tens of millions of Chinese marked the Qingming Festival by returning to ancestral villages to clean graves, honor the dead, and celebrate the start of spring, a three-day holiday that saw parades and outdoor ceremonies across the country. In Shaanxi Province, a grand ceremony was held in honor of the Yellow Emperor Huangdi, considered the founding father of the Chinese nation, with thousands watching a 34-time drum and bell ritual.

Paul Simon, 73, returned to the UK album chart's top spot with "The Ultimate Collection," his first since 1990, outselling albums by younger artists like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. His recent tour with Sting, featuring live performances, is believed to have contributed to the album's success, marking his first chart-topping album in 25 years.

Iker Casillas, Real Madrid's longtime goalkeeper, insists he will stay at the Bernabeu until his contract ends, despite Manchester United's David de Gea being linked to a summer move to replace him. Casillas, 33, has been at the club since 1996 and hopes to fight for his position, stating he will strive and train for it. Real Madrid aims to become the first team to retain the Champions League title, and Casillas emphasizes the importance of fighting and effort in the upcoming semi-finals against Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Juventus.

Britain saw its highest employment level in history, with 31 million people in work in the three months to February, up 557,000 from a year earlier, according to official figures. The International Monetary Fund praised Chancellor George Osborne, saying the UK had created more jobs in the last five years than the rest of the EU combined. David Cameron hailed the Conservatives' 'jobs miracle,' while IMF chief Christine Lagarde and German finance minister Wolfgang Schaeuble endorsed the government's economic strategy, calling it a 'wonderful job.'

Korea's SsangYong is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli, priced under £13,000, aimed at budget-conscious drivers. The Tivoli, with engines ranging from 1.6 litre Euro 6 petrol and diesel, is available in three trim levels with front-wheel drive or 4x4 options. The entry-level SE model starts at £12,950, including seven airbags and smart steering, while the top-of-the-range ELX costs from £16,000 to £19,000, featuring advanced features like a TomTom navigation system and a rear-view camera. SsangYong expects the Tivoli to boost its UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 annually. Meanwhile, Citroen's Aircross SUV, inspired by tough Tonka toys, offers protective alloy bumps for added durability.

A chef named Sam Longhurst created a 10-inch tall, half-kilogram burger at Splendid Kitchen in Manchester, containing six forms of three different meats and 2,000 calories. The burger, called The Whole Damn Farm, features two beef patties, ham chunks, a whole chicken thigh, barbecued pulled pork, and bacon, and costs £13.50. The creation was inspired by a customer's challenge to include more meats in the restaurant's existing 'Cow & Chicken' burger.

A Michelin-starred chef prepares gourmet meals for Yeo Valley's 120 dairy workers at a staff canteen overlooking Blagdon, North Somerset, for as little as £2, using organic and locally sourced ingredients. The menu changes daily and includes dishes like soft-poached quail egg, confit of tomato, and deep-fried polenta, with some items costing up to £4 for the public.

Legendary blues musician B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration due to Type II diabetes, but he was back home resting and enjoying time with his grandchildren, according to his daughter. King, 89, has 30 Grammy nominations and is known for his hit "The Thrill Is Gone."

Manhattan's Fifth Avenue hosted an Easter parade with bizarre hats, including a ship and a diorama of Mayor Bill de Blasio, as thousands of participants, including Christians, Jews, and agnostics, paraded through the streets on Sunday. Some wore traditional bunny ears and eggs, while others displayed more elaborate designs like a butterfly and a bird's nest.

Emergency crews in Essex dispatched two ambulances to Epping Forest after a caller reported a person hit by a car, only to discover the "victim" was a squirrel. The East of England ambulance service has released a list of 1,248 "bizarre and irritating" calls, with front-line crews responding to almost half, potentially endangering lives. Calls included a man claiming to have dropped a "bleeding" burger, a woman reporting being locked out of her house, and a man saying his feet hurt from wearing tight shoes.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake won a head-to-head challenge against teammates Loic Remy and Willian in an Audi-sponsored football competition, securing a 6-0 victory in the final round. Willian accidentally smashed the wing mirror of an Audi during a long-range shot, causing a humorous mishap.

Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, after Sterling admitted Arsenal's interest in him. Rodgers revealed he had spoken with Sterling, advising him to stay at Liverpool, despite Sterling rejecting a £100,000-a-week extension and having two years left on his contract. Rodgers emphasized Sterling's enjoyment of playing for Liverpool and the club's financial benefits for his development.

Countdown co-presenter Rachel Riley was embarrassed when contestants offered the eight-letter word 'erection' as a word game answer, causing host Nick Hewer to laugh. This incident, along with other rude words like 'todgers' and 'm*nges', has become a recurring joke on the show, which has aired 6,000 episodes since 1982.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who tried to buy deadly poison online was spared jail after the court heard he wanted to commit suicide. Officers from the North West Counter Terrorism Unit investigated him after he ordered the toxin on the dark web, unaware he was being tracked. The teenager pleaded guilty to trying to buy the toxin and was sentenced to a 12-month referral order.

Three hours after giving birth to her baby girl, Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four, died at North Manchester General Hospital, where three other babies and one mother had died in the previous eight months. Ms Hindle, who had suffered two previous stillbirths and three premature pregnancies, was taken to the hospital after her condition worsened. Her family called for action to prevent further tragedies, citing concerns about the care she received, including being left alone with a student midwife.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after a video surfaced of her training while eight months pregnant. The 32-year-old plans to compete in the 2016 Rio Olympics, continuing her rigorous training regimen right up until her daughter's birth, as she did with her first child seven years ago. Emily was born at a healthy 3.1 kilograms on Monday.

At least one person died after a powerful storm capsized several sailboats in the Dauphin Island Regatta in Mobile Bay, Alabama, with crews searching for four missing individuals. A man was rescued by the Coast Guard around 9 p.m., and more than 100 sailboats and 200 people were participating. Mayor Jeff Collier confirmed at least one death, with boats scattered across a wide area from Dauphin Island Bridge to Fort Morgan. Richard Mather, aboard a 39-foot O'Day sailboat, rescued three people from sinking vessels but saw others struggle to survive.

Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, eye diseases that can progressively steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening, with her vision closing in. Macular degeneration affects central vision, while glaucoma damages peripheral vision. Barr uses marijuana to relieve glaucoma pressure, though the combination of both diseases is unusual but not unheard of.

An Oklahoma jury convicted 17-year-old Chancey Allen Luna of first-degree murder for shooting and killing Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane during a jog in Duncan on August 16, 2013. The jury recommended life in prison without parole, while defense attorneys argued Luna meant only to scare Lane. Luna did not testify, and his mother testified he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

Arsene Wenger, Arsenal manager, insists his 12-0-7 record against Jose Mourinho will not affect their top-of-the-table clash with Chelsea at the Emirates on Sunday. Wenger, who has lost seven of their 12 meetings, says the result will depend on the day's performance. The game features Fabregas, now a Chelsea player, returning to Arsenal's home ground. Wenger emphasizes the importance of the match, despite their 10-point deficit, and acknowledges Chelsea's consistency and defensive strength.

Manny Pacquiao, now 36, has risen from poverty in the Philippines to become a global boxing icon, facing world champions like Oscar De La Hoya and Juan Manuel Marquez. He began his career in the Far East, fighting in 2001 against Lehlo Ledwaba in Las Vegas, and is set to face Floyd Mayweather in the "Fight of the Century" on the Las Vegas Strip.

Jack Grealish, a top flight starlet, was photographed taking nitrous oxide during Aston Villa's FA Cup semi-final win against Liverpool at Wembley. This incident, though legal, highlights the importance of maintaining a clean body for professional athletes, as emphasized by former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger.

Sam Barton, who underwent £55,000 of cosmetic surgery, was attacked with eggs by a group of men on Easter Monday after checking in at a pub on Facebook. The 22-year-old believes the attackers tracked him down using social media, forcing him to move houses and leading to online abuse. Barton was pelted with six eggs while leaving the Green House pub in Sutton Coldfield, damaging his appearance and leaving him with yolk and shell on his face.

An Indiana university was on lockdown after receiving a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the administration building, prompting police and a bomb squad to respond. No injuries were confirmed, and the university advised students to shelter in place, with the all-clear not given as of early morning.

Luis Suarez and Edinson Cavani will face off in the Champions League quarter-final as Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain vie for a spot in the semi-finals. Cavani, known as El Matador, faces the challenge of breaking through Barcelona's defense, as PSG's key players Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Veratti are suspended. Cavani has struggled with a goal drought, missing seven matches and only scoring twice in the last month, leading to speculation about his future with the team.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title, defeating Tony Luis 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 in Liverpool, after Richar Abril and Ismael Barroso pulled out due to illness and visa issues, respectively. Luis showed aggression but could not sway the judges, who ruled in favor of Mathews in a closely contested fight.

Hull KR bounced back from a Thursday defeat to beat St Helens 28-20 at Langtree Park, securing a surprise win that ended St Helens' three-game losing streak. Jamie Shaul scored the winning try, while Saints nearly equalized through Louie McCarthy-Scarsbrook and Alex Walmsley, but Hull held on thanks to a late penalty.

By 2023, the documented and undocumented immigrant population in the United States could reach 14.8%, with immigrants accounting for one in seven residents. By 2060, immigrants could make up 82% of the country's population growth, reaching 78 million, nearly four times the 2010 population of 306 million. This growth has important implications for the country's workforce, schools, infrastructure, and environment, prompting debate on potential new immigration policies.

Jack Wilshere made his return from injury as captain for Arsenal Under 21s, but the team lost 1-0 to Reading's youngsters at the Emirates Stadium. Former Arsenal defender Martin Keown's son Niall scored the winning goal in the 8th minute, while Wilshere and long-term absentee Abou Diaby managed to last 56 minutes and 88 minutes respectively.

English golfer Justin Rose, struggling with form after three missed cuts and a 55th-place finish, improved significantly in his first round at the Shell Houston Open, hitting 17 out of 18 greens and signing for a 69, a score also achieved by Jordan Spieth. Despite his recent slump, Rose expressed confidence in his return to form, attributing his issues to a lack of consistency and corrected his technique, aiming to perform well at the upcoming Masters tournament.

A mansion in Mayfair, London, that was once a milking parlour for cows has gone on the market for £25 million. Originally a commercial depot, the site now features modern luxury amenities including an indoor swimming pool, gym, lift, cinema room, and roof terrace. Built in 2011, the 8,139 square ft property is on the market for £25 million by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank.

Bayern Munich, without key players Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba, showed unity in recent games against Borussia Dortmund and Bayer Leverkusen, scoring 3-0 against Eintracht Frankfurt. Coach Pep Guardiola expects the team to rely on Thomas Muller and Robert Lewandowski to score against Porto in the Champions League quarter-final, despite injuries. Guardiola acknowledges Porto's physical midfielders but also their quality, stating Bayern will need two good games to reach the semi-finals.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes team-mates, visited Mercedes' Brackley base to collaborate and counter Ferrari's victory in the Malaysian Grand Prix, where Sebastian Vettel beat them by 8.5 seconds. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff was concerned about Ferrari's tactics, noting they were able to run longer on tyres in the high heat, which favoured Vettel.

Oklahoma Gov. Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection is deemed unconstitutional or unavailable. The gas causes unconsciousness within 8-10 seconds and death from lack of oxygen, according to supporters. However, the Death Penalty Information Center's Robert Dunham criticized the bill, noting similar arguments were used for lethal injections, and Oklahoma's previous execution process has been criticized. Oklahoma has been on hold for executions while the Supreme Court reviews lethal injection methods.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday, topping this week's EA Sports' Performance Index with a Game Index score of 52.9 after scoring four goals in his last six Premier League games. Charlie Austin of Queens Park Rangers is the runner-up with a score of 52.2, following his two goals and assists in a 4-1 win against West Brom.

A Russian freezer trawler, the Dalny Vostok, carrying 132 crew members, sank in the Sea of Okhotsk off the Kamchatka Peninsula in just 15 minutes, killing at least 56 crew members. A massive rescue operation involving over 1,300 people is underway, with 63 survivors rescued and 56 bodies recovered. The ship tipped over after a fishing net weighing 80 tons was pulled in, likely due to empty fuel tanks and lack of ballast. Temperatures in the water can dip to -2°C, contributing to the high number of fatalities.

Men with advanced prostate cancer, including those with genetic faults in their tumours, could benefit from the drug olaparib, originally developed for women with breast cancer. Clinical trials found that 16 out of 49 men responded to olaparib, delaying disease progression and improving tumour responses. The drug, a PARP inhibitor, targets DNA repair defects and is the first of its kind to be approved for ovarian cancer, showing promise in men with prostate cancer.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, turned her photography skills into a business by launching 'In Bed With', a website that reviews luxurious hotels worldwide. With over 12,000 Instagram followers, she documents the best beds, pools, and room service, earning income from both hotel stays and professional photos. Taylor has stayed at exclusive properties like the Mineral Springs Hotel in Australia and Than Sanctuary in Bali, generating income from featured hotels and travel product companies.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was thrown into the air and dragged along the surface of water in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, South Africa, after being caught in a deadly fight between two adult males. The calf's mother, a 30-year-old tour operator, tried to protect her baby but was unable to intervene as the sub-adult hippo held the calf in its mouth. The baby died hours later.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea after Branislav Ivanovic was struck by a cigarette lighter thrown from home supporters during Chelsea's 1-0 victory at Loftus Road. QPR is unlikely to face disciplinary action, but the FA will seek observations and ensure clubs take steps to identify the culprit via CCTV and ban those involved. QPR is reviewing footage and appealing for witness information, stating the incident does not represent the club's fan base.

LaTasha Gosling, 27, and her three children—Janyaa, 4, Jenika, 8, and Landen, 7—were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan, one day after they were reported missing. The suspect, found dead hours later, had a six-month-old baby with him who was unharmed. Police have not yet released details on the suspect's death or the relationship between the victim and suspect.

Emily Thornberry, a Labour politician, was criticized for opposing the right to buy policy for council tenants but renting out a property she bought from a housing association for almost £1 million. Thornberry, who could buy her council flat at a discount, has been accused of hypocrisy for advocating against the policy that would benefit hardworking people.

Police dropped an investigation into a vicious assault on Mike Lane, 40, a huntsman, three months after it occurred, despite evidence pointing to a suspected attacker. Lane, who was beaten by protesters armed with iron bars, said the decision was "pathetic" and that unless further evidence comes forward, the attackers are unlikely to be found. Lane suffered concussion and broken teeth, and his trust in the police has been shaken.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer, despite being linked with Manchester United and Chelsea. Gomes, who has scored four times in 25 La Liga appearances since joining from Benfica, says he is happy at Valencia and denies being contacted by Chelsea.

Australian teenager Audrey Pekin, 19, alleged she was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali by Henry Alafu, who had met her earlier and lured her to his remote home. Alafu then assaulted her again in a taxi as she tried to flee. Despite her pleas for help, Alafu followed her and allegedly raped her again. Indonesian police failed to prevent Alafu from escaping back to Nigeria.

Former Made In Chelsea star Ashley James, who loves animals, posed with a fake skinned fox to protest Harvey Nichols' reintroduction of fur products. PETA, with a slogan 'Harvey Nichols: Here's the Rest of Your Fur Coat,' is mounting a billboard campaign against the department store, which previously banned fur but now sells it. Ashley encourages informed consumer choices, while Harvey Nichols claims to prioritize ethical trading practices.

Chile enacted a new law recognizing civil unions between same-sex couples, allowing around 2 million people to benefit from greater legal rights, including property, health care, pensions, and inheritance, effective in six months. President Michelle Bachelet called it a step to end discrimination faced by common-law couples.

Chelsea are on track to break the Premier League record for most days at the top of the table, currently leading for 230 days since August 30, 2022, surpassing Manchester United's record of 262 days in the 1993/94 season. Should they stay atop the table until the end of the season, they could set a new record by 12 days.

Cape Verde, a small island nation with 500,000 people, has a rich musical heritage and is seeking to capitalize on its cultural wealth to boost its economy, which lacks conventional natural resources. The country's prime minister and culture minister support the idea, recognizing music and culture as key sectors for development. The Kriol Jazz Festival, celebrating its seventh year, has attracted international artists and has become a significant event in Cape Verde, with locals deeply immersed in the music.

A hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of Sydney's Opera House went viral again after heavy storms. Originally posted by Sydney resident Darren Johnson in 2012, the video was retweeted by popular radio duo Fitzy and Wippa on Tuesday. Skeptics noted inaccuracies, including rocks around the Opera House and a cardboard-like appearance, while wave experts claimed it was impossible for waves to reach that far inside the harbor.

Reading lost 1-0 to Birmingham in a Sky Bet Championship game at the Madejski Stadium, with Clayton Donaldson scoring the winner in the 83rd minute after Reading dominated most of the match but failed to capitalize on several chances. Reading, who lost in the FA Cup semi-finals to Arsenal, had no pressure to avoid relegation after Millwall's defeat, while Birmingham had little to play for beyond improving their poor recent league record.

French champions Paris Saint-Germain suffered a significant setback as David Luiz, a key player, will miss the Champions League match against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained in the first half against Marseille. The Brazilian defender, known for his runs, will be out for at least four weeks, potentially impacting PSG's Ligue One title defense and their Champions League campaign.

The return of Game of Thrones sparked a surge in internet piracy, with fans making over 100,000 illegal downloads per day. More than seven million episodes from seasons one to four were illegally downloaded between February and April, up 45% year-on-year. The top country for illegal downloads was Brazil, accounting for almost one million episodes, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO announced a new streaming service, HBO Now, to curb piracy and recapture revenue, though it is only available in the US.

Leicester City, bottom of the Premier League, face West Ham United at King Power Stadium on Saturday, with Matt Upson and Dean Hammond unavailable due to injury. West Ham's Winston Reid returns from injury, while Andy Carroll misses after scoring in their previous meeting. Leicester has won just one of their last 10 home Premier League matches, while West Ham have not won away from home in seven games.

Residents of Celoron, N.Y., have reacted with shock to a statue of Lucile Ball, the hometown icon, unveiled in 2009. The statue, based on a drunken pitch scene from 'I Love Lucy,' has been criticized for its unflattering depiction, leading to a Facebook page with over 600 likes. Artist Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has declined to comment, while the mayor estimates a $8,000 to $10,000 cost to recast it.

A 43-year-old woman named Sharon Smith, who weighed almost 20 stone, lost nearly half her body weight to 9 stone 9 pounds after standing for an entire 11-hour flight due to her size causing discomfort to a passenger next to her. Smith, a children's clothes designer, quit her job to freelance and began exercising at home, leading to her significant weight loss.

Nicola Bonn, 34, from London, started an Upfront Mama blog to share her experiences raising 14-month-old daughter Poppy, detailing the challenges and often conflicting advice she received from others. Her post "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves" went viral, addressing the overwhelming opinions new mothers face and the need to stop apologizing for their decisions.

Hassan Munshi, 17, and Talha Asmal, 17, feared to have crossed into Syria to join ISIS, are two teenagers from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, who have not been in contact with their families for several days. Their families, shocked and worried, implore anyone with information to contact police, fearing the pair may have boarded a flight to Turkey. Hassan is reportedly related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 and later convicted for planning to murder non-Muslims.

Stephanie Scott, a school teacher from Leeton, was brutally murdered just days before her wedding, leaving her grieving father Robert devastated. Her body was found in nearby bushland, and a guest list of 120 had been prepared for her wedding at Eat Your Greens venue in Eugowra. The couple, Stephanie and Aaron Leeson-Woolley, had been taking dancing lessons to prepare for their first dance, but the planned wedding was instead a memorial.

Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old Holland U21 international winger, is set to leave Feyenoord this summer, with Southampton interested and ready to make the move. Vilhena, whose contract expires in one year, is reportedly keen to join the Premier League. Southampton, currently seventh in the Premier League, is also monitoring Feyenoord's other Dutch midfielder Jordy Clasie, who is valued at £10 million. Koeman, Southampton's manager, is looking to strengthen his squad for potential European qualification.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House in Suffolk, angering heritage experts who called the move misguided. The Trust plans similar experiments at nine other venues, sparking debate on how to engage visitors without diminishing the historical significance of the spaces.

Former Prime Minister John Howard found himself with a flat tyre in Sydney, standing on the footpath as his driver, Felicity Waterford, offered assistance. The pair, including Waterford's daughter, who was at a concert nearby, changed the tyre at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music, with Howard agreeing to a selfie. This incident occurred weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television, earning him the nickname 'The Fixer'.

Tony Pulis, West Bromwich Albion manager, conceded that Joey Barton, his player, "probably had a point" when Barton criticized the team for losing despite being 2-0 up against Queens Park Rangers in December. Pulis recalled his own experience of leading 2-0 and losing in a play-off final, admitting that leads can be hard to maintain. West Brom are now hoping to continue their strong performances after losing 3-2 to QPR.

A Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought extinct for over 50 years, was captured in the Ntokou-Pikounda National Park in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Primatologists Lieven Devreese and Gaël Elie Gnondo Gobolo took the first-ever photograph of the species, proving it is not extinct. However, the monkeys are vulnerable to hunters in the commercial bushmeat trade, and their population remains unknown.

Kim Kardashian and her family visited Armenia, a country her father fled, for eight days, arriving in the capital Yerevan for a rock star welcome. They explored local landmarks and stayed at the Armenia Marriott Hotel on Republic Square, a culturally rich area known for its music and dance performances.

British expats Patrick and Valerie Jubb are 'trapped' in southern Spain amid a legal battle with the local town hall over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, face losing their estate due to illegal additions made by a previous owner, despite obtaining a certificate stating no infractions existed when they bought it. The Jubbs are attempting to sell the property, valued at €680,000, but the town hall has ruled it must be demolished, citing the four-year-old illegal alterations. They plan to move back to the UK but are financially tied to the property.

Apple reported its best-ever quarterly results, selling more than 61 million iPhones for $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit, up 40% from a year ago. Sales in China outpaced those in the US, with iPhone accounting for more than two-thirds of revenue. iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer revenue rose 2% to $5.6 billion.

A 3-year-old girl, Elisa Tyler, has been having recurring nightmares about a white van, which her father believes may be linked to her mother's death in a 2002 Ford Explorer crash in Virginia. Natali Castellanos-Tyler, 30, died in the accident, ruled a one-car collision due to poor road conditions, but Elisa has since reported visions of a white van harming her and her car. This has led to reports of hit-and-run incidents involving a white delivery-style truck in the area, sparking renewed suspicion about the cause of the crash.

Researchers at New York University found that the brain can more easily remember 'neutral' or boring events tied to emotion, contrary to the assumption that we remember emotionally charged events better. This study, which also looked at how the September 11 terrorist attacks affect memory retention, suggests that emotion enhances the strength of memories, even for mundane details. Sleep can also boost memory consolidation, with a 45-minute nap reportedly improving recall five times.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of 18-year-old Jackson Byrnes with a stage four brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 from the community to fund his life-saving surgery by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo on Wednesday. Despite being paralysed and unable to dress himself, Jackson has completed school and put his psychology studies on hold to care for his boyfriend.

Nedum Onuoha, a 28-year-old QPR centre-back with 15 months left on his contract, is wanted by Hull City, who are considering downsizing their squad. Onuoha played in QPR's crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion and is also of interest to Everton and West Ham United. Hull City are also monitoring West Bromwich Albion striker Victor Anichebe, who could be sold this summer.

From 'here's you a piece of pizza' to 'this glass needs washed', every state has its own phrases that can seem odd to the rest of the world. Researchers at Yale University documented these patterns by creating an interactive map showing common phrases for each state, including 'I ain't never had no trouble with none of 'em' in Florida and 'I so might run this [race] with you' in California.

A Canadian man, Kalman Kallai, travelled 2,796 miles from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia in a green rocking chair, taking breaks to watch planes, pose with cows, and even chase birds, sharing his journey on video. He brought his father on part of the trip, which provided a bonding experience.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood, after being passed over for the Villa manager position by Tim Sherwood when Paul Lambert was sacked, quizzed the media about a letter from six-year-old fan Charlie Pye. Sherwood revealed his "win bonus" to the assembled media, jokingly offering Pye a Twix multi-pack, which Pye had sent him for a different win at Tottenham.

World boxing champion Kell Brook watched the Premier League Darts in Sheffield, receiving a hero's welcome after his recent title defense. Dave Chisnall, the 28-year-old, won both of his games in the 10th week, moving to 17 points and second place in the table. Brook is set to defend his title against Frankie Gavin on May 30.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic, the club's 33-year-old striker, for his "essential" role, saying Ibrahimovic plays a crucial off-pitch role helping young players and exuding confidence. Despite a suspension for the Champions League quarter-final first leg against Barcelona, Ibrahimovic is available for the return match.

The Ministry of Defence faced criticism after a secret RAF base on the Falklands Islands, containing GPS coordinates and runway depth information, was accidentally published on their website, potentially giving Argentina an 'invasion guide.' The manual, uploaded to a public section, could aid Argentine intelligence in planning an attack. Argentina is considering leasing 12 Cold War-era SU-24 bombers from Russia, which could pose a threat to the Falklands' defenses.

Huddersfield Giants, currently ninth in Super League, coach Paul Anderson hopes to improve their struggling offense to match their strong defense, aiming to climb back up the ladder after losing all three games over the Easter holiday period. The Giants face Catalans Dragons, who have the best defensive record in the league, in a crucial home game. A first win in four games could propel Huddersfield to a season-high fourth position.

Windsor planners approved two Costa Coffee shops less than 500 yards apart, including one replacing a cycle shop earlier this year, adding to the city's existing Costa Express at a petrol station. One resident criticized the decision, while another argued it signals economic growth in the area, with planners stating there was no legal reason to refuse.

The British Veterinary Association withdrew its support for shooting free-running badgers in pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, concluding that trapping and then shooting them was not conclusively effective or humane. The BVA still supports badger culling to control bovine tuberculosis in cattle, but animal welfare campaigners criticized this stance. The Environment Secretary pledged to expand culls if the Tories win the election, despite criticism from wildlife groups and a lack of expected benefits in Gloucestershire.

Portishead's Geoff Barrow accused streaming services of underpaying his band, receiving just £1,700 in royalties despite 34 million plays, while criticizing Universal Music for selling his music cheaply. Barrow, founder of Invada, said streaming hurts young talent and wants musicians paid more, leading to the launch of Tidal by Jay-Z to offer better deals.

Online pirates leaked the first four episodes of Game of Thrones' fifth season, which is set to premiere tonight, before its scheduled release. The episodes were downloaded more than 550,000 times and began appearing on torrent sites on Saturday night, originating from press review copies. HBO, the show's producer, is investigating the breach.

Melbourne singer Daniel Buccheri, 25, composed an emotional song to use as his best man's speech at his brother Adrian's wedding, which was performed at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke, east of Melbourne. The unique speech, set to the tune of "Stay With Me," was viewed over 100,000 times online and included tributes to his brother and his new sister-in-law, Sarah.

Zara Phillips, Queen's granddaughter, regained her fitness after her daughter Mia's birth by exercising on an exercise bike every morning before Mia woke up, aiming to qualify for Team GB at the 2016 Olympics. She eats well, avoids sugary foods, and includes swimming and cycling in her workouts, starting at 7 am.

Raheem Sterling, Liverpool's star player, said he was not ready to sign a new contract, causing anger among Liverpool fans. The interview, ill-timed, has changed fans' opinions, with many now wanting him to leave. Sterling trains ahead of a match against Arsenal, and Liverpool fans support his potential move to Arsenal.

Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola engaged in a playful banter during a Barcelona training session in 2016, with Guardiola joking he would win the treble one day. This photo sparked a series of discoveries in archived images, revealing that current PSG coach Laurent Blanc, Porto coach Julen Lopetegui, and four other coaches from the 1996-97 Barcelona team, including Albert Ferrer and Abelardo Fernández, are now managers.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona, speaking at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai, declared Paris Saint-Germain's Javier Pastore the best player in the world, praising his creativity and passing ability. Pastore, who cost £29 million, has three goals and five assists this season, compared to Messi's 45 goals for Barcelona and Ronaldo's 51 for Real Madrid. Cantona noted Pastore's ability to surprise with his passes and scoring, calling him the most creative player in the world.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder after hacking his 39-year-old tenant Michael Spalding, known as Spud, into pieces and dumping the body parts in a canal. Simon and his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, dismembered Spalding using a hacksaw and two suitcases, with Simon later admitting to assaulting Spalding during a fight. The case was solved when police found the suitcases containing Spalding's body parts in the canal, linking the hacksaw to lacerations on other bones. Simon was arrested in Derby after moving there to evade police.

Health experts warn that social isolation can be as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day, leading to dementia and high blood pressure. Essex and Gloucestershire county councils have developed 'loneliness maps' to identify areas with the highest risk of social isolation among elderly residents. Gloucestershire used public health statistics and resident surveys to map vulnerable areas, with the most at-risk marked in red. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends other councils follow suit to target local people most in need.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary working at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she has served for half a century. Eddingfield, who began working at age 15, remembers when French fries and a classic Coca-Cola cost 65 cents. She recounted a memorable incident from her first day, when she spilled a shake on a customer's fur coat, but was forgiven. Eddingfield, who has worked alongside her mother for 13 years, says her job is her family tradition and that her kind customers are what make her job worthwhile.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not automatically return to the international team, even if he scores runs for Surrey, citing that other players like Gary Ballance and Ian Bell are performing well. Gatting also suggests that Alastair Cook, England's Test captain, might face questions if he fails to score runs against West Indies, despite Cook's previous 100s.

A 17-year-old Californian student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' for iOS, allowing users to upload photos directly from their computer to Instagram. The app, which he sells for $4.99, now faces a potential lawsuit from Instagram, which claims it violates the company's terms of service. Benn, however, argues that Instagram's strict API restrictions open up possibilities for abuse and that users should be able to post from a computer if they wish.

Most South Korean companies host hoesik, a monthly or weekly dinner with co-workers that often involves multiple rounds of alcohol. For foreign business travelers, drinking is intense and considered a way to get to know someone, as it's seen as an invitation to talk. Drinking etiquette is crucial, with Koreans expecting everyone to have an empty glass and turning away from seniors while drinking to show respect.

The Duke of Kent, 79, suffered a dislocated hip while visiting Balmoral estate in Aberdeenshire and was hospitalized at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. He was discharged today with a walking stick, two years after a mild stroke. The Duke, a respected Army officer and former international trade ambassador, continues to perform royal duties.

The 50-year-old Surfers Paradise Meter Maids, started in 1965 by Gold Coast developer Bernie Elsey, are facing criticism from local business leaders who argue they are outdated and no longer perform a public service. Advancements in parking meter technology mean expired meter times are not always displayed, and the group is now seen as a business violating anti-touting laws by selling branded merchandise. Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president Peter Yared supports ending the tradition, stating the Meter Maids are no longer relevant and fleece tourists, while Meter Maids' general manager Michael Yarwood defends the group, saying tourists embrace them as quintessential part of the Gold Coast experience.

Greece denied it will fail to repay a £330 million IMF loan due on April 9, with Deputy Finance Minister Dimitris Mardas stating the country will make the payment on time. However, sources close to the ruling Syriza party claimed the government prioritizes paying wages and pensions over loans, potentially leading to a default if the eurozone does not agree to pay the next portion of its bailout deal.

Turkey blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after the social media platforms refused to remove images of prosecutor Mehmet Selim Kiraz, who was held hostage and later killed during an armed siege. The images upset the prosecutor's wife and children, and the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front (DHKP-C) was blamed for the attack.

Seven-year-old Colin Gilpatric, an aspiring Jedi Knight with autism, wrote to George Lucas, creator of Star Wars, asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucas responded, granting Colin's request and explaining that forming attachments is crucial for Jedi values, which can prevent the 'dark side.' Colin was thrilled to receive a letter from Lucasfilm with Star Wars merchandise and a supportive message.

Wisconsin beat Kentucky 71-64 in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending the Wildcats' 38-1 unbeaten season, to advance to the final. Frank Kaminsky scored 20 points and grabbed 11 rebounds for Wisconsin, who won with a 7-0 run and 7-for-8 free throws in the final 24 seconds. Wisconsin will play Duke in the final at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Monday.

Vince Neil of Mötley Crüe famously butchered the American national anthem before a Las Vegas Arena Football League game, drawing criticism and likened to a butcher's work, following a long tradition of varying performances and reactions to the anthem.

CCTV footage showing Barry Lyttle, from Belfast, Ireland, punching his younger brother Patrick, causing him to fall and suffer a head injury, has been released. Patrick, who had only recently reunited with his brother in Australia, was treated at the scene and later hospitalized. Barry pleaded guilty to grievous bodily harm and could face up to two years in Sydney jail, with his fate to be decided at a sentencing hearing.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, born with disrosopus, found their gravesite at Pinegrove Memorial Park in Sydney's west completely bare after cemetery staff had cleared all mementos and discarded them. The twins died 19 days after birth, and their parents had set up a small shrine with flowers and statues at the gravesite. When they visited on Thursday, they discovered everything had been removed, leaving only a few flowers. The family confronted cemetery staff, who said they were supposed to be notified for cleaning, but no warning was given.

Britain's Supreme Court President Lord Neuberger suggested Muslim women should be allowed to wear full-face veils in court to show respect for their cultural customs. This comes amid uncertainty over the place of Muslim traditional dress in the legal system, following a 2003 trial where a woman was sentenced for refusing to remove her veil to testify. Last year, the European Court of Human Rights upheld a ban on wearing the Muslim full-face veil in public, prompting debate on how to accommodate diverse cultural practices in courts.

Andre Cole, 52, was executed by lethal injection in Missouri on Tuesday night for killing Anthony Curtis 16 years ago over child support payments. Cole became the third convicted killer put to death this year in Missouri, despite appeals claiming he was mentally ill and unfit for execution. The execution took place at Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, and Cole declined a last meal. Governor Jay Nixon noted the forgotten victims of violent crime, including Curtis, and asked for prayers for his family.

Prince Harry will fly to Australia without meeting his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is now overdue for the birth of her second child, who will be fourth in line to the throne. Harry had hoped to see the baby at the weekend but is now returning to Australia for a month-long army placement and a week-long tour of New Zealand.

Justin Jackson, a Florida man, has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager to trick people into giving him freebies and jobs worth $2.4 million. Jackson allegedly contacted a New York City jeweler in 2007, pretending to be Madonna's manager, and received items worth $2.4 million, which he then sold. He also sent letters to hotel groups and jewelry companies, claiming to be Oprah and her representatives, and even suggested Oprah would make a personal appearance at the hotels. Jackson was convicted for grand theft over one of these schemes.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini valued Paulo Dybala at €50 million (£36 million), dubbing him the 'new Lionel Messi', and Palermo is in a bidding war with PSG, Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, and Juventus for Dybala, who is also wanted by PSG. Zamparini said Dybala would be a good investment for PSG but a first-team spot in Italy is more likely, though he wants €50 million for the player.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians protested against President Dilma Rousseff, calling for her impeachment due to an economic downturn and a massive bribery scandal at state-run oil company Petrobras, where executives and politicians allegedly received bribes for contracts. Rousseff defended her position, denying involvement, but her approval rating plummeted to 13% after the protests, and the economy is expected to contract this year.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona, defending himself at the Laureus Sports Awards in Shanghai, insisted that his film "You and the Night," featuring racy scenes including him on his hands and knees in just his underwear, is a "piece of art" and not pornography. Cantona said the film is "beautiful" and praised its director, stating that such stories, when done by an artist, can be "too beautiful" and "confusing" for audiences.

Psychologists found that certain types of music can enhance flavors in food and drinks, with researchers suggesting that The Beatles' music can improve enjoyment of a fish and chip supper. In Shanghai, fish and chips are served with The Beatles playing, while in Spain, scented meringue is paired with commentary on Lionel Messi's actions, which highlights citrus flavors. Professor Charles Spence from Oxford University found that music can draw attention to certain notes in wine or food, potentially increasing enjoyment by up to 15%.

Players' chief Gordon Taylor insists Raheem Sterling is not disloyal to Liverpool by postponing contract talks until the summer, despite the 20-year-old England player receiving an £100,000-a-week offer from the club. Sterling has been linked with moves to Arsenal and Spanish clubs, and Taylor believes waiting until the season ends could be wise, citing Steven Gerrard's experience.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same company and lived just six minutes away. After receiving birth records for people born between 1964 and 1996, Mitchell-Clark connected with Simmons on Facebook and eventually met her. Simmons, who had always wanted to contact her daughter, was surprised to find Mitchell-Clark, who now knows she has three younger sisters.

Oscar 'Papoo' Hernandez Jr., a gun trafficker for convicted killer Aaron Hernandez, pleaded guilty to weapons charges. Hernandez shipped three guns, including an assault rifle and handguns, to Aaron Hernandez a month before Odin Lloyd's murder in April 2013. Hernandez, blinded by fame, was later beaten by inmates and spent time in solitary confinement. Hernandez now faces up to 30 months in prison.

Joel Parker, 33, was arrested in St Johns County, Florida, after throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head during a ride, threatening and disrupting the driver, according to police. The driver was not injured but called the police, leading to Parker's arrest for battery. He posted $250 bond and was issued a trespass warning, never allowed to use the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis discussed pre-season plans with striker Saido Berahino, indicating he plans to keep the 21-year-old beyond the summer transfer window despite Berahino's desire to play in Champions League football. Pulis said Berahino is happy at the club and has been working well, though the England under-21 striker is likely to be away with the national team until late June.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a project manager with German aid organization Welthungerlife, was abducted in Pakistan in 2012 by armed men and later killed in a U.S. drone strike in Afghanistan, along with American hostage Warren Weinstein. Lo Porto worked on reconstruction projects following Pakistan's 2010 flooding, which killed over 1,500 people. He was known for his humanitarian work and was described by colleagues as passionate and friendly.

Photographer John Massung captured images of hundreds of sharks, including Blacktips and Spinners, swarming just 100 feet from the beach at Sebastian Inlet, south Florida, on Thursday. The swarm was spotted by a fellow photographer further out and continued for about a mile down the shore. The sighting, shared on Facebook, raised concerns as the sharks migrated to breed in shallower waters.

An 11-year-old retired German Shepherd K-9 officer, Zeus, was honored in a heartwarming farewell procession by Ridgefield Police Department officers and residents on Wednesday before being put down due to severe hip disorder and declining health. The tribute began at 4:45 pm and ended at the Ridgefield Veterinary Hospital, with residents lining the streets to watch the procession. Zeus, who served eight years with the department, assisted with over 250 narcotics arrests and helped track down 50 missing or wanted individuals.

Reports of child sex abuse cases rose by more than 60% since Operation Yewtree, sparked by Jimmy Savile's assaults, with nearly 9,000 reports filed in 2014. Despite a 577% increase in South Yorkshire's reported cases, arrests fell by 9%, prompting critics to accuse the government of failing victims.

Iceland has become a popular filming location, with 17 production services companies established nationwide. Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Skaftafell National Park, Vatnajökull, and Dettifoss have been used in productions like Game of Thrones, Interstellar, Prometheus, and Thor: The Dark World, showcasing the island's stunning landscapes.

A blue and yellow 1862 bathing box on Melbourne's Brighton beach sold for $276,000, $150,000 over the original asking price, setting a record for the area. Meanwhile, a 1917 grey-fronted fire station in Sydney's Paddington sold for $1.2 million to be converted into a home, with its heritage façade preserved. In Victoria, a couple has listed an 1850s maximum security prison as a $2 million home, despite its haunted reputation.

40-year-old Samantha Rawcliffe, a mother from Morecambe, crashed her car after a rare brain disorder caused uncontrollable shaking and bladder control issues. Diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) in September, she now relies on a mobility scooter and takes 32 medications daily, unable to walk or drive. FND is an umbrella term for neurological symptoms with no known cause, making it rare and difficult to treat.

Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created a controversial Lucille Ball statue in Celoron, New York, has admitted to being disappointed in his work, offering to remake the bronze statue for free. The statue, based on Ball's famous drunk pitch scene, has been nicknamed 'Scary Lucy' and has drawn shock and horror from residents, leading to a social media campaign to have it removed. Poulin now pledges to create a new, more flattering statue for the town.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba, 22, will miss the remainder of the season with a torn knee ligament, ruling him out for around seven weeks after an injury sustained in Austria's 1-1 draw against Bosnia. Alaba, who had been in excellent form for Bayern, had been sidelined for three months earlier this season. He is set to start rehabilitation in about a month. Bayern, top of the Bundesliga, faces Porto in the Champions League quarter-finals.

Beatrice Nokes, 21, a University College London student, appeared in court accused of running a prostitution ring with suspended detective Daniel Williams, 37, who faces multiple charges including voyeurism and concealing profits. Nokes, whose parents are respected legal professionals, is accused of grooming three young women to sell sex, while Williams is charged with controlling prostitution and spying on clients.

A firm called Sequester, offering details of eating disorder sufferers for just 12p a head, has been selling information on 43 different health conditions, including skin problems, insomnia, and migraines, to Pharmacy2U, a UK online pharmacy. The Information Commissioner’s Office and Direct Marketing Commission are investigating, and the General Pharmaceutical Council is also probing. A whistleblower revealed the data, including personal financial and health information, which he said was available to anyone in the industry and could be used to scam vulnerable individuals.

Jordan Spieth, 21, won the Masters golf tournament, equalling Tiger Woods' 1997 record score of 18 under par. His 14-year-old sister Ellie, who could not attend, inspired him, and he expressed hope to win again in 50 years.

Sunderland's Dick Advocaat, facing the Wear-Tyne Derby against Newcastle, warns against underestimating the significance of the Old Firm rivalry, recalling his mistake from 1998 when he downplayed the derby's importance, leading to a 5-1 loss to Celtic. Sunderland, currently one point above the relegation zone, aims for three points rather than bragging rights, with Advocaat considering starting Adam Johnson despite his recent arrest.

A young woman, Belinda Bartholomew, claims she was racially abused and called names by a butcher at Sam the Butcher in Bondi, Sydney, when she tried to change her chicken selection for a Game of Thrones-inspired feast. The butcher denies the allegations, stating Bartholomew was the one being rude and agitated due to issues with his eftpos machine.

Cadbury reduced the size of Freddo Frogs from 20g to 12g, a 20% decrease, while keeping the price the same. The move was due to manufacturing cost increases, with the company citing unaffordable ingredient and packaging costs. The change sparked public backlash, with thousands voicing anger on Cadbury's Facebook page.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met in Brooklyn on Saturday, a day before her official announcement, with Robby Mook as campaign manager. The campaign's "values statement" outlines goals and principles, avoiding mistakes from Clinton's 2008 campaign, emphasizing humility, discipline, and unity. The document aims to be "Hillary for America," focusing on grassroots efforts and winning votes.

A 29-year-old woman, Kyli Wilfson, battled chronic pancreatitis for over a year and a half, unable to eat due to excruciating abdominal pain, despite feeling desperately hungry. Initially misdiagnosed with acute pancreatitis, she was finally diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis after a camera was inserted into her throat, leading to a permanent feeding tube. Her weight dropped to 80 lbs, and she postponed her wedding as she spent more time in hospitals.

Labour leader Ed Miliband was superimposed over London rapper Plan B in a meme, referencing his direct message to Prime Minister David Cameron to debate one-on-one. Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon posed sceptically, and the debate participants were placed in the Power Rangers lineup, with David Cameron and Nick Clegg superimposed over Gogglebox commentators.

Amir Khan, seeking a fight with the two best boxers, Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao, could face Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after waiting for Mayweather. Khan, who has sparred with Pacquiao, is now being offered a November or December fight in the Middle East by Pacquiao's promoter Bob Arum, who sees Khan as a potential draw. Khan would need to win his upcoming fight against Chris Algieri to secure the bout.

A tiny two-bedroom home, only 5 feet wide in some areas, sold for £750,000 in Islington, north London. Despite its narrow dimensions, the property, 8 feet 8 inches wide at its maximum, sold for almost double its 2001 price and garnered interest despite the estate agency's description of it as 'well proportioned.'

Nicola Sturgeon, Scotland's First Minister, launches an SNP election manifesto today, including policies that overlap with Labour, such as reducing tuition fees to £6,000 in England and rolling back NHS competition. The manifesto also includes plans to halt benefit changes and cancel Trident, aiming to form a 'progressive alliance' with Labour for a minority Labour government. The SNP is expected to win a majority of seats in Scotland, potentially triggering constitutional changes similar to those after the 1910 election.

Two mistakes by Rangers' Robby McCrorie—missing a corner and dropping a free kick—allowed Celtic to win the Glasgow Cup 2-0 at Hampden, clinching the trophy for the fourth time in eight seasons. Josh Kerr scored for Celtic, while Rangers missed several chances, including a handball penalty claim.

West Bromwich Albion's Tony Pulis led his team to a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, claiming he will never change his pre-game attire of cap, track suit, and white trainers. The win moved West Brom to 36 points, virtually guaranteeing their Premier League safety, much like he did at Crystal Palace last year.

Jameela Jamil, a television presenter, spent £3,000 to remove and replace all 10 of her amalgam fillings with white ones after experiencing health issues for nearly seven years, including puffy face, exhaustion, and fainting. Dental amalgam, used for robust back teeth, contains mercury, which can be released as vapour during fillings. Despite concerns, a review by the EU Commission's Scientific Committee concluded there was no risk from amalgam use.

Rap mogul Suge Knight, awaiting trial for murder and attempted murder, was denied bail reduction to $5 million. Knight, who hopes Floyd Mayweather will bail him out after Mayweather wins his next fight, was wheeled out of court in a wheelchair. Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Ronald Coen set 16 days for the trial unless a motion is made to continue. Knight, 48, has been hospitalized due to medical issues since his arrest in January.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine, 35, featured in Puss Puss magazine, posed with her British shorthair cat Kimchi at a lavish feast including caviar, salmon roe, and seafood sculptures. Kimchi, known for its discerning palate, loves human food like poppadoms and tortilla chips, with taramasalata being his "death row dish." Erskine admits Kimchi occasionally indulges in cat food but is also obsessed with Dreamies biscuits.

Martin Springall, 38, photographed his unnamed daughter near a rocky outcrop in Zushi, Japan, in 2014.
