The image, showing a pair of black boots behind the child, sparked debate on Reddit, with some suggesting they could be samurai boots, while others questioned if the boots were a trick of the light or paranormal. Springall insists there was no one else in the area and the photo was not Photoshopped.

Foreign workers in the UK will face a £22,000 tax bill before they can claim benefits under Tory plans, including a four-year ban on receiving state support and a six-month job requirement for those in work, announced by Home Secretary Theresa May. The measures aim to curb EU migration and limit access to benefits, following the government's failure to meet its net migration target.

Eight-year-old Cody Neatis, who has Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and is fed by a tube, has been sleeping on the floor in a hospital bed since arriving after a chest infection, as the facility lacks a special cot to keep him safe. Cody's mother, Lynne Neatis, 48, has slept with him on the mattress for a week, fearing he might injure himself or pull out his oxygen tubing. She demands answers from the local health trust, stating they have had two years to provide a suitable bed for Cody and other disabled children.

Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods are among the key figures at the Masters golf tournament, where McIlroy aims to complete a career grand slam, and Woods returns after a comeback. Ian Poulter forgot his golf clubs, and Henrik Stenson, recovering from flu, faces challenges. Tiger Woods will play with his children, and the 16th hole's par-three tradition sees few players successfully skipping their balls onto the green.

Juventus, who ruled out signing Manchester United's loan striker Radamel Falcao due to his high wages, expressed interest in Palermo's Paulo Dybala and Paris Saint-Germain's Edinson Cavani. Falcao, who has struggled at Manchester United, is expected to leave the club in the summer, with Juventus unable to afford him.

David Cameron plans to sell £4 billion worth of Lloyds Bank shares if re-elected, offering public shares at a 5% discount and allowing individuals to buy up to £10,000 worth. This would be the largest privatization since the Thatcher era, with a loyalty bonus for long-term holders. Police are investigating Tory MP Jesse Norman for allegedly giving out chocolate cake to voters during his re-election campaign.

Living near congested roads with high PM2.5 levels can cause ‘silent strokes,’ leading to brain damage and increasing dementia risk, according to a study. Researchers found that for every 10 micrograms per cubic meter increase in PM2.5, there was a 46% higher risk of silent strokes in over 900 people aged 60 and over. The study, published in Stroke, links air pollution to brain shrinkage and other cognitive issues.

Jessica Ainscough, a 'wellness warrior' battling epithelioid sarcoma, died in February after refusing chemotherapy and radiation. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, revealed she began targeted radiation in her final weeks, a risky decision she embraced despite scientific lack of support for Gerson Therapy. The treatment successfully shrunk her tumour but led to complications, with Pamenter saying Ainscough displayed courage and grace throughout their seven-year fight.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale, 2km south of Fernvale, on Wednesday afternoon. A 40-year-old man and a five-year-old boy were flown to Princess Alexandra Hospital with serious injuries, while a 27-year-old woman and a six-year-old girl were also taken to the same hospital with arm and abdominal injuries. Six others, including an infant and two young girls, were taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries. The highway was closed for a few hours with diversions in place south of Fernvale, and emergency crews used hydraulic cutting gear to free a trapped person.

Jason McDonald, a 34-year-old alligator farm manager from Colorado, walked a 10-foot-wide slackline over a pool containing over 50 alligators, some up to ten feet long, at the Colorado Gator Farm. The alligators, initially wary, did not seem bothered by the rope, and McDonald plans to attempt walking over larger and albino alligators in the future. He has never been bitten before but was clamped by an 8-foot alligator for over 10 minutes last month.

Abdul Hadi Arwani, a Syrian imam and Muslim Brotherhood activist, was shot dead in London on a quiet street near Paddocks and Greenhill, Wembley, after being called to provide a building quote. Days before his death, Arwani visited the area with his son, and the supposed client asked him to return another day, suggesting the man might have been a hired killer. Scotland Yard is investigating whether the man was a hired assassin who postponed the hit because Arwani was not alone.

Hong Kong's tiny Jenny's cookie shop, known for "little bear cookies," has become a black market hit, with tourists and locals lining up for hours to buy $9 tins. Knockoffs are now sold by bakeries, and the original shop warns against buying 'fake' cookies. The frenzy has led to resellers buying in bulk and reselling at a 70% markup. Similar food crazes, like cronuts and ramen burgers, have also swept other parts of the world, though they often fade quickly.

Kira Hollis, a 27-year-old from Tamworth, Staffordshire, diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and depression, gained weight and improved her mental health by becoming a bodybuilder. Initially ordered to the gym to gain weight, she turned her life around and now works as a personal trainer. Her daughter Olivia and boyfriend Michael Dennis supported her recovery, and her story went viral online.

Jockey Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular double somersault fall from favorite Merrion Square at Wincanton on Wednesday, sustaining only a cut on his nose. The fall, caught on video, has been viewed by hundreds of thousands online. Ferguson, who was mucking out the stables as usual, said he was undeterred and plans to return to racing, aiming to compete in the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree.

Hillary Clinton launched her 2016 presidential campaign with a video and road trip, aiming to reframe herself as empathetic and relatable. Critics like Ruth Marcus dismissed her launch as vapid, but her team may have successfully rebranded Clinton, projecting a more confident and forward-looking image. The campaign's logo, introduced later, further reinforces this new identity, targeting everyday Americans.

More than 1,700 Chinese freshmen students took an exam in a high school playground in Yichuan, Shaanxi province on Saturday, due to lack of indoor space. The students organized the outdoor exam themselves, rotating their chairs and desks to avoid sun glare, and believed it would help them feel more relaxed and prevent cheating. The school saw it as a test of students' organizing capacity.

A lucky reader will win a pair of Joe Hart-signed Nike Magista Obra boots, a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor, and shaving gel, valued at £14.99, in a competition closing on April 19. Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart is a Gillette ambassador, making this a unique chance to own his autographed gear.

One-year-old baby orangutan Kecil, rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate, found a loving home with 53-year-old surrogate mother Maggie at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. After 10 months of care, Kecil now cuddles with Maggie ahead of his first public outing this weekend, following a turning point when he ran to her during a fire alarm.

Noelle Baynham, a 61-year-old from Winchester, Hampshire, died after an accidental overdose of medication. Her body was found partially eaten by her two dogs, a Jack Russell and Staffordshire Bull Terrier, who had been locked in the house for days. The cause of death was an accidental overdose, but the pathologist could not determine the exact cause because the dogs had consumed her vital organs.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, a multiple gold medalist, will stand trial for fraud over match-fixing allegations, including betting on a Montpellier match that the team lost to a struggling team. The trial, likely to occur within months, could result in up to five years in prison for Karabatic, who was previously banned by the French league for his involvement. Other former or current Montpellier players are also facing trial.

Six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were jailed for a total of 31 years after being convicted of sexually abusing teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. The victims, aged 13 to 16, were targeted at under-18s parties organized by Hassan-Sule, who was described as a "celebrity" by the judge. The judge rejected the defense's argument that the victims were lying, emphasizing the emotional impact on the young victims.

Aaron Hernandez, former New England Patriots player, will face another murder trial after being convicted of killing Odin Lloyd, with prosecutors alleging he fatally shot Daniel de Abreu and Safiro Furtado in July 2012. Hernandez is also facing two civil suits and a $5 million asset freeze, pending the outcome of the murder trial.

The Emirates Airline will rebrand the FA Cup as the Emirates FA Cup in a £30 million, three-year deal, adding to their existing sports sponsorship portfolio which includes a £150 million deal with Arsenal and a £80 million deal with AC Milan.

Michael Phelps, 29, aiming for a fifth Olympic appearance in Rio, confirmed he will compete in the Olympics next year but won't participate in the world championships in Russia this summer due to a six-month suspension from USA Swimming for a second DUI arrest.

Gareth Bale, a key Real Madrid forward, is sidelined with a calf injury and a muscular lesion in his soleus muscle, likely missing Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday. Real Madrid also lacks Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who is out for six weeks with a knee ligament strain.

Scientists warn older people are more susceptible to emotional decisions in retirement, leading to significant financial losses. In the 2007-2008 global financial crisis, 50% of pensioners panicked and sold investments, losing £37,000 compared to £141,000 had they held onto them. New pension reforms allow Britons over 55 to access their savings, but experts advise managing emotions to avoid similar mistakes.

Stuart Pearce, former Manchester City player and manager, believes Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to turn around Manchester City's Premier League fortunes. City's recent 2-0 loss to Manchester United has compounded their struggles, but Pearce argues the club should retain Pellegrini, who has been at the helm since 2012. Pearce cited fading influence of Ivorian midfielder Yaya Toure as a key factor in City's poor form.

Manchester United trained in the sunshine ahead of their Premier League derby with Manchester City on Sunday, with stars Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera, and Robin van Persie back in action. United are one point behind City in the table and aim to end their seven-game winning run at Old Trafford, where they last won 2-1 in 2011.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona at home, conceding a late goal from substitute Mounir Obbadi, dropping nine points behind third-placed AS Roma and leaving them in sixth place. Former West Ham midfielder Alessandro Diamanti missed a penalty in the 65th minute, and Alberto Gilardino's penalty was saved by Verona's Rafael, allowing Obbadi to score the decisive goal in the 90th minute.

Miley Cyrus, at the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, displayed armpit hair in a social media snap, causing a social media stir. Some users advised her to shave, while others defended her choice, noting that men's armpit hair is generally accepted.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez scored 102 goals this season, including six penalties and two free-kicks, after netting six in a 6-0 win over Getafe, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi has 49 goals, Neymar 32, and Suarez 21, with all but nine of their 102 goals coming from inside the box.

44-year-old pedestrian Andrea McVeigh was left scarred for life after being hit by a cyclist riding on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene, prompting McVeigh's husband to chase him. She suffered two three-inch gashes to her forehead and other injuries. Police have issued CCTV footage and an appeal for the cyclist, who is suspected of causing significant facial injuries and fleeing the scene.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 and ordered to do 150 hours of unpaid work after pleading guilty to dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by falsely claiming he could only walk 200 metres, despite being a keen walker. The fraud was exposed when council officials read a newspaper article about his 191-mile hike in Cumbria, which showed he had also walked in Wales shortly before applying for the badge.

Apple has patented a facial recognition system that unlocks devices by scanning a user's face with the front-facing camera when the phone is moved into a specific position. The patent, filed in 2011 and awarded this week, aims to automatically unlock a device if the scanned face matches a previously stored image, eliminating the need for PINs, passwords, or fingerprints. Android users already have a similar feature called Trusted Face.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, a cancer patient battling multiple myeloma, was forcibly removed from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California along with her family because she lacked a doctor's note, leading to an emotional video of her family being kicked off a packed plane. The airline was concerned she might collapse during the eight-hour flight, but her oncologist later cleared her to fly.

Three people, including the owner of a $120,000 1973 E-Type Jaguar, were taken to hospital after a head-on collision with a Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night at a traffic light intersection on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney. The crash, which left the classic car completely destroyed, did not result in any injuries. NSW police are investigating, warning that the Easter long weekend is a high-risk period for traffic incidents.

Google is setting up a four-person team to develop and test battery technologies for phones, tablets, and electric cars, including flexible and wearable options. The team has been working on similar projects since 2012, when former Apple battery expert Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj led a testing team. Google has also been collaborating with AllCell Technologies to develop batteries for Project Loon, which requires functioning at subfreezing temperatures.

The 223ft Explorer, a superyacht designed by Tony Castro, comes with a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests, including car and jet ski storage. It costs approximately 40 million euros to build and is intended for the ultra-wealthy, who can also bring their own car on board.

Labour leader Ed Miliband plans to impose rent controls despite warnings from experts, who say it will slash investment in new housing and lead to more evictions, while Labour figures and some experts support the move to help 'forgotten' renters. Critics argue the plans have loopholes and could discourage investment, leading to higher rents in the long term.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town supporter, Ryan Dearnley, was removed from his role as a Reading mascot for the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after he posted a video saying he hopes Arsenal win, sparking outrage from Reading fans. The Football Association moved him away from the match to avoid a negative reception, instead offering him an England mascot role.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may explain a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, a region 20% less dense than other parts. If confirmed, this would be the largest structure ever found by humanity, according to Hawaii scientists. The supervoid, a region with less matter, could sap light passing through it, causing it to lose energy and appear colder.

The red, worn chair where Abraham Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre in 1865 will be displayed at the Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, on April 15 for the 150th anniversary of the assassination. Two days earlier, renowned historian Doris Kearns Goodwin will deliver a lecture at the museum. The chair, which has a dark stain believed to be blood, has been on display at the museum since 1930.

Jake Boys, 19, from Hailsham, booked plane tickets to Dublin instead of Cardiff for a One Direction concert, surprising his girlfriend Emily Canham, 18, from Kettering, who thought Cardiff was in Ireland. The couple, both vloggers, are planning to take a train to the gig on June 5-6.

Romanian company MB Telecom unveiled the Roboscan 2M Aeria, a mobile X-ray scanner capable of detecting contraband, bombs, and weapons inside planes. The device, costing €3 million, is being used to inspect trucks at borders in Eastern Europe, where it has seized 76,000 packs of illegal cigarettes. Currently, it can scan entire planes in about 20 minutes, filling a security gap for low-security airports, and the company claims it can detect weapons and other contraband.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, described as having a 'fanatical obsession' with young girls, has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit near Hook, Hampshire. Last seen leaving the Winchfield hospital, Munden was last detained under the Mental Health Act for sexually touching a three-year-old girl. Officers are searching for him, who is about 5ft 8ins tall, heavy build, and has dark hair, possibly having shaved his beard.

Middlesbrough lead the Championship with four weeks to go, seven points ahead of second-place Bournemouth, who lost 1-0 to Watford. With Watford and Norwich also playing, Boro's victory over Watford on Monday could secure their promotion, while Bournemouth's defeat could hand the top spot to Derby, which has lost seven of their last eight games.

Instagram users are embracing grey hair, using the hashtag #grannyhair, with models and regular people posting images online, creating a trend that has gained popularity, especially among women seeking a feminist or quirky fashion statement, as seen in catwalk shows by designers like Jean Paul Gaultier.

Randy and Jodi Speidel, a couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, struggling with chronic conditions, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning in their bedroom, two months after creating online fundraisers on GiveForward.com and GoFundMe.com for financial help. They had been living without gas, water, and electricity, and were left with only $33. The couple, who had removed their cats to avoid poisoning, left a note warning of carbon monoxide and a suicide note.

Nick Clegg vowed to remain Liberal Democrat leader despite potential election losses, stating he would fight for his job 'in all circumstances,' as the party faces the risk of losing its current number of MPs and potentially being left out of power. Clegg emphasized his commitment to lead the party through the next Parliament, warning of the risk of the Labour and Conservative parties vacating the center ground.

A 79-year-old pensioner, Terry Cooper, was saved from a badger attack by his Jack Russell dog Sam, which dragged him back indoors after the badger, described as the size of a pig with six-inch teeth, burst through a hedge. Following the incident, the National Farmers' Union advised residents on protecting their properties from badgers, suggesting measures like covering gaps in fences and using badger-proof fencing.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto U21s on Wednesday at his son's club, Fulham, avoiding Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid's Champions League matches. Mourinho joked with Fulham's goalkeeping coach and seemed in good spirits, while his team Chelsea had already crashed out of the Champions League. Chelsea are closing in on their first Premier League title since 2010, with six games remaining.

Andreas Christopheros, 29, was critically injured when corrosive liquid was thrown at his home in Truro, Cornwall. He lost vision and facial scars. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, has been charged with perverting the course of justice, while her husband David Phillips, 48, was charged with grievous bodily harm with intent.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has posted signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the path, drawing both complaints from residents and amusement from some pilgrims. The signs, showing a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line, have become an attraction as some pilgrims pose for photos with them.

A massive fire consumed a building formerly housing a strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon, according to MLive. Only the building and a few nearby power lines were affected, though the site was not vacant, officials said.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent, Shoshana Hebshi, reached a $40,000 settlement in a lawsuit against the federal government, Frontier Airlines, and the Wayne County Airport Authority after being strip-searched at Detroit Metropolitan Airport on the 10th anniversary of 9/11. The incident occurred when Hebshi was detained for hours after being removed from a plane with two Indian-American men, whom TSA agents suspected of spending time in the bathroom.

Twenty people were injured after an Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 made a crash landing and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, believed to have missed the landing point on the runway and spun 180 degrees after impact. The Airbus A320 had departed from Incheon International Airport in South Korea and was en route to Hiroshima when it reportedly had a tailstrike. Emergency services are at the scene, with injured passengers taken to hospital. The airport has been closed.

Made In Chelsea star Mark-Francis Vandelli, son of a multimillionaire industrialist, has a watch collection worth several thousand pounds. He buys a new watch each year, boasting 16 eye-wateringly expensive pieces, including a £32,000 Cartier Moonphase and a £6,500 Bulgari Chrono 42. His most prized watch is a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, no longer made, which he wears to rave nights in East London.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is auctioning over 200 antiques worth up to £100,000, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt and a longbow, as he downsizes his home. The items, valued at up to £4,000, reflect his interest in military history and classic literature.

Brazilian commuter Nelson Felippe posted a photo on a train platform in Rio de Janeiro, expressing his disapproval of two women hugging. The post, cleverly mocking conservative attitudes, went viral after being shared over 100,000 times in 24 hours. Felippe, who works at the Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, actually criticized a man standing on the yellow safety line, warning against the normalization of such behavior in public spaces.

A young English cricket fan named Jonathan Stevenson, aged 16, wrote to Richie Benaud, a legendary Australian cricket spin bowler, for tips on left-handed leg spin bowling in 1996. Benaud, now deceased, responded with a detailed letter and a full sheet of notes, offering advice on different deliveries and emphasizing the differences in coaching for left-handed bowlers. Stevenson shared Benaud's response on Twitter as a tribute to the cricket legend.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts the future of travel will involve sharing virtual reality environments, allowing users to experience world locations from multiple viewpoints without physical travel. Facebook plans to support virtual reality on its newsfeed and explore immersive videos using Oculus Rift, a virtual reality headset.

A loving boyfriend arranged for professional wedding photographs to be taken for his girlfriend Dong Hui, 22, who is bedridden in a hospital due to bone cancer. Despite her condition, Dong was dressed in a wedding dress and posed with her boyfriend Guo Kai, who has been by her side every day. The couple had planned to marry in Sichuan this month but postponed the ceremony due to Dong's illness.

Police in Houston charged a 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, with intoxication manslaughter and failure to stop after three separate DUI crashes within three hours, killing a 6-year-old boy and a homeless man, and injuring his mother. Boudreaux, with a history of DUIs, was arrested after running a red light and crashing into a Honda Civic, then later dozing off and killing a pedestrian on Texas 5 Spur.

Microsoft announced a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions at its Redmond campus in Washington, partnering with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit that trains individuals with autism for IT careers. This follows Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's apology for comments suggesting women should trust the system to pay them fairly, highlighting the company's focus on diversity.

Two deputies in Tulsa, Oklahoma, involved in the fatal arrest of Eric Harris were reassigned due to threats against them and their families. They were not charged but criticized for their actions during the arrest, including pinning Harris' head to the ground. Bates, one of the deputies, shot Harris with a handgun after calling for a Taser, leading to a manslaughter charge. The sheriff apologized to Harris' family and said the FBI cleared the agency of civil rights violations.

A couple, Katie Prager and Dalton Prager, both 24, married in their teens and suffer from cystic fibrosis. Katie, diagnosed with an infection in her lungs, urgently needs a lung transplant but her insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not cover the out-of-state treatment at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Dalton, who already received new lungs, is pleading for help as doctors predict Katie will not live a year without a transplant.

New data from the Sleep Cycle app shows South Africans wake up earliest on Mondays at 6:09 am, while Americans wake up latest at 8:24 am on Fridays. Countries report the best sleep quality on Wednesdays, with 58% of surveyed nations experiencing their best sleep on this day, including China.

A collection of 25 unpublished love letters from Mexican artist Frida Kahlo to her lover Jose Bartoli, written between 1946 and 1949, is expected to fetch up to $120,000 at an auction. The letters, penned in Spanish and saved by Jose until his death in 1995, reveal details of Kahlo's secret three-year romance with Bartoli while married to Diego Rivera.

British trade union leader Len McCluskey, head of Unite, campaigned for Labour during a sunny election visit in South Wales, charming activists with his warm demeanor. However, his union's influence on Labour candidates is alarming, given its socialist policies and potential for using its financial and organizational muscle to revert Britain to the 1970s era of high union power and state intervention.

Zookeeper Elad Hershkowitz filmed 30 hours of animals drinking water using a GoPro camera placed in their troughs at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv. The footage, culled into four minutes, showcased unique drinking methods from a variety of animals, including a rhino almost kissing the water and a lemur delicately licking it. Initially, some animals were sceptical but eventually adapted to the presence of the camera.

A poll reveals that only 25% of voters think David Cameron is the hungriest to win the election, while 43% believe Ed Miliband is most up for the fight, despite Mr. Cameron insisting he is working hard. This contrasts with Mr. Cameron's frequent portrayal as the strongest leader.

A man charged with assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov, Zaur Dadaev, has retracted his confession to the murder, saying he was beaten and pressured into confessing. Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused of the crime, appeared in court via video link, contradicting his previous confession and sparking claims of torture.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from under collapsed rubble 22 hours after a 7.8-magnitude earthquake in Nepal, killing over 5,000 people. Sonit was rescued by the Nepalese Army on Sunday morning, his eyes still closed, after being trapped alive under debris for 22 hours.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization, Narconon, is attempting to have a 40-acre property near Camp David, Maryland, designated as historic to circumvent zoning laws and build a drug rehab center. The property, previously bought by Narconon for $4.85 million, is currently zoned for resource conservation and cannot be used for medical purposes. Narconon claims the site has historical significance due to President Herbert Hoover's fishing trip there, while opponents argue it is a tactic to bypass regulations and create a potentially dangerous program.

In Kabul, five English-speaking former NATO workers, fired and blacklisted, struggle to survive in the city's market stalls, fearing reprisals and isolation. The population has grown fivefold since NATO's arrival, leaving many of the city's former Western enclaves empty.

One US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured on Friday while swimming in a pool at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia. The incident occurred during routine training, with both SEALs not wearing gear and not performing dives. They were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two. The second service member is in critical condition. An investigation is ongoing.

One season, NBC expects more Americans to watch Premier League matches live than in Britain. US interest in the league has doubled in two years, with 32 million Americans watching last season. NBC moved its entire production to England this weekend, including star anchor Rebecca Lowe, who covered Burnley's match against Arsenal with former MLS star Kyle Martino and Robbie Earle.

Boris Johnson, London Mayor, clashed with Ed Miliband, Labour leader, on the BBC's Andrew Marr Show, with Johnson accusing Miliband of potentially harming the country more than his brother did. The encounter turned into a shouting match, but Miliband laughed off Johnson's attack.

A prisoner in Oregon, Dustin Irons, flashed a judge during a video court hearing, leading to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court. Irons, already serving time for assault and mischief, was known as a difficult inmate and was restrained during the incident.

McLaren driver Jenson Button believes his team has made significant progress since starting the Formula One season poorly in Australia, with improved pace in Malaysia. Button and team-mate Fernando Alonso retired in Malaysia but saw the car competitive with midfield runners. McLaren now aims to race with Force Indias, Saubers, and Lotuses, with Button optimistic about their improvement but acknowledging more work is needed.

A hospital in Western Australia, Fiona Stanley Hospital, was stripped of its medical service provider Serco after failing to return sterilizing equipment by February, resulting in a $60,000 fine. The hospital was found to have blood and bone fragments on some medical instruments, damaging its public image and causing concerns among staff and patients.

A couple, Becca Litchfield and Dale, from Nottingham, chose to forgo their dream wedding to fund one final attempt at in vitro fertilization (IVF). Despite two unsuccessful rounds of IVF, they won a wedding competition and successfully conceived twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley.

A family-friendly coffee shop's Facebook page was hacked and flooded with adult content after an employee clicked on a malicious link, locking out staff for almost 24 hours. The hacker posted inappropriate images similar to those seen on other hacked brands, including Crayola. Scooter's Coffee apologized and Facebook only responded after larger businesses reported the issue.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center barked and whined after meeting a husky, causing amusement among onlookers who filmed the interaction. The Shibu Inu's vocalizations, usually beginning around two-to-three weeks old, escalated into a noisy exchange with the husky, with both dogs eventually settling down.

England seamer Liam Plunkett, back in Test contention after a minor injury, aims to use his pace to lead England against the West Indies. He is competing with Chris Jordan and uncapped Mark Wood for a spot in the first Test series in Antigua, April 13. Plunkett emphasizes his adaptability and desire to "rough up" batsmen, contrasting his approach with those of more traditional bowlers.

Paul Smith, having lost to Arthur Abraham twice, faces a third challenge against Andre Ward, a reigning world champion, in a potential warm-up fight before a rematch with Carl Froch. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to meet in a unification fight, with Ward preferring to travel to London rather than Froch's hometown in Nottingham.

Residents of Parma, Missouri, were shocked when five of its six police officers and several other top officials resigned after the city's first black mayor, Tyrus Byrd, was elected. The officials cited 'safety concerns' in their resignations, but Byrd and outgoing mayor Randall Ramsey have no explanation for the departures. The city, with a population of 713, has suffered recent break-ins despite a large police force.

Manchester City will make midfielder Yaya Toure available this summer, despite the club considering his future, though he is content at the club and unlikely to leave for less than £220,000 per week. Inter Milan is interested in Toure, but there are doubts about the club's ability to afford his wages. City will not force Toure out but are set to sell him, with Valencia attempting to block a move for Alvaro Negredo to fund a transfer for Radamel Falcao.

A new study found that more than two-thirds (69%) of people taking antidepressants do not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder, a condition also known as clinical depression. The research, focusing on selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), suggests many are prescribed these drugs without clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller, the mother of Natalie, 28, who suffered from bipolar disorder and psychosis, wrote about her daughter's suicide in Baltimore. Natalie's illness, undiagnosed until her early 20s, worsened over years, leading Fuller to describe her daughter as "the bravest person I have ever known." Despite treatments, Natalie stopped taking her medication, causing her condition to deteriorate, culminating in her death by stepping in front of a train.

Koby Hodder, a 10-year-old boy, suffered a cardiac arrest and collapsed during a British Bulldog game in the school playground, losing consciousness for 12 minutes. His heart stopped for 12 minutes after he was playing the game, and he was later diagnosed with a condition similar to that of footballer Fabrice Muamba. Teachers performed CPR until paramedics arrived and used a defibrillator to revive him.

Britain’s most senior female judge Baroness Hale of Richmond called for divorce laws to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame, suggesting couples should sort out arrangements for children and money before obtaining a divorce, and introducing a one-year cooling-off period.

Tottenham Hotspur are considering a new stadium with a retractable pitch to potentially host a new NFL London franchise, with a design that could include extra-large changing rooms and a synthetic surface underneath for NFL-style games. The stadium, expected to be completed by 2018, could be more suitable for American football than Wembley Stadium, which hosts NFL games but lacks the sightlines needed for large crowds.

U.S. senators, including John McCain and Robert Menendez, wrote to FIFA urging Russia to be removed as host of the 2018 World Cup due to Russia's role in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea, calling it inappropriate and providing economic relief to a regime under international sanctions.

Universal announced "Fifty Shades Darker" sequel will release on February 10, 2017, with husband of author EL James, Niall Leonard, writing the script. Dakota Johnson and Jamie Dornan are negotiating higher pay for the film after the first film's massive worldwide earnings of $568.8 million. Sam Taylor-Johnson, who directed the first film, is not returning.

West Brom manager Tony Pulis, 57, faces a challenging return to Crystal Palace after seven seasons in the Premier League, where he has never finished higher than 11th. Despite his success at Stoke City and Palace, Pulis has yet to guide a team into the top half of the table, leaving him uncertain about his future success in the top flight despite recent positive performances.

Fenerbahçe, while their team bus was attacked with gunfire near the airport following a match, called for the suspension of the Turkish championship. The bus driver was wounded, and the club stated that as long as the attack is not satisfactorily resolved, a championship suspension is inevitable.

A massive avalanche hit Everest Base Camp, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens in Nepal following a devastating earthquake. The quake, which claimed over 4,300 lives, also trapped hundreds of climbers and local hires high on the mountain, complicating rescue efforts due to damaged icefall routes and aftershocks.

87-year-old Gregory Margolin, a WWII Jewish veteran, found himself in another war in Ukraine, this time as a sniper commander. After surviving the Nazis, he lost his daughter in a missile attack in Donetsk. He and his family immigrated to Israel, where he now lives in relative safety.

John Carver, now fighting for the head coach position at Newcastle, faces the daunting task of avoiding a repeat of Ruud Gullit's 1999 defeat to Sunderland in a Tyne-Wear derby. Gullit's controversial decision to leave out Alan Shearer and Duncan Ferguson led to his dismissal after Newcastle lost 2-1, a memory Carver hopes to avoid.

Revered Al Sharpton attended a vigil in North Charleston for Walter Scott, a black man fatally shot by a white police officer, and preached at Charity Missionary Baptist Church, addressing the Scott case and the need for police reform. Elected officials and police were in attendance, including North Charleston Mayor Keith Summey and Police Chief Eddie Driggers, who listened intently to Sharpton's sermon.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the winger hit the headlines for passing out after allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide and puffing on a shisha pipe before scoring the opening goal in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Rodgers said he would speak with Sterling about the demands of being a professional, including off-field behavior.

Labour received over £1.1 million in union donations during the final week of the election campaign, more than twice as much as the Conservatives who received £492,512. Unions like Unison, USDAW, and Unite contributed over £700,000, with most donations coming from Labour's main union supporters.

Police were called twice to a Qatar Airways flight diverted to Birmingham Airport due to severe winds, where passengers became disruptive after being stranded for five hours. Some passengers were left waiting for transport and slept for two days, while the airline apologized for the delay, stating it was caused by crew exceeding flying hours.

Canadian pop star Justin Bieber will accompany boxing champion Floyd Mayweather into the ring for his $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao, marking the biggest fight in history. The 21-year-old performer, known for his close friendship with Mayweather, will lead the American boxer's entourage at the MGM Grand.

Corinthian Colleges Inc., once enrolling over 70,000 students, announced its shutdown of all 28 campuses, marking a positive step in holding for-profit colleges accountable. These schools, which often offer dubious degrees and high debt, receive 86% of their funding from federal student loans, contributing to nearly half of all student loan defaults. Corinthian's closure follows the U.S. Department of Education's curtailment of its access to federal student aid last summer, and the organization's graduates joined a "debt strike," with Education Secretary Arne Duncan signaling potential loan forgiveness for those with no job prospects.

Pep Guardiola, Bayern Munich manager, denied claims of a dispute with former club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the team after the Champions League quarter-final defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the medical staff was blamed for the loss, citing a damaged bond of trust, while Guardiola blamed his own team's injuries and said the responsibility lay with him.

Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, 39, will defend his world title against Bryant Jennings at Madison Square Garden in New York, recalling his Olympic gold medal win in 1996 that catapulted him into Ukrainian hero status. Despite being just shy of his 40th birthday, Klitschko, who has not fought in the US in seven years, remains dominant and believes age is no barrier to his continued success.

Jeremy Clarkson, fired from Top Gear in March for assaulting a producer, expressed his gratitude for support but admitted he would miss being on the show. Former presenter Angela Rippon, 70, said she would be keen to return if invited, while the future of the BBC2 motoring series remains uncertain.

Barcelona's 1-0 victory over Celta Vigo on Sunday featured a bizarre incident where Celta striker Fabian Orellana was shown a red card for throwing a lump of grass at Barcelona midfielder Sergio Busquets, who then grabbed his eye after being struck. Orellana was ejected by referee Inaki Vicandi Garrido, while Barcelona secured crucial points despite Real Madrid's 9-1 win against Granada.

Boston Marathon organizers and a federal judge have asked a jury to avoid attending this year's race or related events due to the upcoming sentencing of Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who was convicted in the 2013 bombing. The sentencing phase begins April 21, with the judge warning jurors not to be influenced by the event.

Tens of millions of Chinese people marked the Qingming Festival by traveling home to clean graves and honor their ancestors, burning fake money and leaving offerings. In Huangling County, Shaanxi Province, a grand ceremony was held in honor of the Yellow Emperor Huangdi, considered the founding father of the Chinese nation. The festival, celebrated for its springtime beauty and outdoor celebrations, falls in the first week of April and is one of 24 Chinese solar terms.

Quarter of a century after his last number one, Paul Simon, 73, topped the UK album chart with The Ultimate Collection, outselling albums by Ed Sheeran, James Bay, and Sam Smith. His recent tour with Sting is believed to have contributed to his return to the top, marking his first chart-topping album since 1990.

Iker Casillas, Real Madrid's longtime goalkeeper, insists he will stay at the club despite David de Gea's potential summer move to Manchester United, stating he will fight for the starting position until his contract ends. Casillas, 33, has been at Real Madrid since 1996 and hopes to fulfill his commitment until the end of his deal.

Britain saw its highest employment level in history, with 557,000 more people in work in the three months to February, according to official figures. This coincided with international praise for Chancellor George Osborne from the International Monetary Fund, which noted the UK had created more jobs in the last five years than the rest of the EU combined.

Korea's SsangYong launches a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli, starting at £12,950, aimed at budget-conscious drivers. The Tivoli offers manual and automatic transmissions with six-speed options, seven airbags, and a choice of front-wheel drive or 4x4. It comes in three trim levels with SE, EX, and ELX options, including features like smart steering, parking sensors, and a TomTom navigation system. SsangYong expects the Tivoli to boost its UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 annually.

A chef named Sam Longhurst created a 10-inch tall, half-kilogram burger at Splendid Kitchen in Manchester, containing six different forms of meat totaling 2,000 calories. The burger includes two beef patties, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, a whole fried chicken thigh, barbecued pulled pork, and bacon rashers, described as a "monster of a burger" by the chef.

Yeo Valley, a yogurt maker, offers a Michelin-starred staff canteen with organic, locally sourced meals for as little as £2, including dishes like soft-poached quail egg with confit of tomato and deep-fried polenta. The canteen, overlooking Blagdon countryside, serves 120 dairy workers and is now open to the public at higher prices, featuring daily menu changes and high-quality ingredients from nearby farms.

Legendary blues musician B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration due to Type II diabetes, but he recovered quickly and was back home with his family, according to his daughter. King, 89, has 30 Grammy nominations and is known for hits like "The Thrill Is Gone" and collaborations with U2.

Manhattan's Fifth Avenue was adorned with bizarre Easter hats as thousands participated in the annual parade, featuring everything from simple bunny ears to elaborate dioramas inspired by city officials. The event included a mix of religious attendees and secular revelers, with participants ranging from conservative to whimsical in their headwear choices.

Emergency crews in Essex dispatched two ambulances to Epping Forest after a caller reported a person hit by a car, only to discover the "victim" was a squirrel. The East of England ambulance service has released a list of 1,248 "bizarre and irritating" calls, with front-line crews responding to almost half, potentially endangering lives. Calls included a dropped burger bleeding, a woman claiming to be locked out, and a man complaining of lethargy after dieting.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake, along with teammates Loic Remy and Willian, participated in an Audi-sponsored football challenge. In the challenge, the Chelsea players scored 6-0 in the final round, defeating their teammates. Willian accidentally broke the wing mirror of an Audi with a long-range shot, causing amusement among the spectators.

Brendan Rodgers, Liverpool manager, criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor Aidy Ward, suggesting Sterling is being influenced by outside forces. Rodgers revealed he has spoken with Sterling, advising him to stay at Liverpool for now despite Arsenal's interest, as Sterling has two years left on his contract and Rodgers believes Liverpool is the best place for his development.

Countdown co-presenter Rachel Riley was embarrassed during an episode when contestants offered the eight-letter word 'erection' as the answer to a word game. Host Nick Hewer, trying to stifle his laughter, failed to stop himself. The word 'erection' is not the first rude word to appear on the show, with previous examples including 'todgers' and 'm*nges'.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who tried to buy deadly poison online was spared jail after pleading guilty to trying to buy the toxin. The teenager, unaware his online requests were being tracked by anti-terror officers, expressed a desire to commit suicide. Officers from the North West Counter Terrorism Unit intervened, arresting him and a girl who was also part of the investigation.

Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four, died three hours after giving birth to her baby girl at North Manchester General Hospital, where three other babies and one mother had died in the previous eight months. The hospital's maternity units were subsequently investigated, and the family called for action to prevent further tragedies. Ms. Hindle was taken to the hospital early December 15, suffering from preterm labor, and died of a cardiac arrest shortly after giving birth. Her family claims she was left alone with a student midwife following the birth, raising concerns about the care she received.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after posting a video of herself training while eight months pregnant. The 32-year-old plans to compete in the 2016 Rio Olympics, continuing her rigorous training regimen right up until her final trimester. Emily was born at a healthy 3.1 kilograms on Monday.

At least one person died and four were missing after a powerful storm capsized several sailboats during the 57th Dauphin Island Regatta in Mobile Bay, Alabama. The storm, which hit around 4 p.m., left boats scattered across a wide area, including Dauphin Island Bridge and Fort Morgan. Rescue efforts continued into the night, with one person rescued by the Coast Guard.

Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, eye diseases that progressively steal vision. Her doctors have not provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. Macular degeneration affects central vision, while glaucoma damages peripheral vision. Both conditions are more common after age 60 and can be influenced by genetic predisposition, high blood pressure, and other risk factors.

An Oklahoma jury convicted 17-year-old Chancey Allen Luna of first-degree murder for shooting and killing Christopher Lane, an Australian college baseball player, while he was jogging in Duncan, Oklahoma. The jury recommended life in prison without parole, despite defense attorneys arguing Luna meant only to scare Lane.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger insists his 12-0 record against Jose Mourinho will not affect their top-of-the-table clash with Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium. Wenger has lost seven and drawn five of their 12 meetings, including a 2-0 loss in October. Despite their past, Wenger says the result will depend on the day's performance, as Arsenal are on a good run and want to beat Chelsea at home. Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas will return for Chelsea, and Wenger requests respect for Fabregas, who left Arsenal for Barcelona in 2011.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer born into poverty, has become a global superstar after mega-fights against notable opponents like Oscar De La Hoya and Juan Manuel Marquez. He rose through the weight divisions, fighting in the Far East before achieving his big break in Las Vegas in 2001. Pacquiao is set to face Floyd Mayweather in the "Fight of the Century" on the Las Vegas Strip, a showdown that has been anticipated for years.

Aston Villa's Jack Grealish, a top flight starlet, was photographed inhaling nitrous oxide during Aston Villa's FA Cup semi-final win against Liverpool at Wembley. This incident, though legal, has raised concerns about his fitness for top-level sports, with former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger emphasizing the importance of maintaining a professional attitude and healthy lifestyle for athletes.

Sam Barton, who underwent £55,000 of cosmetic surgery, including two NHS procedures, was attacked with eggs by a group of men on Easter Monday in Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands, after posting about his appearance on Facebook. The incident occurred after he had been filmed with reality TV star Vicky Pattison and was believed to be targeted due to online abuse.

An Indiana university was placed on lockdown late Friday night after receiving a 'likely prank call' claiming an armed person with explosives was near the administration building, according to officials. Police responded but left after determining it was a hoax, with no injuries confirmed.

Luis Suarez and Edinson Cavani, Uruguay's most famous son and a player known as El Matador, will face off in the Champions League quarter-final match between Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain at Parc des Princes. Cavani, crucial for PSG's chances, has been struggling with a goal drought and recent suspensions, while PSG lacks key players including Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Marco Veratti.

Derry Mathews won the interim WBA lightweight title with a unanimous decision over Tony Luis in Liverpool, after Richar Abril and Ismael Barroso pulled out due to illness and visa issues, respectively. Mathews controlled the fight, landing an uppercut, while Luis showed aggression but could not secure a win, resulting in a tight 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 decision.

Hull bounced back from a loss to Hull KR to defeat St Helens 28-20 at Langtree Park, securing a surprise victory and ending St Helens' three-game losing streak. Jamie Shaul scored the winning try for Hull, while Saints were hampered by injuries and a tactical switch at halftime.

The U.S. Census projects that the documented and undocumented immigrant population could reach 51 million by 2023, making up 14.8% of the U.S. population, with immigrants accounting for 82% of future population growth by 2060. This growth, driven by current immigration policies, could lead to significant changes in workforce, infrastructure, and assimilation challenges.

Arsenal Under 21s lost 1-0 to Reading at the Emirates Stadium, with Jack Wilshere making his return from injury as captain. Reading's Niall Keown scored the only goal in the 8th minute, and Wilshere and other injured first-team players like Abou Diaby and Serge Gnabri played limited minutes.

English golfer Justin Rose, struggling with form after a poor Florida swing, improved significantly in his first round at the Shell Houston Open, hitting 17 out of 18 greens and shooting a 69, a welcome return to the sixties. Despite his recent slump, Rose expressed confidence in his progress and a return to form, noting he had corrected his game faults.

A mansion in central London's Mayfair, formerly a milking parlour, has gone on the market for £25 million. Originally a commercial depot, the site was demolished in the 19th century and rebuilt as a modern luxury property with features like an indoor swimming pool, gym, lift, and cinema room.

Bayern Munich, despite injuries including those of Robben, Ribéry, Schweinsteiger, and Alaba, showed unity in recent games against Dortmund and Leverkusen, scoring 3-0 against Eintracht Frankfurt. Coach Pep Guardiola expects a strong unit to face Porto in the Champions League, emphasizing the team's scoring potential from Muller and Lewandowski. Guardiola acknowledges Porto's physical midfielders but also their quality.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes team-mates, visited Mercedes' Brackley base to collaborate and find a strategy to beat Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel, who won the Malaysian Grand Prix, in the upcoming Chinese race. Mercedes was surprised by Vettel's victory, which came despite Mercedes' comfortable one-two start in Australia, due to Ferrari's effective tyre management in the high-temperature race.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection is deemed unconstitutional or unavailable. The gas causes unconsciousness within 8-10 seconds and death from lack of oxygen, described as a "humane, quick and painless death." The bill was passed after Oklahoma's recent execution took 43 minutes, prompting scrutiny of the state's execution process.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull, topping this week's EA Sports' Performance Index with a Game Index score of 52.9. Gomis has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games, while Charlie Austin of Queens Park Rangers is the runner-up with a score of 52.2 after scoring and assisting in their 4-1 victory over West Brom.

A freezer trawler carrying 132 crew members, including 78 from Russia, 42 from Myanmar, and others from Latvia, Ukraine, and Vanuatu, sank in the Sea of Okhotsk off the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia, killing at least 56 crew members in 15 minutes. A massive rescue operation involving over 1,300 people is underway, with 63 survivors rescued and 13 still missing. Temperatures in the water can be as low as -2°C, contributing to the high death toll.

Men with advanced prostate cancer could benefit from a drug originally developed for women, as clinical trials show olaparib can delay the progression of the disease. The drug, already used to treat women with breast cancer, works by blocking DNA repair in cancer cells with BRCA gene mutations, and has shown promising results in extending survival for up to 30% of men with advanced prostate cancer.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, turned her passion for photography and globetrotting into a business called 'In Bed With', reviewing and photographing luxurious accommodations worldwide. With over 12,000 Instagram followers, she documents the best beds, pools, and room service, earning both hotel stays and professional photos, and has generated income from featuring travel products.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was thrown into the air and dragged along the surface of water in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, South Africa, after getting caught in a fight between two adult males. The calf's mother, watching in horror, tried to protect her but was unable to save the baby, which later died from its injuries.

The Football Association will investigate an incident at a Chelsea vs. QPR match where Branislav Ivanovic was struck by a cigarette lighter thrown from home supporters. QPR is unlikely to face disciplinary action but will review CCTV and ban those involved. Chelsea players celebrated the win, but the match was marred by objects being thrown onto the pitch. QPR is appealing for witnesses and will ban those identified, aiming to prevent future incidents.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. LaTasha Gosling, 27, and her daughters Janyaa, 4, and Jenika, 8, and son Landen, 7, were discovered early Wednesday. The suspect, also a mother with a six-month-old, was found dead hours later, not a homicide.

Labour MP Emily Thornberry, who previously criticized the right to buy policy, owns three homes including a £1 million housing association property she bought eight years ago, while opposing its extension to housing association tenants.

Police dropped an investigation into a vicious assault on Mike Lane, 40, a huntsman, three months after it occurred despite evidence pointing to a suspected attacker. Lane was beaten by protesters armed with iron bars during a hunt, sustaining concussions and broken teeth. The attack, which involved spraying hounds with citronella, left Lane unconscious and kicked in the head. Wiltshire Police issued the suspect's photograph but have not identified, charged, or prosecuted anyone, angering Lane and hunt supporters.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer, despite being linked with Premier League teams Manchester United and Chelsea. Gomes, who has netted four times in 25 La Liga appearances since joining from Benfica, says he is happy and convinced he will stay at the Mestalla.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, 19, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali by Henry Alafu, who had met her earlier and lured her to his remote home. After the first attack, Alafu followed her in a taxi and raped her again. Despite her attempts to escape, Alafu pursued her, and she sought help from passersby and taxi drivers. Police in Bali let Alafu escape back to Nigeria, sparking criticism of their handling of the case.

Former Made in Chelsea star Ashley James, partnering with PETA, protested Harvey Nichols' reintroduction of fur by posing with a fake skinned fox, urging customers to boycott fur products. Harvey Nichols previously opposed fur but recently reintroduced it, prompting James' campaign against the retailer.

Chile enacted a new law recognizing civil unions between same-sex couples, allowing around 2 million people to benefit. The change, signed by President Michelle Bachelet, will take effect in six months and aims to end discrimination faced by common-law couples, giving them rights in property, health care, pensions, and inheritance.

Chelsea are on track to break the Premier League record for most days at the top of the table, currently leading the league for 230 days since August 30, 2022, with a potential 12-day margin to surpass Manchester United's record of 262 days from the 1993/94 season.

Cape Verde, a small island nation with 500,000 people, seeks to leverage its rich musical heritage to boost its economy. The country, historically a hub for the transatlantic slave trade and home to unique musical styles like batuque and morna, is now promoting music and culture as alternative economic sectors. The government supports this initiative, with the prime minister and culture minister emphasizing the importance of creativity and innovation. The Kriol Jazz Festival, in its seventh year, has attracted international artists and has become a significant cultural event, filling venues and hotels across the country.

An old hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of Sydney's Opera House trended on social media again after heavy storms. Initially posted by Sydney radio duo Fitzy and Wippa, the video was debunked by wave experts who claimed it was impossible for waves to reach the Opera House, citing the lack of suitable swells and the impossibility of such a scene occurring naturally.

Reading lost 1-0 to Birmingham City in a Sky Bet Championship match at the Madejski Stadium, with Clayton Donaldson scoring the winner in the 87th minute after Reading dominated the first half. Reading had earlier lost 2-1 to Arsenal in the FA Cup semi-finals.

French football club Paris Saint-Germain suffered a significant setback as David Luiz, a key defender, will miss the Champions League match against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained in a recent match against Marseille. The Brazilian defender, 27, will be out for at least four weeks, potentially impacting PSG's Ligue One title defense and their Champions League campaign.

Fans illegally downloaded more than 100,000 episodes of Game of Thrones per day after its return, with over seven million episodes from seasons one to four illegally downloaded between February and April. The surge in piracy is up 45% year-on-year, with Brazil leading in illegal downloads, and the show remains the most illegally downloaded globally. HBO launched a new streaming service to curb piracy and recapture revenue, but piracy continues to be a significant issue.

Leicester City hosts West Ham United at King Power Stadium in a Premier League match. Leicester lacks key players with Matt Upson and Dean Hammond injured, while West Ham has Winston Reid returning from injury. Leicester has won only one of their last 10 home Premier League matches, while West Ham have not lost away from home in seven games. Kickoff is at 3 PM on Saturday.

Residents of Celoron, N.Y., reacted negatively to a statue of Lucile Ball, the iconic comedian, unveiled in 2009. The statue, based on Ball's drunken pitch for a health tonic on her show 'I Love Lucy,' was criticized for its unflattering appearance, leading to a Facebook page with over 600 likes calling for its removal.

A woman named Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, West Midlands, lost nearly half her body weight from 18st 6lb to 9st 9lb after standing for an entire 11-hour flight due to her bulky size 26 frame, which was causing discomfort for the woman seated next to her. This experience prompted her to join Weight Watchers Online and later start running, leading to her current weight of 9st 9lb and size 10.

Nicola Bonn, a new mother from London, started an online blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and advice for other new mothers, who often face judgment and criticism from those with more experience. Her post "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves" went viral, highlighting the frustration of new mothers feeling the need to explain their decisions to others.

Hassan Munshi, 17, and Talha Asmal, 17, are believed to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS after crossing into Turkey on March 31. Hassan is reportedly related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 and convicted of planning to murder non-Muslims. The families of the two teenagers, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, are in shock and deeply worried about their safety, urging anyone with information to contact the police.

Stephanie Scott, a school teacher from Leeton, was murdered just days before her wedding to childhood sweetheart Aaron Leeson-Woolley, leaving behind a devastated family and a wedding venue decorated with yellow balloons and flowers. Her body was found in nearby bushland, and the couple had sent out a guest list of 120 for their April 11 wedding, which was to be their first dance.

Southampton target Tonny Vilhena, 20, wants to leave Feyenoord this summer, with Saints interested and ready to make a move. Saints also monitor Feyenoord's Jordy Clasie, a £10m-rated midfielder, and are considering Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen, aiming to strengthen their squad for possible Europa League qualification.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House in Suffolk, sparking controversy among heritage experts who deemed the move misguided. Similar experiments with different seating arrangements are planned at nine other National Trust venues.

Former Prime Minister John Howard found himself with a flat tyre while driving in Sydney, and his driver, Felicity Waterford, offered assistance. Waterford, waiting for her daughter at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music, offered to help and was surprised to see Howard standing on the side of the road. Howard agreed to a selfie and chatted while the driver changed the tyre.

Tony Pulis, West Bromwich Albion manager, acknowledges Joey Barton's claim that his players "s*** themselves" after conceding a 2-0 lead to Queens Park Rangers, admitting Barton "probably had a point" given West Brom's subsequent 3-2 loss. Pulis recalls his own experience of leading 2-0 and losing in a play-off final, emphasizing that maintaining composure in leads is crucial.

A Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought extinct for over 50 years, was captured in the Ntokou-Pikounda National Park in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Primatologists Lieven Devreese and Gaël Elie Gnondo Gobolo took the first-ever photograph of the species, proving it is not extinct. Meanwhile, researchers in Tibet discovered a new white-cheeked macaque species with a distinctive penis shape, officially named Macaca leucogenys.

Kim Kardashian and her family visited Armenia, a country her father fled to, for eight days. They stayed in Yerevan, the capital, and visited landmarks including the Yerevan Opera House and the Geghard Monastery. The visit was notable for being Kardashian's first to Armenia, her father's homeland.

British expats Patrick and Valerie Jubb are 'trapped' in southern Spain amid a legal battle with the local town hall over a luxury bed and breakfast they operated. They purchased the property in 2008 and closed it a year ago, planning to sell it for €680,000. However, the town hall ruled that illegal additions made by a previous owner, including a swimming pool, are illegal, and the property is now on the brink of being demolished. The Jubbs have a certificate stating there were no infractions when they bought the estate, and they claim the alterations were legalised by land registry officials in 2005. They are seeking to sell the property but are facing financial difficulties as their money is tied up in it.

Apple reported its best-ever quarterly results, selling more than 61 million iPhones for $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit, up 40% from a year ago. Sales in China outpaced those in the US, with iPhone accounting for more than two-thirds of revenue. iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer sales rose 2% to $5.6 billion.

A 3-year-old girl, Elisa Tyler, has recurring nightmares about a white van, which her father believes may be linked to her mother's death in a SUV crash. Natali Castellanos-Tyler, 30, died in February when her silver Ford Explorer slid off a rain-soaked road and crashed into a tree, according to Virginia police. Elisa has been having disturbing visions about a white van that "hurt" her and her car, and her father has noticed similar hit-and-run incidents involving a white delivery-style truck in the area.

Researchers at New York University found that the brain can more easily remember 'neutral' or boring events when they are tied to an emotion. This study, focusing on the September 11 terrorist attacks, suggests that emotion enhances memory, even for mundane details, by affecting brain regions involved in emotional processing and memory consolidation.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of 18-year-old Jackson Byrnes with a stage four brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 through community support for his life-saving surgery by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo on Wednesday. The surgery is expected to save Jackson's life but will leave him paralysed, requiring a long rehabilitation process. Jackson and Jahnae have put their studies on hold to care for him, with the community in northern NSW contributing significantly to their fundraising efforts.

QPR centre-back Nedum Onuoha, 28, is wanted by Hull City amid QPR's potential relegation, with Everton and West Ham also interested. Onuoha has played regularly for Chris Ramsey and started the crucial 4-1 win against West Bromwich Albion. Hull is also considering Anichebe, 30, a West Brom striker likely to be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University documented and mapped regional English sentence structures across the United States, revealing distinct phrases like "I so might run this [race] with you" in California and "I ain't never had no trouble with none of 'em" in Florida. The map shows variations from the South to the North, with presentative sentences like "Here's you a water bottle" being more common in the South and less so in the North.

A Canadian man, Kalman Kallai, traveled 2,796 miles from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia in a green rocking chair he acquired for free, taking breaks to watch planes, pose in fields, and even chase birds. He was joined by his father for part of the journey, sharing stories and laughter.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood, in a press conference, revealed a 'win bonus' of a Twix multi-pack to six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the Villa manager's job after Paul Lambert was sacked, in a lighthearted moment.

World boxing champion Kell Brook watched Premier League Darts in Sheffield, receiving a hero's welcome. Dave Chisnall, who was second in the table after 10 weeks, won both of his games, including a 7-1 victory over James Wade, boosting his points to 17. Brook is set to defend his welterweight title against Frankie Gavin on May 30.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic, saying the 33-year-old striker plays an essential role for the club, both on and off the pitch, helping young players and exuding confidence. Ibrahimovic missed the Champions League quarter-final first leg against Barcelona due to suspension but will be available for the return match.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published an Aerodrome Manual on their website containing GPS coordinates and runway details of RAF Mount Pleasant on the Falklands Islands, potentially giving Argentine intelligence an invasion guide. The manual, containing sensitive technical information, was available publicly and could be used to plan an attack. This occurred as Argentina was preparing to lease Russian Su-24 bombers, which could pose a threat to British defences.

Huddersfield Giants, currently ninth in Super League, aim to improve their attack to match their strong defense as they prepare for a home game against Catalans Dragons, who lead the league in defensive efficiency. Paul Anderson, Huddersfield's coach, acknowledges the team's offensive struggles but hopes to find their offensive rhythm for a potential climb back up the ladder.

Planners in Windsor approved two Costa Coffee shops less than 500 yards apart, adding to the existing one, making it possible to walk between them in just five minutes. This decision was made despite one resident's concern about the area being "drowning in fast food and coffee shops."

The British Veterinary Association (BVA) has withdrawn its support for shooting free-running badgers in pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, concluding that the culls have not demonstrated conclusively their effectiveness and humaneness. The BVA still supports badger culling to combat bovine tuberculosis in cattle, but animal welfare campaigners criticized this stance, noting the BVA's ongoing support for cage-trapping and shooting.

Geoff Barrow, Portishead's founder, criticized streaming services for paying his band just £1,700 for 34 million plays, arguing this is unfair to musicians and hurting young talent. He called for better compensation, while streaming companies defended their practices, offering a fair price in an age of easy music access.

Game of Thrones fans leaked the first four episodes of the fifth season, scheduled to premiere tonight, onto torrent sites. The episodes, titled The Wars to Come, The House of Black and White, High Sparrow, and The Sons of the Harpy, were downloaded more than 550,000 times by early Sunday morning, potentially from HBO-approved press copies. This leak threatens to spoil the show's premiere, as the remaining episodes will be released over the next month.

A best man at his brother's wedding in Melbourne, Daniel Buccheri, composed an emotional song to use as his speech, which included tributes to his brother and his bride. The 25-year-old singer, using the tune of "Stay With Me" by Sam Smith, performed the unique speech at Poet's Lane, east of Melbourne, and it has been viewed over 100,000 times online.

Zara Phillips, Queen's granddaughter, regained her fitness after giving birth to Mia by exercising on an exercise bike every morning before her daughter wakes up, aiming to qualify for Team GB at the 2016 Olympics. She eats a balanced diet and includes swimming and cycling in her workouts, typically starting her day at 7 am.

Following Raheem Sterling's interview criticizing his contract with Liverpool, he returned to training after the international break. The interview has soured fan opinions, with many now believing Sterling should leave. Sterling is linked with a move to Arsenal for the upcoming match, and Liverpool fans support his departure, believing he is not worth the club's investment.

Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola conversed at a Barcelona training session in 2018, sparking interest in other notable coaches from the same team at the time. This included current PSG coach Laurent Blanc and Porto coach Julen Lopetegui, who were all part of the Barcelona XI that won the Spanish Super Cup in 1996, including players like Luis Enrique, Albert Ferrer, Abelardo Fernández, and Sergi Barjuan.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona, at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai, stated that Paris Saint-Germain's Javier Pastore is the best player in the world, praising his creativity and passing ability. Pastore, who cost PSG £29 million, has three goals and five assists this season, while Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have 45 and 51 goals respectively.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murdering his tenant Michael Spalding, 39, by hacking him to pieces, stuffing the body parts into suitcases, and dumping them in a canal. Simon, with girlfriend Michelle Bird's help, dismembered Spalding at their shared flat in Smethwick, Birmingham, before weighing down the suitcases with concrete slabs and throwing them into the canal. Simon denied knowledge of Spalding's death but later admitted assaulting him.

Health experts warn that social isolation can be as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day, leading to issues like dementia and high blood pressure. Essex and Gloucestershire county councils have developed 'loneliness maps' to identify areas with the highest risk of social isolation among elderly residents and others. These maps help local councils target vulnerable populations, with Gloucestershire's map combining statistics on age, living alone, mental health, and income to pinpoint red zones of loneliness. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends similar maps for other areas to combat the issue.

65-year-old waitress Judy Eddingfield celebrated her 50th anniversary working at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she was trained by her mother and has served for over six decades. The classic burger joint, open since 1940, has been a family tradition for Eddingfield, who has seen many famous faces, including those from 'Leave It to Beaver,' and has witnessed the price of French fries and a Coca-Cola drop from 65 cents to $1.

Former England captain Mike Gatting advises against Kevin Pietersen's immediate return to the international team, citing that other players like Gary Ballance and Ian Bell are performing well for Surrey. Gatting believes Pietersen should only be considered if others are not playing well, suggesting he might not get a spot even if Pietersen scores runs for Surrey.

A 17-year-old Californian student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos directly from their computer to the popular photo-sharing app, violating Instagram's terms of service. The app, which costs $4.99, is currently generating $1,000 daily for Benn, and Instagram has sent him a demand to 'fix' the app by Monday, threatening legal action.

Most South Korean companies host hoesik, or official drinking gatherings, monthly or weekly. For foreign business travelers, these events can be intense due to pressure to participate, as drinking is seen as a way to get to know colleagues. Koreans consider it rude to have an empty glass and defer to senior figures, who pour drinks first. Participants chug their drinks loudly, turning away from seniors during the ritual.

The Duke of Kent, 79, suffered a dislocated hip while visiting the Queen's Balmoral estate in Aberdeenshire, Scotland, and was hospitalized. He was discharged from Aberdeen Royal Infirmary today with a walking stick, having been treated for the injury two years after a mild stroke.

Meter Maids, a 50-year tradition of bikini-clad women placing money into expired parking meters in Surfers Paradise, Queensland, are facing criticism from local business leaders who argue the group is outdated and irrelevant due to advancements in parking meter technology. The Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce's president, Peter Yared, called for the end of the tradition, stating the Meter Maids are now a business and no longer perform a public service. However, the general manager, Michael Yarwood, defended the group, saying tourists embrace them as a quintessential part of the Gold Coast experience.

Greece, facing a £330 million IMF loan repayment on April 9, denied it would default, with Deputy Finance Minister Dimitris Mardas stating the country will make the payment on time.
